from typing import Literal

Category = Literal["repository", "module", "file", "symbol"]
RelationKind = Literal[
    "contains", "contains_logical", "defines", "references", "calls", "imports", "tested_by"
]
Resolution = Literal["resolved", "ambiguous", "unresolved"]
Basis = Literal["syntactic", "resolved", "heuristic"]
Coverage = Literal["complete", "partial", "unsupported"]
SkipReason = Literal["symlink", "special", "too_large", "unreadable", "invalid_name"]
HintKind = Literal["selection", "path", "symbol", "changed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SourceRef:
    """Half-open byte range ``[start, end)`` of one captured file, named by its digest."""

    path: str
    start: int
    end: int
    digest: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Entity:
    key: str
    category: Category
    kind: str
    name: str
    signature: str | None
    source: SourceRef | None
    test: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Relation:
    """One typed edge. An ambiguous relation is several rows sharing ``site``; an
    unresolved one has no ``target``, only the ``name`` it used."""

    kind: RelationKind
    source: str
    target: str | None
    resolution: Resolution
    basis: Basis
    name: str | None
    site: int
    evidence: SourceRef | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Snapshot:
    """Which published generation a result came from (ADR-0010 identities)."""

    repo_id: str
    snapshot_id: str
    derivation_id: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class FileInfo:
    path: str
    digest: str
    size: int
    language: str
    coverage: Coverage
    diagnostics: tuple[str, ...]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Skip:
    path: str
    reason: SkipReason


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class IndexReport:
    snapshot: Snapshot
    status: Literal["built", "unchanged"]
    files: int
    entities: int
    relations: int
    partial: tuple[str, ...]
    unsupported: int
    skipped: tuple[Skip, ...]
    case_collisions: tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]
    lexical: str
    seconds: float
    # Files compared with ``previous``, the generation this one replaced (None when
    # there was no readable one); ``parsed`` Python and TypeScript files were parsed,
    # ``reused`` reused their facts from it. All empty or zero when ``unchanged``.
    previous: Snapshot | None = None
    added: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    modified: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    deleted: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    parsed: int = 0
    reused: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ChannelStatus:
    """``ran``: ``detail`` names the scorer. ``disabled``/``unavailable``: why.
    An unavailable channel is never reported as empty or as a zero score."""

    state: Literal["ran", "disabled", "unavailable"]
    detail: str
    returned: int = 0
    truncated: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Seed:
    kind: HintKind
    hint: str
    case_insensitive: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class HintIssue:
    kind: HintKind
    hint: str
    issue: Literal["not_found", "ambiguous", "truncated"]

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class EntryPoint:

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SearchResult:

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class StructuralMatch:

    declaration containing it (None at module level) and the line it starts on."""

    source: SourceRef

    end_line: int

    ``skipped`` files are not UTF-8 and were not searched."""

    unresolved sites matching a root's name: dependents OXIDE may have missed, though for a
    common name most of them target something else.

    snapshot: Snapshot
    root: Entity
    direction: Literal["upstream", "downstream"]
    roots: tuple[str, ...]
    hops: tuple[ImpactHop, ...]
    unresolved: int
    stopped_by: str | None

class ItemEntity:
    key: str
    name: str
    complete: bool
    reason: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ContextItem:
    source: SourceRef
    lines: tuple[int, int]
    entities: tuple[ItemEntity, ...]
    units: int
    text: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Omission:
    key: str
    stage: Literal["selection", "packing"]
    reason: str


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RouteSummary:
    root_fallback: bool
    regions: int
    candidates: int
    deferred: int
    fanout_truncations: int
    stopped_by: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ContextBundle:
    """``payload`` is the agent-facing context; ``used <= budget`` in ``units``.
    Everything else is the diagnostic envelope, outside the budget."""

    snapshot: Snapshot
    query: str
    budget: int
    used: int
    units: str
    items: tuple[ContextItem, ...]
    omissions: tuple[Omission, ...]
    lexical: ChannelStatus
    hints: tuple[HintIssue, ...]
    route: RouteSummary
    degradations: tuple[str, ...]
    versions: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def payload(self) -> str:
        return "".join(item.text for item in self.items)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class JudgeStatus:
    """Whether ``build_context`` may send this repository's source to the optional judge
    (ADR-0009), where, and what it sends. ``enabled`` needs an authorization stored for
    exactly this repository and ``manifest``; ``authorized`` is the manifest a stored
    authorization names, if any. A key in ``credential`` never enables it by itself."""

    enabled: bool
    provider: str
    endpoint: str
    manifest: str
    authorized: str | None
    credential: str
    credential_set: bool
    discloses: str


class OxideError(Exception):
    """Base of every OXIDE failure; ``code`` is stable, the message is for humans."""

    code = "oxide_error"


class InvalidPath(OxideError):
    code = "invalid_path"


class OwnershipConflict(OxideError):
    code = "ownership_conflict"


class NotIndexed(OxideError):
    code = "not_indexed"


class IncompatibleIndex(OxideError):
    code = "incompatible_index"


class StoreCorrupt(OxideError):
    code = "store_corrupt"


class CaptureConflict(OxideError):
    code = "capture_conflict"


class CaptureLimit(OxideError):
    code = "capture_limit"


class NativeUnavailable(OxideError):
    code = "native_unavailable"


class Closed(OxideError):
    code = "closed"


class InvalidArgument(OxideError, ValueError):
    """A malformed or out-of-range argument; still a ``ValueError`` for callers."""

    code = "invalid_argument"


# What a caller can do about each expected failure. ``{index}`` is the command that indexes
# the repository the caller read, including its data location when one was given.
ADVICE = {
    "invalid_path": "the repository path does not exist or is not a directory",
    "not_indexed": "run `{index}` first",
    "ownership_conflict": (
        "another OXIDE process (e.g. `oxide index`) holds the repository; retry shortly"
    ),
    "incompatible_index": "the index was built by another OXIDE version; run `{index}`",
    "store_corrupt": "the index is damaged; rebuild it with `{index}`",
}


def advice(error: OxideError, repository: str, data_dir: str | None = None) -> str | None:
    """The next command for an expected failure, copy-pasteable; None when there is none."""
    template = ADVICE.get(error.code)
    if template is None:
        return None
    index = f"oxide index {shlex.quote(repository)}"
    if data_dir is not None:
        index += f" --data-dir {shlex.quote(data_dir)}"
    return template.format(index=index)

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
MAX_IMPACT = 100
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a "
        "source bundle within `budget`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024, description="Entity key from oxide_search, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`."
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = str(error) if error.code == "invalid_argument" else advice(error, repository)
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    Two tools. ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``) or ``context`` (``build_context``). ``oxide_impact`` is
    ``Repository.impact``. Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), or builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source "
        "with provenance (mode=context).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(query, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(query, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    impact_schema = {"type": "object", **TypeAdapter(Impact).json_schema()}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=impact_schema)
    def oxide_impact(
        key: Key,
        repository: Repo = None,
        direction: Direction = "upstream",
        depth: Annotated[
            int, Field(ge=0, le=MAX_DEPTH, description=f"hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).")
        ] = DEFAULT_DEPTH,
        limit: Annotated[
            int,
            Field(
                ge=0, le=MAX_IMPACT, description=f"entities to return (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT})."
            ),
        ] = DEFAULT_IMPACT,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """What depends on an entity. upstream: its callers, importers and tests; downstream:
        what it calls or imports. Hops come nearest first, each with its proven depth (resolved
        relations only). Give a key from oxide_search. Read-only; never source text. stopped_by
        names the bound that cut the walk. unresolved counts same-name call sites OXIDE could
        not resolve, so dependents may be missing."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        found = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.impact(key, direction=direction, depth=depth, limit=limit),
            handles,
        )
        value = {"hops_returned": len(found.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(found)
        text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
        return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

`oxide impact` and `oxide_impact` are in, along with the failure-mode fixes (A) and the graph exposure (B). Verify passes on the final code (557 passed, 7 skipped; the skips are the opt-in TypeScript gate). Nothing is committed.

**Not done:**
- **Independent tier-1 review of the final diff.** The earlier review failed on two MAJORs and three MINORs, all fixed. The re-review attempts on the final code hit a provider usage limit. This needs a re-run before merge.
- **Eval protocol amendment.** Both the second `oxide_` tool and the description-free `oxide_search` change the arm under test. `scripts/agent_eval/session.py` reads `tools=N`, so the oxide arm now reports 2 tools instead of 1. I did not edit `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`; it needs a dated amendment before any new run is read. No held-out run happened.

**What changed**

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Empty query | `search ""` exit 0, no entries | `invalid_argument` (CLI exit 2, MCP error). Still valid with a path/symbol/selection hint |
| Hint issues | Dropped in CLI, silent in MCP context | `hint: symbol NoSuchThing: not_found` (CLI); `# hint …` header (MCP) |
| Not-indexed advice | CLI: none. MCP: generic | Both: copy-pasteable `oxide index …` (CLI includes `--data-dir`) |
| Dependents | Not reachable from CLI or MCP | `oxide impact PATH KEY` and MCP `oxide_impact` over `Repository.impact` |
| Unknown key | "no entity" | Points to `oxide search` |

The spec is at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-cli-mcp-usability-design.md`. Its design review passed with factual corrections. `docs/public-api.md` is updated, including the migration wording.

**Design choices to check**
- `oxide_impact` is a second tool, not a `mode` on `oxide_search`. That keeps `query` meaningful and matches the tool-design guidance I researched.
- The MCP recovery advice does not print the server's `--data-dir`. It shows `--data-dir <the server's data location>`. A privacy test caught my first version leaking the path.
- Advice quoting uses double quotes for paths with spaces, not `shlex.quote`, so it works in cmd, PowerShell, and POSIX shells.
- `test_native.py`'s hostile-query stress test now accepts `InvalidArgument` only for blank queries. Every other query must still run and stay deterministic.

**Deliberately left out:** degradation next-step text (core strings aren't parsed in presentation code), the bytes-vs-lines unit mismatch, `entity`/`relations` commands, and any change to the `oxide_search` description or server instructions (both are eval-arm variables).

**Measured.** Probes on `fixtures/py_repo` before and after: `impact` returns `test_decode_claims_parses_payload` at depth 1, proven. Unknown keys and empty queries return exit 2 with the expected code. The CLI "before" snapshot is not clean for the `not_indexed` lines, because I indexed the store after taking it.

**Remaining gap I observed:** `context x` (one-letter query) returns `0/300` units silently. Not changed.

**Next step:** re-run the tier-1 review on the final diff, write the eval protocol amendment, and tell me whether to commit. `AGENTS.md` says commit after verify, and `docs/agents/workflow.md` says commit only when asked; I left the tree uncommitted until you decide.

summary:
## Goal
- Make OXIDE's CLI and MCP interfaces useful to human developers and coding agents, following the user's choice "A now then B":
  - **A:** fail clearly. Reject empty queries, surface hint issues, share one advice table between CLI and MCP.
  - **B:** expose the existing `Repository.impact` as `oxide impact` (CLI) and `oxide_impact` (MCP).
- Prior project context (from memory): OXIDE is a vectorless structural context engine, one Python package at `src/oxide/`. The goal of the broader effort is measurable coding-agent task success, validated on held-out tasks. No success claim is made in this change.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Repo rules (`AGENTS.md`): CLI and MCP are clients of `oxide.api` only and must not parse, route, select, or pack. No speculative features. Tests never touch real user data. Every source file ≤500 LOC. Comments say why, not what. Full `mise run verify` before completion.
- Tier 2 (public API/CLI/MCP surface): needs an intent spec and zero-context review before implementation. Done.
- Tier 1 review is required before commit. The reviewer found issues, which are being fixed.
- Commit: `AGENTS.md` says commit after verify passes; `docs/agents/workflow.md` says commit only when asked. Left uncommitted and not yet resolved.
- Do not change the `oxide_search` tool description or the server `instructions`. The description is a variable in the pre-registered discoverability eval protocol (`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`).
- Do not run held-out evals. Do not edit the eval README without a new protocol version.
- Preserve retrieval, routing, packing, and frozen-baseline output bytes for valid calls.

## Progress

### Done
- [x] Research: mapped CLI (`src/oxide/cli.py`) and MCP (`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`, FastMCP 4.1.2, one tool before this change). Probed both on `fixtures/py_repo` with a private data dir. Found:
  - empty query exits 0 silently
  - hints dropped
  - graph API (`impact`, `relations`, `entity`, `files`) unexposed
  - `not_indexed` had no next step on CLI
- [x] Diagnosed eval evidence: run-3 `oxide diagnose` on `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl` gave 16 not-connected, 56 connected-never-called, 8 called-after-builtins-read-gold, 5 called-first-gold-surfaced, 2 called-first-gold-not-surfaced (87 OXIDE runs). Run-3 verdict was "no demonstrated improvement".
- [x] Intent spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-cli-mcp-usability-design.md`. Zero-context reviewer (`CombativeMarmot`) passed the factual claims. It flagged `more_available` semantics (fixed: the output now leads with `hops_returned` and `stopped_by`) and the unverified fixture hop (verified: `symbol:tests/test_auth.py#test_decode_claims_parses_payload` is a proven depth-1 upstream hop of `symbol:oxidepy/auth.py#decode_claims`).
- [x] **A1** empty query: `_hints` in `src/oxide/api.py` raises `InvalidArgument("query is empty: give words or identifiers, or a path, symbol or selection hint")` only when the query is blank and no seed (`paths`, `symbols`, `selection`, `changed`) is given. `tests/python/test_native.py` stress script was adjusted: blank queries may raise `InvalidArgument`, other queries must run.
- [x] **A2** hint issues: CLI search prints `hint: <kind> <hint>: <issue>` lines before the lexical status line. CLI context prints them to stderr. MCP context text adds `# hint <kind> <hint>: <issue>` header lines.
- [x] **A3** shared advice: `ADVICE` dict and `advice(error, repository, data_dir=None)` in `src/oxide/models.py`. Imports `shlex` (to be replaced). CLI prints `hint: <advice>` after `error[code]: …`. The api message for an unknown impact key is `no entity 'KEY' in this snapshot; find keys with oxide search`.
- [x] **B1** CLI: `oxide impact PATH KEY [--direction upstream|downstream] [--depth 0-8, default 3] [--limit 0-1000, default 200] [--data-dir D] [--json]`. `_impact_summary` in `cli.py`.

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |

with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) On the agent's tree only a failed bubblewrap
launch is a harness error; a hang, a broken `conftest.py` or a collection error is the agent's
unresolved result (gold-patch verification stays strict). (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the
adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    Two tools. ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``) or ``context`` (``build_context``). ``oxide_impact`` is
    ``Repository.impact``. Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), or builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source "
        "with provenance (mode=context).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(query, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(query, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    impact_schema = {"type": "object", **TypeAdapter(Impact).json_schema()}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=impact_schema)
    def oxide_impact(
        key: Key,
        repository: Repo = None,
        direction: Direction = "upstream",
        depth: Annotated[
            int, Field(ge=0, le=MAX_DEPTH, description=f"hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).")
        ] = DEFAULT_DEPTH,
        limit: Annotated[
            int,
            Field(
                ge=0, le=MAX_IMPACT, description=f"entities to return (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT})."
            ),
        ] = DEFAULT_IMPACT,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """What depends on an entity. upstream: its callers, importers and tests; downstream:
        what it calls or imports. Hops come nearest first, each with its proven depth (resolved
        relations only). Give a key from oxide_search. Read-only; never source text. stopped_by
        names the bound that cut the walk. unresolved counts same-name call sites OXIDE could
        not resolve, so dependents may be missing."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        found = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.impact(key, direction=direction, depth=depth, limit=limit),
            handles,
        )
        value = {"hops_returned": len(found.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(found)
        text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
        return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""

# ADR-0013: Selective, source-backed graph navigation and tiered context in `oxide_search`

## Status

**Proposed**, 2026-10-25. Nothing is implemented in `src/oxide`. The experimental server
lives only in `docs/phase-6/agc-v4/scripts/server.py` (at `013e791`). AGC v4, the study
that was to decide it, stopped at stage 1 without promoting the interface
([docs/phase-6/agc-v4](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/phase-6/agc-v4/README.md)):
there is no evidence for this proposal yet. It can become Accepted only through a new
preregistered study that promotes it, and the maintainer's agreement.

## Context

Earlier studies:

| Study | Result | What it showed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AGC v1 (7eca108), REJECT | Tool cost doubled tokens | The cause was OpenCode's code mode, not the tool |
| AGC v2 (5cf699d), REJECT | The agent rarely used a direct tool | Tasks were ones grep/read already solved (94%) |
| AGC v3 (0381565), PROMOTE G (preregistered) | Structural tasks (dispatch, two-hop impact) | Forced use: success 0.86 vs 0.57 for grep/read, false claims 0.67 vs 2.05, cost per success 0.58× |

In v3, the agent picked the tool unprompted in 67% of runs. The guided arm (G) was worse
than the unguided one (D):

- **Measured:** CPS G/D 1.33 (CI 1.10–1.77). The success gap was not significant
  (16/21 vs 14/21, p = 0.73).
- **Mechanism (*inferred*):** the guidance ("callers first, depth 2, don't grep again")
  doubled tool calls and halved verification greps. Precision fell from 0.86 to 0.81 at
  the same recall, with depth-2 walks run from intermediate symbols.
- Analysis: `docs/phase-6/agc-v4/scripts/v3_dg.py` (at `013e791`).

Production MCP already has one tool, `oxide_search`, with `mode=search|context`. A second
tool adds schema to every prompt and one more choice for the agent to make. A new mode
reuses an interface the agent already sees.

## Decision (proposed)

1. **One tool.** `oxide_search` gains three read-only modes. There is no separate
   `oxide_context`, unless AGC v4 shows the split shape has a clear advantage.
   - `mode=callers` or `mode=callees` with a symbol in `query`:
     - the bounded upstream or downstream walk (`Repository.impact`);
     - each hop's count from that symbol and the source line that links it
       (`Repository.relations` evidence);
     - for callers, the name's occurrences that no edge explains, or for callees, the
       calls that weren't resolved.
     - `depth` 1–3, default 1.
   - `mode=outline`: the package map (empty `query`), a file's declarations with line
     ranges, or a symbol's signature, docstring and members.
   - Today's API does not carry all of this. Additive, read-only API is needed first:
     `Repository.outline`; per hop, the linking relation's evidence (`ImpactHop` has only
     `via`), as `path:line` (relation evidence is a byte range, so the API converts);
     and unresolved calls for downstream walks (`Impact.unresolved` is upstream only).
     The server stays a formatter over that API (decision 5).
2. **Source-backed.** Every listed relation cites `path:line` evidence from the index.
   The tool never returns source beyond those lines: exact source is the client's `read`,
   or `mode=context`.
3. **Selective.**
   - No ranking, no packing, and no change to `search` or `context`.
   - The tool's description says when the modes help (relationship questions,
     orientation) and when grep/search is enough (where a single name is defined).
   - No fixed depth, and no "call this first" or "don't grep again" instructions.
   - No system-prompt guidance ships: v3 measured the cost.
4. **Honest about completeness.**
   - Output says it is not exhaustive.
   - It reports the bound that stopped the walk (`stopped_by`) and the unexplained
     residual.
   - Heuristic and ambiguous edges are labelled ("likely"), as in `Impact.proven_depth`.
5. **Boundaries.**
   - MCP stays a client of `oxide.api` (AGENTS.md § Layout): no parsing, routing or
     selection in the server.
   - LadybugDB stays authoritative ([ADR-0002](0002-ladybugdb-knowledge-store.md)).
   - Graph algorithms over projections follow [ADR-0012](0012-networkx-graph-algorithms.md).
   - Code mode is not used.

## Evidence required before Accepted

AGC v4 stopped without promotion, so a new preregistered study must pass. Its rule
should keep AGC v4's terms:

- **Interface:** the single shape is chosen unless the split shape shows the defined clear
  advantage.
- **Gate:** the chosen shape must clear it with *natural* use against a capable grep/read
  baseline. Forced use is a separate diagnostic and never counts as adoption.
- **Tasks:** fresh, rule-selected, across Python and TypeScript and five question types.

Until one does, this ADR stays Proposed (or is withdrawn), and graph navigation stays
API-only (`Repository.impact`).

## Consequences

- **Costs:**
  - About 600 more first-step prompt tokens per session for the larger `oxide_search`
    schema (dev measurement: 615).
  - A new public API read (`outline`).
  - The MCP surface grows by three modes rather than a tool.
- **Risks:**
  - Agents may over-call the graph modes, as G did in v3. The description must stay
    selective, and the gate measures cost per success.
  - Graph incompleteness, which the residual and `stopped_by` make visible.
- **Not decided here:** CLI parity for the new modes; non-OpenCode clients (to be
  measured separately).

## MCP

`oxide mcp [--repo PATH]... [--data-dir D] [--http [--host H] [--port P]]`
(`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`, FastMCP 4.1) is another client of this API: it never
parses, routes, selects or packs.

It serves two tools. `oxide_search`'s `mode` picks one API operation (table below); `oxide_impact` is one API call, `Repository.impact`:

| `mode` | Arguments (bounds) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search` (default) | `query` (≤ 2000 chars), `repository`, `limit` (0–100, default 20), `paths`, `symbols` (≤ 32 × ≤ 1024 chars) | `Repository.search`: `SearchResult` as structured content and compact JSON text, led by `entries_returned` and `more_available` (the lexical limit was hit or a symbol hint was capped); locations, never source |
| `context` | `query`, `repository`, `budget` (0–32768 units, default 2048), `paths`, `symbols` | `Repository.build_context`: `ContextBundle` as structured content; the text is a one-line summary, any degradations and hint issues, then `payload` |
| `oxide_impact` (second tool) | `key` (required, ≤ 1024 chars), `repository`, `direction` (`upstream` default, or `downstream`), `depth` (0–8, default 3), `limit` (0–100, default 25) | `Repository.impact`: `Impact` as structured content, led by `hops_returned` in the text; `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; locations and relations, never source |

`limit` with `mode="context"` and `budget` with `mode="search"` are `invalid_argument`
errors, never silently ignored. The output schema is either result type (`anyOf`).

An empty `query` without a `paths`, `symbols` or selection hint is `invalid_argument`.

**Migration (2026-10-18, intentional break).** `oxide_context` is gone. Call
`oxide_search` with `mode="context"`: the arguments, text and structured result are
the old tool's, byte for byte. A call without `mode` is the old `oxide_search`, with

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
MAX_IMPACT = 100
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a "
        "source bundle within `budget`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024, description="Entity key from oxide_search, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`."
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    Two tools. ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``) or ``context`` (``build_context``). ``oxide_impact`` is
    ``Repository.impact``. Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), or builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source "
        "with provenance (mode=context).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(query, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(query, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    impact_schema = {"type": "object", **TypeAdapter(Impact).json_schema()}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=impact_schema)
    def oxide_impact(
        key: Key,
        repository: Repo = None,
        direction: Direction = "upstream",
        depth: Annotated[
            int, Field(ge=0, le=MAX_DEPTH, description=f"hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).")
        ] = DEFAULT_DEPTH,
        limit: Annotated[
            int,
            Field(
                ge=0, le=MAX_IMPACT, description=f"entities to return (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT})."
            ),

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(found.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )


    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

    VENV/python -I scripts/smoke_dist.py FIXTURES_DIR

its locked dependencies installed, after ``oxide prepare``. It drives the installed
``oxide`` console script in subprocesses against a copy of ``fixtures/py_repo`` and
``fixtures/ts_repo`` plus a non-ASCII, CRLF file, in a private data location whose
path has spaces and non-ASCII characters:

- the package is imported from the environment, never the source tree;
- child processes have only the installed environment's scripts on PATH;

Exits non-zero with a message on the first failure. Stdlib only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import sysconfig
import tempfile
from importlib.metadata import version
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

MESSAGES = [
    {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": 1,
        "method": "initialize",
        "params": {
            "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
            "capabilities": {},
            "clientInfo": {"name": "smoke", "version": "0"},
        },
    },
    {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"},
    {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/list"},
    {
        "jsonrpc": "2.0",
        "id": 2,
        "method": "tools/call",
        "params": {
            "name": "oxide_search",
            "arguments": {"query": "TTLCache", "symbols": ["TTLCache"]},
        },
    },
]
HOLD = (
    "import sys, oxide\n"
    "with oxide.open_repository(sys.argv[1], data_dir=sys.argv[2]):\n"
    "    print('held', flush=True); sys.stdin.read()"
)


def check(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        sys.exit(f"smoke: FAILED: {message}")

    scripts = sysconfig.get_path("scripts")
    exe = shutil.which("oxide", path=scripts)
    if exe is None:
        sys.exit(f"smoke: FAILED: no installed oxide console script in {scripts}")

        [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", "import oxide; print(oxide.__file__)"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=tempfile.gettempdir(),
    )
    check(where.returncode == 0, f"import oxide failed: {where.stderr}")
    origin = Path(where.stdout.strip()).resolve()
    check(
        not origin.is_relative_to(fixtures.resolve().parent),
        f"oxide imported from the checkout ({origin}), not the installed artifact",
    )

        root, data = Path(temp) / "repo ü", Path(temp) / f"data dir{accent}"
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "py_repo", root)
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "ts_repo", root / "web")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "js_repo", root / "javascript")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "go_repo", root / "golang")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "rust_repo", root / "rustlang")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "java_repo", root / "javalang")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "c_repo", root / "clang")
        shutil.copytree(fixtures / "cpp_repo", root / "cpplang")
        (root / "naïve_ünicode.py").write_bytes(b"def caf\xc3\xa9_total():\r\n    return 1\r\n")

            )

            return run

            return json.loads(oxide(*args, "--json").stdout)

        built = result("index", str(root))
        check(built["status"] == "built", f"first index: {built['status']}")
        if pinned:
            check(built["lexical"] == "available", f"FTS unavailable: {built['lexical']}")
        check(not built["partial"], f"partial parses: {built['partial']}")
        check(result("index", str(root))["status"] == "unchanged", "reopened store rebuilt")
        (root / "oxidepy" / "retry.py").write_text("# emptied\n", encoding="utf-8")
        edited = result("index", str(root))
        check(edited["status"] == "built", "an edit was not published")
        check(edited["modified"] == ["oxidepy/retry.py"], f"modified: {edited['modified']}")
        print(f"smoke: indexed {edited['files']} files, {edited['entities']} entities")

        found = result("search", str(root), "RetryPolicy")
        state = "ran" if pinned else "unavailable"
        check(found["lexical"]["state"] == state, f"lexical channel: {found['lexical']}")
        keys = [e["entity"]["key"] for e in found["entries"]]
        check(not any(k.startswith("symbol:oxidepy/retry.py#") for k in keys), "stale search")
        if pinned:
            found = result("search", str(root), "café total")
            keys = [e["entity"]["key"] for e in found["entries"]]
            check("symbol:naïve_ünicode.py#café_total" in keys, f"non-ASCII entity: {keys}")
        js = result("search", str(root), "normalize", "--symbol", "normalize")
        check(
            any(
                e["entity"]["key"] == "symbol:javascript/src/use.cjs#normalize"
                for e in js["entries"]
            ),
            "installed JavaScript extraction unavailable",
        )
        js_context = result(
            "context", str(root), "normalize", "--symbol", "normalize", "--budget", "1024"
        )
        check("function normalize" in js_context["payload"], "installed JS context unavailable")
        go = result("search", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "MustGet")
        check(
            go["entries"][0]["entity"]["key"] == "symbol:golang/store/store.go#Store.MustGet",
            "installed Go extraction unavailable",
        )
        go_context = result("context", str(root), "open", "--symbol", "Open", "--budget", "1024")
        check("func Open(mode int)" in go_context["payload"], "installed Go context unavailable")
        rust = result("search", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "must_get")
        # C++ fixtures also define Store::must_get, so rank among same-named symbols is a tie.
        check(
            "symbol:rustlang/crates/shop/src/store/mod.rs#<impl Store>.must_get"
            in [e["entity"]["key"] for e in rust["entries"]],
            "installed Rust extraction unavailable",
        )
        rust_context = result(
            "context", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "must_get", "--budget", "1024"
        )
        check(
            "pub fn must_get(&self, key: &Key) -> String" in rust_context["payload"],
            "installed Rust context unavailable",
        )
        java = result("search", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "mustGet")
        check(
            java["entries"][0]["entity"]["key"]
            == "symbol:javalang/src/main/java/com/example/shop/store/Store.java#Store.mustGet",
            "installed Java extraction unavailable",
        )
        java_context = result("context", str(root), "open", "--symbol", "open", "--budget", "1024")
        check(
            "static Store open(Mode mode)" in java_context["payload"],
            "installed Java context unavailable",
        )
        c = result("search", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "store_must_get")
        check(
            c["entries"][0]["entity"]["key"].startswith("symbol:clang/")
            and c["entries"][0]["entity"]["name"] == "store_must_get",
            "installed C extraction unavailable",
        )
        c_context = result(
            "context", str(root), "open", "--symbol", "store_open", "--budget", "1024"
        )
        check(
            "Store *store_open(enum Mode mode)" in c_context["payload"],
            "installed C context unavailable",
        )
        cpp = result("search", str(root), "must get", "--symbol", "Store.must_get")
        check(
            cpp["entries"][0]["entity"]["key"].startswith("symbol:cpplang/")
            and cpp["entries"][0]["entity"]["name"] == "must_get",
            "installed C++ extraction unavailable",
        )
        cpp_context = result(
            "context", str(root), "open", "--symbol", "Store.open", "--budget", "1024"
        )
        check(
            "Store Store::open(Mode mode)" in cpp_context["payload"],
            "installed C++ context unavailable",
        )
        hint = ("--file", "oxidepy/cache.py", "--budget", "400")
        context = result("context", str(root), "cache", *hint)
        check(0 < context["used"] <= 400, f"context used {context['used']} of 400")
        first = context["items"][0]["source"]["path"]
        check(first == "oxidepy/cache.py", f"the hinted file did not come first: {first}")
        print(f"smoke: search and context ok ({context['used']}/400 units)")

        server = subprocess.Popen(
            [exe, "mcp", "--repo", str(root), "--data-dir", str(data)],
            env=env,
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        assert server.stdin is not None and server.stdout is not None
        server.stdin.write("".join(json.dumps(m) + "\n" for m in MESSAGES))
        server.stdin.flush()
        replies = [json.loads(server.stdout.readline()) for _ in range(3)]
        # Closing stdin is how a host shuts the server down.
        rest, stderr = server.communicate(timeout=60)
        check(server.returncode == 0 and rest == "", f"mcp exit {server.returncode}: {stderr}")
        responses = {r.get("id"): r for r in replies}
        check(set(responses) == {1, 2, 3}, f"mcp replies: {replies}")
        tools = responses[3]["result"]["tools"]
        check(
            sorted(t["name"] for t in tools) == ["oxide_impact", "oxide_search"],
            f"mcp tools: {tools}",
        )
        entries = responses[2]["result"]["structuredContent"]["entries"]
        check(entries[0]["entity"]["key"].endswith("#TTLCache"), f"mcp search: {entries[:1]}")
        print("smoke: mcp stdio ok")

            [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", HOLD, str(root), str(data)],
            env=env,
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,

        holder.wait(timeout=60)

            blocked.returncode == 2 and "ownership_conflict" in blocked.stderr,
            f"second owner: exit {blocked.returncode}, {blocked.stderr}",
        )
        oxide("index", str(root))  # the lock is released with its owner
        print("smoke: store lock exclusive and released")
    print("smoke: OK")


def environment() -> dict[str, Any]:
    from oxide.storage.ladybug import fts_location, fts_unavailable

    return {
        "platform": f"{sys.platform}-{platform.machine()}",
        "os": platform.platform(),
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "packages": {
            p: version(p)
            for p in (
                "oxide-agent",
                "ladybug",
                "tree-sitter",
                "tree-sitter-javascript",
                "tree-sitter-go",
                "tree-sitter-rust",
                "tree-sitter-java",
                "tree-sitter-c",
                "tree-sitter-cpp",
                "fastmcp",
            )
        },
        "fts": fts_unavailable(fts_location()) or "available",
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if sys.argv[1] == "--environment":
        print(json.dumps(environment(), indent=1))
    else:
        main(Path(sys.argv[1]))

PUT 346.=365:
+It serves one tool. `oxide_search`'s `mode` picks one API operation (table below):
+
+| `mode` | Arguments (bounds) | Result |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `search` (default) | `query` (required, ≤ 2000 chars), `repository`, `limit` (0–100, default 20), `paths`, `symbols` (≤ 32 × ≤ 1024 chars) | `Repository.search`: `SearchResult` as structured content and compact JSON text, led by `entries_returned` and `more_available` (the lexical limit was hit or a symbol hint was capped); locations, never source |
+| `context` | `query` (required), `repository`, `budget` (0–32768 units, default 2048), `paths`, `symbols` | `Repository.build_context`: `ContextBundle` as structured content; the text is a one-line summary, any degradations and hint issues, then `payload` |
+| `impact` | `key` (required, ≤ 1024 chars, an entity key from a `search` entry), `repository`, `direction` (`upstream` default, or `downstream`), `depth` (0–8, default 3), `limit` (0–100, default 25) | `Repository.impact`: `Impact` as structured content, led by `hops_returned` in the text; `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; locations and relations, never source |
+
+Arguments that do not apply to a mode are `invalid_argument` errors, never silently ignored:
+`limit` with `context`; `budget` with `search` or `impact`; `paths` and `symbols` with `impact`;
+`query` with `impact`; `key`, `direction` and `depth` outside `impact`. The output schema is any
+of the three result types (`anyOf`).
+
+An empty `query` without a `paths`, `symbols` or selection hint is `invalid_argument`.
+
+**Migration (2026-10-18, intentional break).** `oxide_context` is gone. Call
+`oxide_search` with `mode="context"`: the arguments, text and structured result are
+the old tool's, byte for byte. A call without `mode` is the old `oxide_search`, with
+the same arguments, defaults and output (as of that change). Since 2026-11-10 `oxide_search`
+changed: an empty query with no `paths`, `symbols` or selection hint is `invalid_argument`,
+context text adds `# hint` lines for unmatched hints, and `mode="impact"` was added. A separate
+`oxide_impact` tool existed only in uncommitted work and was folded into `mode="impact"` before
+commit, so the server advertises one tool.
