# OXIDE

A structural context engine for coding agents.

OXIDE captures a repository, derives a typed graph of its files, modules, symbols, and
relations, persists that graph in LadybugDB, and answers "what code matters for this
task?" with a bounded, source-backed context bundle. Retrieval is vectorless: BM25 over
code-aware terms plus structural seeds from typed hints, then TreeRouter and
deterministic selection and packing. No embeddings, model runners, or network access on
the query path.

Status: pre-release, on `main`. Python, TypeScript/TSX, JavaScript/JSX, Go, Rust,
Java, C and C++ have parser slices ([TypeScript](docs/typescript.md), [JavaScript](docs/javascript.md),
[Go](docs/go.md), [Rust](docs/rust.md), [Java](docs/java.md), [C](docs/c.md), [C++](docs/cpp.md)); other files are kept as
unsupported file evidence. The public Python API is the product boundary
([docs/public-api.md](docs/public-api.md)). The legacy v1 implementation and its README
are pinned at commit
[`ac985b28`](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/ac985b28fcff7663aedadf2db5b40aa2dc325580);
the original documentation remains available in
[the pinned v1 README](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/ac985b28fcff7663aedadf2db5b40aa2dc325580/README.md).

## Install

OXIDE needs CPython 3.12-3.14. Development uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide && cd oxide
mise run bootstrap        # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare`
```

Without mise, run `uv sync --locked`, then `uv run oxide prepare`. `oxide prepare` is
the only network access OXIDE makes. It downloads the pinned LadybugDB FTS extension for
your platform (Linux x86_64, macOS 15+ arm64, Windows x86_64;
[docs/platforms.md](docs/platforms.md)) and checks its SHA-256. Without that extension,
the lexical channel reports `unavailable` and structural seeds and routing still work.

Outside the checkout, install the `oxide-agent` distribution (`pip install oxide-agent`
once it is published, or build it with `uv build` and `pip install dist/oxide_agent-*.whl`),
then run `oxide prepare`. That needs only Python and the native wheels. It does not need Rust,
Node.js, or a compiler. On Windows, LadybugDB also needs the OpenSSL 3 x64 DLLs in the
system directory. It opens only ASCII paths there, so with a non-ASCII user name, set
`OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and `OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION` ([docs/platforms.md](docs/platforms.md)).

## Use

```bash
uv run oxide index  path/to/repo                      # built | unchanged
uv run oxide search path/to/repo "where are failed requests retried" --limit 20
uv run oxide context path/to/repo "where are failed requests retried" --budget 1024 \
    --symbol RetryPolicy --file src/http/client.py
```

Every command takes `--json` (the typed result) and `--data-dir`. `context` prints
the payload on stdout and `used/budget units` on stderr. Errors print
`error[<code>]: <message>` and exit 2.

```python
import oxide

with oxide.open_repository("path/to/repo") as repo:   # owns the store until closed
    repo.index()
    hits = repo.search("where are failed requests retried")
    bundle = repo.build_context("where are failed requests retried", budget=1024)
    print(bundle.payload)                             # used <= budget
```

### MCP

`oxide mcp` serves one read-only tool, `oxide_search`, over stdio (FastMCP). Its
`mode` is `search` (ranked locations, the default) or `context` (a budgeted source
bundle); `oxide_context` was folded into it on 2026-10-18. It never indexes: run
`oxide index` first, and again whenever you want fresher results, even while the
server runs.

```bash
uv run oxide mcp --repo path/to/repo                      # stdio, for a local agent
uv run oxide mcp --repo path/to/repo --http --port 8765   # stateless HTTP, loopback only
```

For example, in Claude Code: `claude mcp add oxide -- uv run --directory /path/to/oxide
oxide mcp --repo /path/to/repo`. With `--repo` (repeatable) calls may only name those
repositories, and with exactly one they may omit `repository`.

The store lives under `--data-dir`, else `$OXIDE_DATA_DIR`, else
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/oxide/py` (`~/.local/share/oxide/py`). It is never captured, even
when it sits inside the repository.

## Limits

- One owner per store, across processes. A `Repository` is not thread-safe.
- Indexing is a full rebuild per change, and capture holds the captured bytes in
  memory (at most 1 GiB in scope, 1 MiB per file).
- Verified on Linux x86_64, macOS 15+ (arm64) and Windows x86_64 by the
  Platforms workflow. Windows needs the OpenSSL 3 DLLs and ASCII store paths; see
  [docs/platforms.md](docs/platforms.md).

[docs/public-api.md](docs/public-api.md) has the full list, with errors, bounds and
recovery behavior.

## Develop

```bash
mise run verify           # ruff, mypy --strict, pytest (CI runs exactly this)
uv run python scripts/bench.py path/to/corpus   # latency and peak RSS, JSON report
```

Architecture: [docs/spec/SPEC.md](docs/spec/SPEC.md), [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md)
and the decisions in [docs/adr/](docs/adr/), in particular
[ADR-0011](docs/adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md) (Python engine, vectorless
retrieval). Contributor workflow: [docs/agents/workflow.md](docs/agents/workflow.md).
Documentation and historical evidence: [docs index](docs/README.md).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# C source support `oxide-c-v1` adds C as a language slice of the existing engine: `core/languages/c.py` extracts syntax facts with `tree-sitter-c==0.24.2`, and `core/languages/c_resolve.py` resolves them over the whole capture. No compiler, preprocessor, build system, `compile_commands.json` or repository code runs during indexing or querying. The ordinary Python API, CLI, retrieval, graph, router and context packer serve these files unchanged, and MCP remains exactly one tool, `oxide_search`, with `search` and `context` modes. ## Extraction and identity `.c` and `.h` files report `FileInfo.language == "c"`, except a `.h` file with C++ syntax, which is C++ ([cpp.md](cpp.md)). File-level declarations become symbols, including those in every branch of an `#if`/`#ifdef`/`#else`: | C declaration | Kind | Key segment | | --- | --- | --- | | a function definition, or a prototype `T f(...);` | `function` | `f` | | `struct S { … }`, `union U { … }`, `enum E { … }` with a body | `struct` / `union` / `enum` | the tag | | `typedef … T;` | `type` | `T` | | each declarator of another declaration (`int a, *b;`, `extern int c;`, `int (*fp)(int);`) | `variable` | the name | | `#define N …`, `#define F(x) …` | `macro` | the name | Keys are `symbol:#`; every symbol's physical parent is its file. A prototype and its definition are separate symbols (ADR-0010), and so are a tag and a same-named typedef: equal segments in one file (a prototype before its definition, `#ifdef` branches, `typedef struct S {…} S;`) take `~n` in scope order, a tag before the declaration that holds it. Declarations inside function bodies, struct members, enumerators, anonymous tags and forward declarations (`struct S;`) are not symbols. A function spans its definition or prototype, a tag its specifier, and a typedef, variable or prototype its whole declaration (several declarators share it). A macro spans its `#define` line(s). Signatures are whitespace-collapsed headers with bodies cut out (`Store *store_open(enum Mode mode)`, `typedef struct Store Store;`, `struct Store`); a variable's is its first line, a macro's its first line without the continuation backslash. Doc comments are not part of a symbol's range. C has no modules: there are no `module:` entities or `defines` edges, and `#include` edges name files. There is no test convention either, so no symbol is a test and there are no `tested_by` edges. ## Resolution Everything below follows C's translation-unit, linkage and name-space rules without a preprocessor or a type checker; nothing that needs one is inferred. - **Includes** (`imports`, file to file). `#include "p"` resolves beside the including file, else, standing in for an unknown `-I` path, to the one captured file whose path ends with `p`; several are ambiguous. `#include

` resolves only by that suffix and only when `p` has a directory part, so `` never binds a project file. System headers and computed includes (`#include NAME`) stay unresolved with their path as name. - **Visibility.** A file sees its own declarations and those of every captured file its resolved includes reach, transitively. - **Macros first.** A call or type name that a visible macro defines resolves to the macro, as the preprocessor would expand it. - **Calls** through an identifier (`f(x)`) resolve by linkage: a visible definition (the file's own or a header's, `static` or not), else every external definition in the capture, else a visible prototype. Another file's `static` function is never a target. Calls through function pointers, struct fields and expressions are unresolved. - **References** cover typedef names in any type position (declarations, parameters, casts, `sizeof`) and `struct`/`union`/`enum` tags without a body, each resolved in its own name space among visible declarations. A prototype references its definitions (the visible ones for a `static` prototype, the external ones otherwise). - **Conservative locals.** A name bound anywhere in a declaration (parameters, local variables, local typedefs, locally defined tags) is opaque throughout it, so shadowing never produces a wrong edge. Same-named declarations in several branches or files (`#ifdef _WIN32`, `posix.c` / `windows.c`, several programs each defining a helper) make a use ambiguous, listing every candidate: conditional compilation and the build's link units are not evaluated. ## Unexpanded macros The grammar parses source as written. Common macro idioms are handled: - `API int f(void)`: an unknown leading macro is grammar recovery, and the name is the identifier before the parameters, whichever way recovery places it. A declarator that would name a keyword (`API int (f)(void);`) is dropped rather than misnamed. - A block comment inside a multi-line macro body ends the body in the grammar, so the parser sees every block comment as spaces (byte offsets and line breaks kept); all texts and spans still come from the original bytes. - Declarations recovered under a top-level parse error are kept, as in the other slices. Other macro-heavy code parses partially: files with syntax errors report `partial` coverage with bounded diagnostics, and keep every declaration recovery preserves. ## Not modeled These need the preprocessor, a type checker or a build configuration, and stay unresolved (with their name) or absent rather than guessed: - macro expansion: what a macro's body calls, conditional compilation, `#undef`, include guards and macro-generated declarations; - the build's include paths and link units (beyond the suffix rule above), `compile_commands.json`, and system or third-party headers that are not captured; - uses of variables, enumerators and functions as values (`return ERR_X`, `cb = handler`), member access, and calls through pointers; - struct members, enumerators and block-scope declarations as symbols, and block scoping (a shadowed name is opaque in the whole declaration); - K&R parameter declarations, and non-UTF-8 sources (unsupported file evidence). Structural search (`Repository.structural_search`, ast-grep) remains Python and TypeScript only. ## Reliability The shared bounded native query, downward-only node reads, depth limit (65,535), UTF-8 check and bounded syntax diagnostics apply unchanged. Resolution always reruns over the full capture, so adding, removing or moving a header re-resolves includes with all facts reused. Facts are cached by `(c, source digest)` under `oxide-c-facts-v1`; the cache decoder validates types, ranges, identifier names and the scope list, and anything else is parsed again. Derivation components add `c` (`oxide-c-v1`) and `c-parser`; older indices are re-indexed. Evidence and reproduction: [phase-6/c-v1](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/phase-6/c-v1/README.md).

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(found.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            walk = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(walk.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(walk)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

# CLI and MCP usability: fail clearly, expose impact
…
## Approach (chosen)
…
### B1. CLI `oxide impact`
…
`oxide impact PATH KEY [--direction upstream|downstream] [--depth 0..8, default 3]
…
count; then one line per hop: `depth proven key via <via>` (proven `-` when None; `(cyclic)` when
set).

### B2. MCP `oxide_impact`

New tool, read-only, same `repository` resolution and `_read` lock/handle path as `oxide_search`.
Inputs: `key` (required, ≤ 1024 chars), `repository`, `direction` (`upstream` default),
`depth` (0–8, default 3), `limit` (0–100, default 25; MCP bound, below the API's 1000).
Output: the `Impact` structured content, prefixed by `hops_returned`. `stopped_by` (not
`more_available`) says which bound cut the walk: a depth stop means the traversal is incomplete
within the bound, not that more results exist. Compact JSON text leads with the same fields, as in `oxide_search`.
Output schema from `TypeAdapter(Impact)`. Description says when to use it (after `oxide_search`
gives a key) and what `unresolved` means.

Consequence: the server advertises two tools. `tests/python/test_mcp.py` (two places),
`scripts/smoke_dist.py` and the platform smoke's "exactly oxide_search" check are updated to the
two-tool list.

## Verification plan

- New tests: empty-query rules in `test_retrieval.py`; CLI hint lines, empty-query exit,
  `impact` round trip (text and `--json`), unknown key; MCP `oxide_impact` returns a known
  caller (`symbol:tests/test_auth.py#test_decode_claims_parses_payload` upstream of
  `symbol:oxidepy/auth.py#decode_claims`, depth 1), rejects out-of-range bounds and an unknown
  key with `invalid_argument`.
- `mise run verify`; before/after the CLI and MCP probes from the research step.

Exact help strings and the human layout of `impact` output, as long as the fields above appear.

# CLI and MCP usability: fail clearly, expose impact

Status: approved by the user (2026-11-10: "A now then B"). Tier 2 (public API and CLI/MCP surface).

## Intent

Coding agents and developers using `oxide` on a repository hit three problems, measured on
`fixtures/py_repo` (2026-11-10 probes):

1. An empty query exits 0 with zero entries and no message.
2. Unmatched `--symbol`/`--file` hints are dropped from the CLI, and silent in the MCP context text.
3. The graph queries the API already offers (`Repository.impact`: who calls or imports a
   symbol, nearest first) reach neither the CLI nor MCP, so an agent cannot ask "what depends on X".

Also, `not_indexed` advice differs between CLI (no next step) and MCP (names `oxide index`).

## Goals

- A. Failures that an agent or human can act on, with one advice table shared by CLI and MCP.
- A. Hint issues visible in every client that accepts hints.
- B. `oxide impact` (CLI) and `oxide_impact` (MCP) over the existing `Repository.impact`.

## Non-goals

- No change to retrieval, routing, packing, ranking, or the bytes of any valid `search`/`context`
  call. Frozen baselines and ContextBench stay untouched.
- No change to the `oxide_search` tool description in this change. It is the variable of the
  pre-registered discoverability protocol (`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`).
- No degradation rewriting (core strings are not parsed by presentation code), no line/byte
  unit unification, no `entity`/`relations` commands. Each is a separate decision.
- No new dependency.

## Anti-goals

- Presentation code (`cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`) must not parse source, route, select or pack
  (AGENTS.md). Hint and impact logic stays in `api.py`/`core`.
- An empty query must not break selection-only searches: `search("", selection=…)` is used in
  `tests/python/test_retrieval.py` and is valid.
- No success claim from these changes. No held-out run.

## Constraints

- Public API and CLI/MCP changes are tier 2: this spec, a zero-context review, then implementation.
- Protocol: `scripts/agent_eval/session.py` reads `tools=N` from the connection log, so a second
  tool changes what the eval measures. The arm definition needs a dated protocol amendment before
  any further eval result is read. This change does not edit that README.
- Keep every source file at or below 500 LOC.

## Approach (chosen)

Approach A, then B, as the user chose from three options (A only; A + B; rebuild MCP around agent
workflows). The rebuild was rejected: no measured need, and it breaks the single-tool decision.

### A1. Empty query

`_hints` (used by `search` and `build_context`) raises `InvalidArgument` when the query is blank
and no seed hint (`paths`, `symbols`, `selection`, `changed`) is given. Message:
`query is empty: give words or identifiers, or a path, symbol or selection hint`.
Effect: CLI exit 2, MCP `invalid_argument`. With any seed hint the empty query stays valid.

### A2. Hint issues in clients

- CLI `search`: after the entries and before the lexical status line, print one
  `hint: <kind> <hint>: <issue>` line per `HintIssue`.
- CLI `context`: the same lines to stderr, next to the existing `degraded` output.
- MCP `oxide_search` mode=context: `# hint <kind> <hint>: <issue>` header lines, after `# degraded`.
  Mode=search already returns hints in its structured content and text; unchanged.

### A3. One advice table

Move `_ADVICE` from `mcp_server.py` to `models.py` as `ADVICE`, with a `{repository}`
placeholder, and a function `advice(error, repository) -> str | None`. MCP uses it as today
(now with the real repository path). CLI prints `hint: <advice>` after `error[code]: …` when one
exists. `invalid_argument` keeps its own message in both clients.

`api.py` message for an unknown impact key becomes
`no entity 'KEY' in this snapshot; find keys with oxide search`.

### B1. CLI `oxide impact`

`oxide impact PATH KEY [--direction upstream|downstream] [--depth 0..8, default 3]
[--limit 0..1000, default 200] [--data-dir D] [--json]`. Opens with `create=False`.
Human output: a header with the root key, direction, reached count, `stopped_by`, and unresolved
count; then one line per hop: `depth proven key via <via>` (proven `-` when None; `(cyclic)` when
set).

### B2. MCP `oxide_impact`

New tool, read-only, same `repository` resolution and `_read` lock/handle path as `oxide_search`.
Inputs: `key` (required, ≤ 1024 chars), `repository`, `direction` (`upstream` default),
`depth` (0–8, default 3), `limit` (0–100, default 25; MCP bound, below the API's 1000).
Output: the `Impact` structured content, prefixed by `hops_returned`. `stopped_by` (not
`more_available`) says which bound cut the walk: a depth stop means the traversal is incomplete
within the bound, not that more results exist. Compact JSON text leads with the same fields, as in `oxide_search`.
Output schema from `TypeAdapter(Impact)`. Description says when to use it (after `oxide_search`
gives a key) and what `unresolved` means.

Consequence: the server advertises two tools. `tests/python/test_mcp.py` (two places),
`scripts/smoke_dist.py` and the platform smoke's "exactly oxide_search" check are updated to the
two-tool list.

## Verification plan

- New tests: empty-query rules in `test_retrieval.py`; CLI hint lines, empty-query exit,
  `impact` round trip (text and `--json`), unknown key; MCP `oxide_impact` returns a known
  caller (`symbol:tests/test_auth.py#test_decode_claims_parses_payload` upstream of
  `symbol:oxidepy/auth.py#decode_claims`, depth 1), rejects out-of-range bounds and an unknown
  key with `invalid_argument`.
- `mise run verify`; before/after the CLI and MCP probes from the research step.

## Left to the builder

Exact help strings and the human layout of `impact` output, as long as the fields above appear.

import asyncio, json, os, sys
from fastmcp import Client
from oxide.mcp_server import server

REPO = os.path.realpath("fixtures/py_repo")


async def call(c, label, **args):
    try:
        r = await c.call_tool("oxide_search", args, raise_on_error=False)
        text = "".join(getattr(b, "text", "") for b in r.content)
        print(f"\n## {label}: is_error={r.is_error} text_bytes={len(text)} "
              f"structured_bytes={len(json.dumps(r.structured_content)) if r.structured_content else 0}")
        print(text[:900])
    except Exception as e:  # noqa
        print(f"\n## {label}: EXC {type(e).__name__}: {e}")


async def main():
    app = server([REPO], os.environ["OXIDE_DATA_DIR"])
    async with Client(app) as c:
        tools = await c.list_tools()
        for t in tools:
            print("TOOL", t.name, "| annotations", t.annotations)
            print("DESC:", t.description)
            print("INPUT:", json.dumps(t.inputSchema)[:1500])
            print("OUTPUT schema bytes:", len(json.dumps(t.outputSchema)))
        await call(c, "search basic", query="parse headers")
        await call(c, "search no repo arg, symbols hint missing", query="parse headers", symbols=["NoSuch"], paths=["nope.py"])
        await call(c, "context basic", query="parse headers", mode="context", budget=400)
        await call(c, "context bad hint", query="parse headers", mode="context", budget=400, symbols=["NoSuch"], paths=["nope.py"])
        await call(c, "empty query", query="")
        await call(c, "bad mode combo", query="x", limit=5, mode="context")
        await call(c, "other repo", query="x", repository="/tmp")
        await call(c, "natural-language question", query="where is the JWT token decoded and who calls it")


asyncio.run(main())

# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test

Arguments that do not apply to a mode are `invalid_argument` errors, never silently ignored:
…
`query` with `impact`; `key`, `direction` and `depth` outside `impact`. The output schema is any
of the three result types (`anyOf`).

An empty `query` without a `paths`, `symbols` or selection hint is `invalid_argument`.

**Migration (2026-10-18, intentional break).** `oxide_context` is gone. Call
`oxide_search` with `mode="context"`: the arguments, text and structured result are
the old tool's, byte for byte. A call without `mode` is the old `oxide_search`, with
the same arguments, defaults and output (as of that change). Since 2026-11-10 `oxide_search`
changed: an empty query with no `paths`, `symbols` or selection hint is `invalid_argument`,
context text adds `# hint` lines for unmatched hints, and `mode="impact"` was added. A separate
`oxide_impact` tool existed only in uncommitted work and was folded into `mode="impact"` before
commit, so the server advertises one tool.

Structural search (`Repository.structural_search`) is **not** an MCP mode. In a
preregistered agent trial, agents given it matched what they already found with grep
(shape-task F1 0.994 vs 0.978) ([phase-6/structural-mcp-trial](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/phase-6/structural-mcp-trial/README.md)).

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            walk = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(walk.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(walk)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            walk = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(walk.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(walk)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search and mode=impact only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )
