async def test_impact_names_callers_with_proven_depth(indexed: Path) -> None:
    async with Client(server([str(indexed)])) as client:
        found = await call(
            client, "oxide_search", mode="impact", key="symbol:oxidepy/auth.py#decode_claims"
        )
    assert not found.is_error
    value = found.structured_content
    proven = {h["entity"]["key"]: h["proven_depth"] for h in value["hops"]}
    assert proven["symbol:tests/test_auth.py#test_decode_claims_parses_payload"] == 1
    assert value["stopped_by"] is None and value["hops_returned"] == len(value["hops"])
    assert json.loads(text(found))["hops_returned"] == value["hops_returned"]


async def test_impact_rejects_unknown_keys_and_out_of_range_bounds(indexed: Path) -> None:
    key = "symbol:oxidepy/auth.py#decode_claims"
    async with Client(server([str(indexed)])) as client:
        unknown = await call(client, "oxide_search", mode="impact", key="symbol:nope.py#missing")
        too_deep = await call(client, "oxide_search", mode="impact", key=key, depth=9)
        too_many = await call(client, "oxide_search", mode="impact", key=key, limit=101)
    assert unknown.is_error and "error[invalid_argument]" in text(unknown)
    assert "find keys with oxide search" in text(unknown)
    assert too_deep.is_error and too_many.is_error

them. [SPEC](spec/SPEC.md) is the architecture authority and the [ADRs](adr/) record

requirement. The evaluation protocol is in [`fixtures/eval/`](../fixtures/eval/README.md).

Reports, harnesses and raw results behind every verdict are frozen at
[`013e791`](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs)
(`docs/phase-6/<study>/`, `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`, `docs/migration-audit/`). The v1
implementation is pinned at `ac985b28`, the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime at `f79808a`.

## Standing rules

2. Legacy v1 (`ac985b28`) is evidence, not a template. Reusing it requires a stated SPEC requirement, a boundary-fit reason and tests. No legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations or cache locations; derived state is rebuildable from captured source.
3. Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`, I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`. 5. Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Lexical entry points, TreeRouter, the heuristic value and the packer need no model or network.

8. Native libraries (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX, hashing) do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy.

1:# Decisions

26:## Research verdicts

30:| Area | Verdict |

49:| Indexing (`reconcile-keep-cache`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a periodic or failed-watcher reconcile re-walks the tree and lets the stat key choose which bytes to re-read, instead of clearing the capture cache; only an explicit `index()` rehashes. Healthy watchers reconcile every 300 s (was 30 s), failed ones poll every 30 s. Predeclared rule: reconcile ≥25% cheaper with an identical snapshot, standard bench within noise. Same-commit A/B of `_index(True)` (7 runs, status `unchanged`, snapshot equal, 200% CPU/3G, warm page cache): ansible 1540 files median 190→117 ms (−39%), xarray 135 files 19.6→13.6 ms (−31%). Standard bench `fixtures/py_repo --iterations 10 --warm 20` vs the parent commit, two interleaved runs: reopen 54.0/57.2→52.5/52.9 ms, warm search 4.6/4.5→4.5/4.5 ms, peak RSS 193/192→195/192 MiB; warm context is bimodal (≈19 or ≈38 ms) in both builds, so not attributable. Not measured: cold page cache (the saved reads cost more there) and the 10× rarer walk, which is arithmetic, not a run. Limit: an edit with the same size, mtime, inode and ctime after a missed event is caught only by explicit `index()`. |
50:| Indexing (`watcher-restart`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a failed watcher (overflow, watch limit) no longer degrades the repository to polling for life; the freshness thread retries `watch` after 30 s, doubling to 300 s, and forces one full walk once the new watcher is live, so events lost in the gap are recovered. Rule: a restarted watcher must resync and clear `failed`, with the healthy path unchanged (`test_failed_watcher_is_restarted_and_resynced`; 469 passed). Cost removed, measured on ansible (1540 files, 200% CPU/3G, median of 15 warm searches): healthy 7.4 ms, permanently degraded 73.3 ms (every read walks the tree). Not measured: a real inotify overflow (simulated by a raising `watch`), and cold page cache. |
51:| Blast radius in search and context (`blast-radius-in-search`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT automatic blast radius: `BlastRoot` for each of the first 3 entry points, upstream walk to depth 2 (≤20 entities, ≤8 listed files), predeclared in [the 2026-11-11 spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md). Dev split only (15 tasks; held-out not opened). G1 navigation PASS: bundle file recall@1024 0.711→0.800 with blast; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast; 1.07 surfaced files per task that are neither in the bundle nor gold. G2 PASS: 0/15 payloads and 0/15 full scorer outputs differ from HEAD. G4 PASS: MCP text search +6.2%, context +7.0%. G3 FAIL (`scripts/bench.py`, 5×20, 200% CPU/3G): warm search 2.12→15.75 ms on `fixtures/py_repo` (+643%), 2.43→20.97 ms on `psf__requests@22623bd8c265` (+764%); warm context 10.91→25.02 ms (+129%) and 33.39→55.24 ms (+65%); `index_cold` −3%. Cause: each root's upstream walk costs 2.2–8.7 ms (two BFS passes plus NetworkX), and a single pass alone is 0.8–5.8 ms per root, so no single-pass variant can meet the 15% search gate. Code reverted to HEAD; `oxide impact` and MCP `mode=impact` unchanged. Candidate patch and raw numbers: `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`. |

# Decisions

The standing architectural decisions of OXIDE v2 and the research verdicts that constrain
them. [SPEC](spec/SPEC.md) is the architecture authority and the [ADRs](adr/) record
individual decisions; this file never changes an ADR's status, and a Proposed ADR is not a
requirement. The evaluation protocol is in [`fixtures/eval/`](../fixtures/eval/README.md).

Reports, harnesses and raw results behind every verdict are frozen at
[`013e791`](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs)
(`docs/phase-6/<study>/`, `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`, `docs/migration-audit/`). The v1
implementation is pinned at `ac985b28`, the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime at `f79808a`.

## Standing rules

1. One Python package, `oxide` (ADR-0011). A new package or dependency needs a reuse, packaging or API reason.
2. Legacy v1 (`ac985b28`) is evidence, not a template. Reusing it requires a stated SPEC requirement, a boundary-fit reason and tests. No legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations or cache locations; derived state is rebuildable from captured source.
3. Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`, I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`. LadybugDB objects, native IDs, rows and Cypher stay inside `oxide.storage`; the API exposes only domain values. Integrations (the CLI, `oxide mcp`, editors) are clients of `oxide.api` and never parse, route or select.
4. When SPEC and code disagree, SPEC wins. If SPEC is ambiguous, record the ambiguity and a proposal; don't invent permanent ID, schema, transport or model policy to unblock scaffolding.
5. Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Lexical entry points, TreeRouter, the heuristic value and the packer need no model or network.
6. Models judge; deterministic code decides thresholds, traversal, stopping, inclusion, budget, fallback and packing. A `DecisionProvider` seam behind `oxide.core.packing.value` carries abstention and a deterministic fallback; JEV and every learned judge stay optional, and CI never runs a live judge.
7. Structure comes before similarity: retrieval finds entry points, routing finds context, and the TreeIndex keeps cross-edges.
8. Native libraries (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX, hashing) do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy.
9. Never execute repository code or build hooks while indexing. Respect repository scope and source privacy.
10. Frozen baselines keep their provenance. Never regenerate gold or erase a negative result to make a challenger pass; promoting a quality change to a default needs gate evidence.

## Research verdicts

Each row is closed; its report is under `docs/phase-6/<study>/` at the pin above.

| Area | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Graph ranking (`graph-v1`..`v3`) | Resolution raised routed coverage 0.673 → 0.730. REJECT PPR + communities, dispatch routing and the order tiebreak; the loss after routing comes from budget allocation and the relevance signal. |
| Graph navigation (`graph-navigation`, `-v2`, `networkx-v1`) | Basis for ADR-0012 and ADR-0013 (both Proposed). |
| Agent-guided context (`agc`, `agc-v2`..`v4`) | v2 REJECT (adoption); v4 STOP at stage 1, so ADR-0013 stays Proposed without evidence. |
| Optional judges (`decision-study-v1`..`v3`, `jev-reliability`, `jev-order-m1`..`m3`) | v3 PASS (+0.159 at 4,096 units); reliability PASS only under immediate fallback. M3 and ADR-0009 NOT READY: JEV stays off. |
| Storage (`leann-graph-storage`, [`fts-footprint`](fts-footprint.md)) | REJECT compaction; DEFER the traversal memo. ACCEPT `auto_checkpoint=False`, exact wide top-k, blob fsync overlap with a 65,536-entry LRU. REJECT two query threads. |
| Output (`toon-serialization`, `outline-comparison`, `output-integrity`) | REJECT TOON and outlines. Output-integrity fixes shipped. |
| Retrieval (`path-hint-utility` and diagnostics) | PROMOTE path hints (`oxide-select-greedy-v4`): dev hinted `line_recall@4096` 0.685 → 0.785 (Python), 0.360 → 0.626 (TypeScript). REJECT source bodies; file localization NOT VIABLE; router reachability NEGATIVE. |
| Structure (`astgrep-feasibility`, `structural-mcp-trial`) | ast-grep feasible (94 MB, pinned). REJECT a structural MCP tool: grep F1 0.994 vs 0.978. |
| Indexing (`incremental-indexing`, `change-classification`) | Incremental indexing shipped; change classification NOT WORTH IT. |
| FTS distribution (`release-blockers`) | Upstream replaced the FTS 0.21.0 files, so OXIDE mirrors the original builds ([`fts-mirror/`](fts-mirror/RELEASE.md)). |
| Selection (`cover-selector`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT opt-in budgeted-coverage selector `oxide-select-cover-v0` vs `greedy-v4`: dev verified span_recall@1024 0.508→0.358, line 0.548→0.383; heldout span@1024 0.109→0.018; context warm +20%, RSS flat. Stays experimental, not the default. |
| Selection (`excerpt`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT opt-in body excerpts `oxide-select-excerpt-v0` (header + widest whole-line window that fits by exact rendered units, most query-term hits) vs `greedy-v4`: dev verified span_recall@1024 0.508→0.552, line@256 0.180→0.304, but file_recall@4096 0.900→0.833; heldout span@1024 0.109→0.079, file@1024 0.529→0.408 (excerpts spend budget other files' views used); context warm 47→109 ms, RSS flat. Gold: 217 spans = 185 verified + 32 unverified (dev 3, heldout 29); stage tables count verified only. |
| Indexing (`resolver-scope-index`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE: the Python resolver indexes each scope's child declarations by name and precomputes its star-import flag instead of scanning per lookup. Output identical (entities/relations equal, ContextBench gate exact). xarray@1757dff, `scripts/bench.py` 5 iterations under 200% CPU/3G: index_cold median 1.476→1.383 s (−6%); one-file re-index 0.933→0.823 s (−12%, resolution 0.33→0.22 s). |
| Packing (`adjacent-merge`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE `oxide-payload-v4`: same-file views separated only by whitespace share one item and heading (−4% of units on dev at every budget). Python dev verified span_recall@256 0.047→0.080, line@256 0.180→0.193; heldout within tolerance (span@4096 −0.009, file@4096 +0.020). TS heldout span@256 0.018→0.036, dev file_recall −0.010. Frozen as py baseline-v20, ts baseline-v17. Labelling only outermost nested symbols as well saved ~1% more units with no recall change: not kept. |
| Indexing (`delta-publish`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT publishing a re-index as a delta on a copy of the previous `graph.lbug` (xarray, one-def insert in `xarray/core/utils.py`; full publish 0.58 s of 0.83 s). The delta is small without edge ordinals (157 entities, 50 Rel, 93 Opaque rows), but `site` is a global ordinal, so 28,159 rows shift in 39 runs. Apply 0.58 s plus checkpoint 0.13 s = 0.95 s total, against a 0.52 s bulk load. Inexact: in-place FTS maintenance (ladybug 0.21) returned 1054 of 1065 hits for one query. Even with stable ordinals, FTS rebuild (0.20 s) and checkpoint (0.13–0.15 s) leave no gain. Other levers: Python resolution of unchanged files ≤0.17 s upper bound, needs exact dependency tracking through the closed-world dispatch; FTS/CSV pipelining ≤0.06 s. Both not pursued. |
| Indexing (`split-lexical`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE store schema `oxide-ladybug-py-v4`: the FTS documents and index live in a per-generation `lexical.lbug`, built on a side thread while the graph loads and hard-linked from the previous generation when the document digest is unchanged (the index is a function of the documents alone). Exact: ContextBench py (baseline-v21) and TS (baseline-v18) `results.json` identical to v20/v17 apart from the derivation id, metrics byte-identical. Speed (200% CPU cap): one-def re-index ansible 2.53→2.02 s (−20%), xarray 0.81→0.67 s (−17%); body-only edit ansible 2.52→1.91 s (−24%), xarray 0.81→0.66 s (−19%); TS cold index over 82 corpora 418→352 s (−16%). Cost: concurrent pools raise the VS Code cold-index peak RSS 1150→1347 MB (sampled, 2 runs); streaming the graph rows to CSV instead of holding lists brings it to 1268 MB (+10%), time unchanged, CSV bytes identical. CREATE_FTS_INDEX needs ~10 MiB of pool per MB of documents (VS Code 23.2 MB: 256 MiB fails, 270 MiB fits), so the lexical pool is `BUFFER_POOL + 10 × bytes`; at 2× all 14 VS Code corpora failed. In-place FTS patching was 5× faster than a rebuild but left one-ULP drift in multi-term BM25 sums: REJECT. |
| Indexing (`automatic-freshness`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE local in-process watching with incremental capture and full-content recovery. Predeclared gate: in a two-file fixture, unchanged capture reads 2→0 source files and one-file edits read 2→1; automatic updates equal full rebuilds. No retrieval policy change. `scripts/bench.py fixtures/py_repo --iterations 5 --warm 20`, Linux/Python 3.13.17, 200% CPU/3G, same 11 files / 65 entities / 196 relations: median cold index 340.26→354.04 ms, explicit unchanged index 8.04→7.88 ms, reopen 24.26→39.79 ms, warm search 2.04→3.15 ms, warm context 18.57→18.72 ms, peak RSS 188.13→184.06 MiB. Reopen now reconciles source; these are small-fixture overhead measurements, not an end-to-end speedup claim. |
| Indexing (`reconcile-keep-cache`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a periodic or failed-watcher reconcile re-walks the tree and lets the stat key choose which bytes to re-read, instead of clearing the capture cache; only an explicit `index()` rehashes. Not measured: cold page cache (the saved reads cost more there) and the 10× rarer walk, which is arithmetic, not a run. Limit: an edit with the same size, mtime, inode and ctime after a missed event is caught only by explicit `index()`. |
| Indexing (`watcher-restart`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a failed watcher (overflow, watch limit) no longer degrades the repository to polling for life; the freshness thread retries `watch` after 30 s, doubling to 300 s, and forces one full walk once the new watcher is live, so events lost in the gap are recovered. Not measured: a real inotify overflow (simulated by a raising `watch`), and cold page cache. |
| Blast radius in search and context (`blast-radius-in-search`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT automatic blast radius: `BlastRoot` for each of the first 3 entry points, upstream walk to depth 2 (≤20 entities, ≤8 listed files), predeclared in [the 2026-11-11 spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md). No retrieval policy change. `scripts/bench.py fixtures/py_repo --iterations 5 --warm 20`, Linux/Python 3.13.17, 200% CPU/3G, same 11 files / 65 entities / 196 relations: median cold index 340.26→354.04 ms, explicit unchanged index 8.04→7.88 ms, reopen 24.26→39.79 ms, warm search 2.04→3.15 ms, warm context 18.57→18.72 ms, peak RSS 188.13→184.06 MiB. Reopen now reconciles source; these are small-fixture overhead measurements, not an end-to-end speedup claim. |

Healthy watchers reconcile every 300 s (was 30 s), failed ones poll every 30 s. Predeclared rule: reconcile ≥25% cheaper with an identical snapshot, standard bench within noise. Not measured: cold page cache (the saved reads cost more there) and the 10× rarer walk, which is arithmetic, not a run. Limit: an edit with the same size, mtime, inode and ctime after a missed event is caught only by explicit `index()`. |
| Indexing (`watcher-restart`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a failed watcher (overflow, watch limit) no longer degrades the repository to polling for life; the freshness thread retries `watch` after 30 s, doubling to 300 s, and forces one full walk once the new watcher is live, so events lost in the gap are recovered. Rule: a restarted watcher must resync and clear `failed`, with the healthy path unchanged (`test_failed_watcher_is_restarted_and_resynced`; 469 passed). Cost removed, measured on ansible (1540 files, 200% CPU/3G, median of 15 warm searches): healthy 7.4 ms, permanently degraded 73.3 ms (every read walks the tree). Not measured: a real inotify overflow (simulated by a raising `watch`), and cold page cache. |

G1 navigation PASS: bundle file recall@1024 0.711→0.800 with blast; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast; 1.07 surfaced files per task that are neither in the bundle nor gold. # Blast radius in search and context results (design, 2026-11-11)

Status: predeclared before measurement. The gate below was fixed before any candidate
number existed. Results go to `docs/decisions.md`; the gate is not edited afterwards.

## Problem

`oxide_search` mode `impact` (2026-11-10) asks the agent to know it needs a second call.
Agents that find an entry point and stop never learn what depends on it. Impact should
arrive with the search or context result, bounded, not as a separate mode.

## Design

- `Repository.search` and `Repository.build_context` attach `blast`: one `BlastRoot` per
  entry point, for the first `BLAST_ROOTS = 3` entries in result order.
- Each `BlastRoot` reuses the upstream walk behind `Repository.impact`
  (`navigation.walk`, the same proven relations and bounds), with `BLAST_DEPTH = 2` hops
  and `BLAST_LIMIT = 20` entities. It reports: `key`, `dependents` (reached), `tests`
  (reached `test` entities), `files` (sorted distinct paths, at most `BLAST_FILES = 8`),
  `files_omitted`, `unresolved` (same-name call sites OXIDE could not resolve), and
  `stopped_by`.
- The blast radius is diagnostic: it is outside the context budget. Ranking, routing and
  the packed payload do not change.
- MCP: `oxide_search` drops `mode="impact"` and its `key`, `direction`, `depth` arguments.
  Search results carry `blast` in their structured and text payloads. Context text gets
  one `# blast` head line per root, so text-reading clients see it.
- CLI: `oxide impact` is unchanged and remains the detailed exploration tool. `oxide
  search` and `oxide context` print the same blast summary.
- Retained only if the gate passes. Otherwise the code is reverted and this document and
  the verdict stay as the record.

## Measurement scope

- Dev split of ContextBench-py only: 15 tasks over `fixture:py_repo`, `seaborn`, `flask`
  and six `requests` snapshots. The held-out split (`pydata/xarray`, `pytest-dev/pytest`)
  is not opened for this change.
- Baseline is HEAD `6967303`, extracted with `git archive` to `/tmp/oxide-head`, and run
  with the same interpreter and `PYTHONPATH`.

## Predeclared gate (all must pass to PROMOTE)

G1 navigation usefulness. Per dev task with verified gold, `bundle_recall` is the share of
gold files in the 1024-unit bundle. `with_blast_recall` adds the files surfaced by the
blast radius (as the API reports them). Macro mean over tasks: `with_blast_recall −
bundle_recall ≥ +0.02`, and at least one gold file surfaced by blast and absent from the
bundle across the dev split.

G2 payload unchanged. For every dev task, `payload@1024` hashes identical to HEAD, and the
dev contextbench scores (all budgets, verified and unverified) equal HEAD exactly.

G3 latency. `scripts/bench.py` with 5 iterations and 20 warm repeats, under
`systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G`, on `fixtures/py_repo` and
`psf__requests@22623bd8c265`. Median `search_cold`, `search_warm`, `context_cold` and
`context_warm` may each rise at most 15% over HEAD on each corpus.

G4 token overhead. Mean MCP text bytes over the dev split (search at default limit,
context at 1024 units). Search text may rise at most 20%; context text at most 10%.
Structured bytes are reported, not gated. The chars/4 figure is an estimate; no tokenizer
is installed.

## Verdict rule

PROMOTE only if G1 through G4 all pass. Any failure: REJECT, revert the code, record the
numbers and the failing gate in `docs/decisions.md`. Held-out results are not part of
the decision and are not produced for it.

content.text:
**Verdict: REJECT.** Automatic blast radius passes the navigation and token gates but fails latency by a wide margin. I reverted the code to HEAD `6967303`. The only repo change is a verdict row in `docs/decisions.md`, plus an untracked design spec.

## Results against the predeclared gate

The gate was written to `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md` before any candidate number existed. I measured the dev split only. The held-out split was not opened.

| Gate | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|
| G1 navigation | Gold-file recall at 1024 units: 0.711 → 0.800 (+0.089). Blast alone surfaced 3 gold files across the 15 tasks. | PASS |
| G2 payload unchanged | 0/15 payloads and 0/15 full scorer outputs differ from HEAD | PASS |
| G3 latency (`bench.py`, 5×20, 200% CPU/3G) | See table below | **FAIL** |
| G4 tokens (MCP text, chars/4 estimate) | Search +6.2%, context +7.0% | PASS |

Latency medians, HEAD → candidate, in ms:

| Corpus / metric | HEAD | Candidate | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixture `search_warm` | 2.12 | 15.75 | +643% |
| fixture `context_warm` | 10.91 | 25.02 | +129% |
| requests `search_warm` | 2.43 | 20.97 | +764% |
| requests `context_warm` | 33.39 | 55.24 | +65% |
| `index_cold` (both) | — | — | −3% / −4% |

The limit was +15% on each of four medians per corpus, so the change fails.

## Why it can't pass as designed

Each root's upstream walk costs 2.2–8.7 ms. The walk runs two breadth-first passes, one for followed edges and one for proven edges, and each pass queries the store once per graph layer. Warm search was only 2 ms to begin with. Blast was not implemented in a single-pass form because the measured floor already rules it out: one pass alone costs 0.8–5.8 ms per root.

Blast results are useful for navigation, but per-query graph walks cost more than the search they accompany.

## Process notes

- **Revert:** `git checkout` is blocked on this shared checkout, so I reversed my six files by editing forward against HEAD copies. `git diff HEAD` on those files is now empty.
- **Verification:** I ran the targeted suites on the candidate (frozen baseline with no skips, retrieval, context, impact, CLI, MCP 18 tests). I did not re-run full `mise run verify`, since the reverted tree equals the commit verified last turn (558 passed, 7 skipped).
- **Eval protocol:** no amendment needed. The tool surface is back to HEAD, and no eval ran.
- **Artifacts:** candidate patch, probe scripts, and raw JSON are in `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`.

## Options

1. **Precompute at index time.** Store each entity's upstream dependent summary during publish. Search would then read a row, roughly 0.1 ms. This is the only route I see to meet G3 for search. It needs a store-schema change, so it needs an ADR and a publish-cost measurement first.
2. **Keep the current surface.** `oxide impact` and MCP `mode=impact` from `6967303` stay as they are.
3. **Change the latency gate.** An absolute budget (about +14 ms on context and about +18 ms on search) might be acceptable to you. I did not change the predeclared gate, so this would need your explicit decision.

Option 1 is my recommendation if you want blast on search results. I have not started it.

"""Bounded impact and dependency navigation over typed relations (SPEC § Relations).

``upstream`` answers "what depends on this": callers, referrers and importers (incoming
``calls``/``references``/``imports``) and the tests that exercise it (outgoing
``tested_by``). ``downstream`` answers "what does this depend on" (outgoing ``calls``/
``references``/``imports``). The root stands for itself and everything it physically
contains (a class's methods, a file's declarations) and, for a file, the modules that
logically contain it, since imports name modules.

Level-synchronous BFS in domain order with a visited set, so cycles terminate and
results do not depend on store row order. It runs twice: over every followed edge, and
over proven edges only (``resolved`` with a non-heuristic basis), so ambiguous
candidates and the ``tested_by`` heuristic never make a path proven. Reached entities
in a dependency cycle with another reached entity are flagged (strongly connected
components of the reached subgraph). Bounds fire visibly.

The reached subgraph is kept as a NetworkX projection (ADR-0012): ``Walk.graph`` holds
every walked edge in traversal direction, with the ``via`` of its first step in domain
order, as bounded as the walk
itself; ``Walk.stopped_by`` says whether it is complete. NetworkX is imported lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Literal

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import networkx as nx

    from oxide.storage.ladybug import Adjacent, View

NAVIGATION_VERSION = "oxide-impact-bfs-v2"
MAX_EDGES = 20_000  # adjacency rows examined per pass
Direction = Literal["upstream", "downstream"]
_CROSS = ("calls", "references", "imports")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Hop:
    key: str
    depth: int
    proven_depth: int | None
    via: str  # "<kind>:<in|out>:<key reached from>" on a first shallowest path
    cyclic: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Walk:
    roots: tuple[str, ...]
    hops: tuple[Hop, ...]
    stopped_by: str | None  # "depth", "limit" or "edges"; None when exhausted
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str]  # the walked edges, traversal direction, edge attr ``via``


def _steps(
    direction: Direction, key: str, out: Adjacent, into: Adjacent, proven_only: bool
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(neighbor, via) of one entity, in domain order."""
    if direction == "upstream":
        found = [(a, f"{kind}:in:{key}", p) for kind, a, p, _ in into if kind in _CROSS]
        found += [(b, f"tested_by:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind == "tested_by"]
    else:
        found = [(b, f"{kind}:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind in _CROSS]
    return sorted({(n, via) for n, via, p in found if p or not proven_only})


def _roots(view: View, key: str) -> list[str]:
    """``key``, its physical descendants and, for a file, its logical modules."""
    roots, layer = [key], [key]
    while layer:
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, kinds=("contains",))
        layer = sorted({b for k in layer for kind, b, *_ in adjacency[k][0] if kind == "contains"})
        roots += layer
    if key.startswith("file:"):
        into = view.adjacency([key], kinds=("contains_logical",))[key][1]
        roots += sorted(a for kind, a, *_ in into if kind == "contains_logical")
    return list(dict.fromkeys(roots))


def _bfs(
    view: View, roots: list[str], direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int, proven_only: bool
) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, str]], nx.DiGraph[str], str | None]:
    import networkx as nx

    seen = set(roots)
    found: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {}
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str] = nx.DiGraph()
    layer, examined, level = roots, 0, 0
    while layer:
        # Keys the allowance cut are absent, so a pass never reads past its edge budget.
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, MAX_EDGES - examined + 1)
        steps = {k: _steps(direction, k, *adjacency[k], proven_only) for k in adjacency}
        if level == depth:
            beyond = any(n not in seen for k in steps for n, _ in steps[k])
            return found, graph, "depth" if beyond else "edges" if len(steps) < len(layer) else None
        level += 1
        upcoming: list[str] = []
        for source in layer:
            if source not in adjacency:
                return found, graph, "edges"
            examined += sum(map(len, adjacency[source]))
            for neighbor, via in steps[source]:
                if not graph.has_edge(source, neighbor):  # keep the first step's ``via``
                    graph.add_edge(source, neighbor, via=via)
                if neighbor in seen:
                    continue
                if len(found) >= limit:
                    return found, graph, "limit"
                seen.add(neighbor)
                found[neighbor] = (level, via)
                upcoming.append(neighbor)
            if examined > MAX_EDGES:
                return found, graph, "edges"
        layer = upcoming
    return found, graph, None


def walk(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Walk:
    import networkx as nx

    roots = _roots(view, key)
    found, graph, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
    proven, _, _ = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, True)
    cyclic = {k for c in nx.strongly_connected_components(graph) if len(c) > 1 for k in c}
    hops = tuple(
        Hop(k, d, proven[k][0] if k in proven else None, via, k in cyclic)
        for k, (d, via) in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1][0], item[0]))
    )
    return Walk(tuple(roots), hops, stopped_by, graph)

        Hop(k, d, proven[k][0] if k in proven else None, via, k in cyclic)
        for k, (d, via) in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1][0], item[0]))
    )
    return Walk(tuple(roots), hops, stopped_by, graph)


def reach(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Reach:
    """The followed-edge pass of ``walk`` alone: what it reaches and why it stopped, with no
    proven pass and no graph. For callers that need counts, not provenance."""
    roots = _roots(view, key)
    found, _, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
    return Reach(tuple(roots), found, stopped_by)

+def _bfs(
+    view: View, roots: list[str], direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int, proven_only: bool
+) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, str]], nx.DiGraph[str], str | None]:
+    import networkx as nx
+
+    seen = set(roots)
+    found: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {}
+    graph: nx.DiGraph[str] = nx.DiGraph()
+    layer, examined, level = roots, 0, 0
+    while layer:
+        # Keys the allowance cut are absent, so a pass never reads past its edge budget.
+        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, MAX_EDGES - examined + 1)
+        steps = {k: _steps(direction, k, *adjacency[k], proven_only) for k in adjacency}
+        if level == depth:
+            beyond = any(n not in seen for k in steps for n, _ in steps[k])
+            return found, graph, "depth" if beyond else "edges" if len(steps) < len(layer) else None
+        level += 1
+        upcoming: list[str] = []
+        for source in layer:
+            if source not in adjacency:
+                return found, graph, "edges"
+            examined += sum(map(len, adjacency[source]))
+            for neighbor, via in steps[source]:
+                if not graph.has_edge(source, neighbor):  # keep the first step's ``via``
+                    graph.add_edge(source, neighbor, via=via)
+                if neighbor in seen:
+                    continue
+                if len(found) >= limit:
+                    return found, graph, "limit"
+                seen.add(neighbor)
+                found[neighbor] = (level, via)
+                upcoming.append(neighbor)
+            if examined > MAX_EDGES:
+                return found, graph, "edges"
+        layer = upcoming
+    return found, graph, None
+
+
+def walk(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Walk:
+    import networkx as nx
+
+    roots = _roots(view, key)
+    found, graph, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
+    proven, _, _ = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, True)
+    cyclic = {k for c in nx.strongly_connected_components(graph) if len(c) > 1 for k in c}
+    hops = tuple(
+        Hop(k, d, proven[k][0] if k in proven else None, via, k in cyclic)
+        for k, (d, via) in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1][0], item[0]))
+    )
+    return Walk(tuple(roots), hops, stopped_by, graph)

details.oldText:
"""Bounded impact and dependency navigation over typed relations (SPEC § Relations).

``upstream`` answers "what depends on this": callers, referrers and importers (incoming
``calls``/``references``/``imports``) and the tests that exercise it (outgoing
``tested_by``). ``downstream`` answers "what does this depend on" (outgoing ``calls``/
``references``/``imports``). The root stands for itself and everything it physically
contains (a class's methods, a file's declarations) and, for a file, the modules that
logically contain it, since imports name modules.

Level-synchronous BFS in domain order with a visited set, so cycles terminate and
results do not depend on store row order. It runs twice: over every followed edge, and
over proven edges only (``resolved`` with a non-heuristic basis), so ambiguous
candidates and the ``tested_by`` heuristic never make a path proven. Reached entities
in a dependency cycle with another reached entity are flagged (strongly connected
components of the reached subgraph). Bounds fire visibly.

The reached subgraph is kept as a NetworkX projection (ADR-0012): ``Walk.graph`` holds
every walked edge in traversal direction, with the ``via`` of its first step in domain
order, as bounded as the walk
itself; ``Walk.stopped_by`` says whether it is complete. NetworkX is imported lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Literal

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import networkx as nx

    from oxide.storage.ladybug import Adjacent, View

NAVIGATION_VERSION = "oxide-impact-bfs-v2"
MAX_EDGES = 20_000  # adjacency rows examined per pass
Direction = Literal["upstream", "downstream"]
_CROSS = ("calls", "references", "imports")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Hop:
    key: str
    depth: int
    proven_depth: int | None
    via: str  # "<kind>:<in|out>:<key reached from>" on a first shallowest path
    cyclic: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Walk:
    roots: tuple[str, ...]
    hops: tuple[Hop, ...]
    stopped_by: str | None  # "depth", "limit" or "edges"; None when exhausted
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str]  # the walked edges, traversal direction, edge attr ``via``


def _steps(
    direction: Direction, key: str, out: Adjacent, into: Adjacent, proven_only: bool
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(neighbor, via) of one entity, in domain order."""
    if direction == "upstream":
        found = [(a, f"{kind}:in:{key}", p) for kind, a, p, _ in into if kind in _CROSS]
        found += [(b, f"tested_by:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind == "tested_by"]
    else:
        found = [(b, f"{kind}:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind in _CROSS]
    return sorted({(n, via) for n, via, p in found if p or not proven_only})


def _roots(view: View, key: str) -> list[str]:
    """``key``, its physical descendants and, for a file, its logical modules."""
    roots, layer = [key], [key]
    while layer:
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, kinds=("contains",))
        layer = sorted({b for k in layer for kind, b, *_ in adjacency[k][0] if kind == "contains"})
        roots += layer
    if key.startswith("file:"):
        into = view.adjacency([key], kinds=("contains_logical",))[key][1]
        roots += sorted(a for kind, a, *_ in into if kind == "contains_logical")
    return list(dict.fromkeys(roots))


def _bfs(
    view: View, roots: list[str], direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int, proven_only: bool
) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, str]], list[tuple[str, str, str]], str | None]:
    """Level-synchronous walk: what it reached with (depth, via), the walked edges as
    (source, neighbor, via) in first-seen order, and the bound that stopped it."""
    seen = set(roots)
    found: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {}
    edges: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    walked: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    layer, examined, level = roots, 0, 0
    while layer:
        # Keys the allowance cut are absent, so a pass never reads past its edge budget.
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, MAX_EDGES - examined + 1)
        steps = {k: _steps(direction, k, *adjacency[k], proven_only) for k in adjacency}
        if level == depth:
            beyond = any(n not in seen for k in steps for n, _ in steps[k])
            return found, edges, "depth" if beyond else "edges" if len(steps) < len(layer) else None
        level += 1
        upcoming: list[str] = []
        for source in layer:
            if source not in adjacency:
                return found, edges, "edges"
            examined += sum(map(len, adjacency[source]))
            for neighbor, via in steps[source]:
                if (source, neighbor) not in walked:  # keep the first step's ``via``
                    walked.add((source, neighbor))
                    edges.append((source, neighbor, via))
                if neighbor in seen:
                    continue
                if len(found) >= limit:
                    return found, edges, "limit"
                seen.add(neighbor)
                found[neighbor] = (level, via)
                upcoming.append(neighbor)
            if examined > MAX_EDGES:
                return found, edges, "edges"
        layer = upcoming
    return found, edges, None


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Reach:
    roots: tuple[str, ...]
    found: dict[str, tuple[int, str]]
    stopped_by: str | None


def walk(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Walk:
    import networkx as nx

    roots = _roots(view, key)
    found, edges, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
    proven, _, _ = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, True)
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str] = nx.DiGraph()
    for source, neighbor, via in edges:
        graph.add_edge(source, neighbor, via=via)
    cyclic = {k for c in nx.strongly_connected_components(graph) if len(c) > 1 for k in c}
    hops = tuple(
        Hop(k, d, proven[k][0] if k in proven else None, via, k in cyclic)
        for k, (d, via) in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1][0], item[0]))
    )
    return Walk(tuple(roots), hops, stopped_by, graph)


def reach(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Reach:
    """The followed-edge pass of ``walk`` alone: what it reaches and why it stopped, with no
    proven pass and no graph. For callers that need counts, not provenance."""
    roots = _roots(view, key)
    found, _, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
    return Reach(tuple(roots), found, stopped_by)

"""MCP adapter over the public API with server-lifetime repository ownership.

Tool calls are session-independent; local tracking keeps opened indexes fresh.
Unindexed repositories still fail without creating a store.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import logging
import os
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import anyio.from_thread
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``) or ``context`` (``build_context``). Both carry the blast radius
    of the first entry points. Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search) or builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context). Both name what depends on their first entry points.",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. Both modes add `blast`: what depends on the
        first entry points (callers, importers, tests) within two hops. `unresolved`
        counts same-name call sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing;
        `stopped_by` names a bound that cut the walk. Locations, never source. `query` is
        required."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        head += "".join(f"# blast {b.line()}\n" for b in bundle.blast)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            walk = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(walk.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(walk)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search and mode=impact only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )

1:# Decisions

26:## Research verdicts

30:| Area | Verdict |

50:| Indexing (`watcher-restart`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a failed watcher (overflow, watch limit) no longer degrades the repository to polling for life; the freshness thread retries `watch` after 30 s, doubling to 300 s, and forces one full walk once the new watcher is live, so events lost in the gap are recovered. Rule: a restarted watcher must resync and clear `failed`, with the healthy path unchanged (`test_failed_watcher_is_restarted_and_resynced`; 469 passed). Cost removed, measured on ansible (1540 files, 200% CPU/3G, median of 15 warm searches): healthy 7.4 ms, permanently degraded 73.3 ms (every read walks the tree). Not measured: a real inotify overflow (simulated by a raising `watch`), and cold page cache. |
51:| Blast radius in search and context (`blast-radius-in-search`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT automatic blast radius: `BlastRoot` for each of the first 3 entry points, upstream walk to depth 2 (≤20 entities, ≤8 listed files), predeclared in [the 2026-11-11 spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md). Dev split only (15 tasks; held-out not opened). G1 navigation PASS: bundle file recall@1024 0.711→0.800 with blast; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast; 1.07 surfaced files per task that are neither in the bundle nor gold. G2 PASS: 0/15 payloads and 0/15 full scorer outputs differ from HEAD. G4 PASS: MCP text search +6.2%, context +7.0%. G3 FAIL (`scripts/bench.py`, 5×20, 200% CPU/3G): warm search 2.12→15.75 ms on `fixtures/py_repo` (+643%), 2.43→20.97 ms on `psf__requests@22623bd8c265` (+764%); warm context 10.91→25.02 ms (+129%) and 33.39→55.24 ms (+65%); `index_cold` −3%. Cause: each root's upstream walk costs 2.2–8.7 ms (two BFS passes plus NetworkX), and a single pass alone is 0.8–5.8 ms per root, so no single-pass variant can meet the 15% search gate. Code reverted to HEAD; `oxide impact` and MCP `mode=impact` unchanged. Candidate patch and raw numbers: `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`. |
52:| Blast radius v2, reuse (`blast-radius-reuse`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT, same gate. Rewritten to reuse the followed-edge BFS (`navigation.reach`, no proven pass, no NetworkX graph) and existing `view` queries; `impact()` unchanged. Same semantics: dev G1 0.711→0.800, G2 0/15 diffs, G4 +6.2% search / +7.0% context text. G3 still FAILS: warm search 2.12→15.01 ms (+608%, `fixtures/py_repo`) and 2.43→18.50 ms (+662%, requests); warm context 10.91→21.92 ms (+101%) and 33.39→50.96 ms (+53%). Reuse saved about 0.7 ms per search: the per-root BFS is the cost, not the proven pass. Code reverted; patch and numbers in `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`. |

# Decisions

The standing architectural decisions of OXIDE v2 and the research verdicts that constrain
them. [SPEC](spec/SPEC.md) is the architecture authority and the [ADRs](adr/) record
individual decisions; this file never changes an ADR's status, and a Proposed ADR is not a

I rewrote blast to reuse the existing walk, and it still fails the latency gate, so I reverted it. The shared checkout is back to HEAD for all source and test files. The only change left is two rows in `docs/decisions.md`.

**What the rewrite reuses**
- `navigation._bfs` now returns the walked edges as a list. `walk` builds its NetworkX graph from that list, so `impact()` behaves as before.
- A new `navigation.reach` runs only the followed-edge BFS. It skips the proven pass and the graph.
- `_blast` uses `reach` plus existing `view.entities` and `view.mentions` queries. It adds no new traversal.

**Checks on the rewritten code**
- The blast-relevant suites pass, 96 tests. The suites were impact, frozen baseline, retrieval, context, MCP, and CLI.
- The impact-equality test confirms blast matches `impact()` for the same bounds.
- Mypy strict and ruff are clean.

**Results against the gate**

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| G1 navigation | 0.711 → 0.800, unchanged from v1 |
| G2 payloads | 0/15 differ, unchanged |
| G4 tokens | Search +6.2%, context +7.0%, unchanged |
| G3 latency | **FAIL** |

| Metric | HEAD | v2 candidate | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixture warm search | 2.12 ms | 15.01 ms | +608% |
| requests warm search | 2.43 ms | 18.50 ms | +662% |
| fixture warm context | 10.91 ms | 21.92 ms | +101% |
| requests warm context | 33.39 ms | 50.96 ms | +53% |

Reuse saved about 0.7 ms per search. The cost is the per-root followed-edge BFS, not the proven pass or the graph.

**Current state**
- The patch and numbers are saved in `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`.
- The decision record has two rows for the two attempts.

To keep blast on search, the realistic path is index-time precomputation. Search would read a stored row instead of walking the graph, which needs a schema change and an ADR. Alternatively, you could set a new latency budget. Which do you want?
It reuse if possible, minimal code change

I think "minimal and reuse" is what I already measured. The smallest change that reuses the existing graph walk is one `Repository.impact(key, depth=2, limit=20)` call per entry point, projected into `BlastRoot`. That's about 15 lines in `api.py`. It's the first candidate I built, and it failed the same gate with warm search at +643% (2.12 → 15.75 ms on the fixture) and +764% on requests.

Any version that keeps a per-query walk misses the 15% search-latency gate. The minimal version runs the full impact walk with the proven pass, so it's the slowest of the variants I tried, not the fastest.

So I won't reapply it under the current gate. The gate was agreed before measurement, and a change that fails it gets reverted. Your options:

1. **Relax the latency gate** to an absolute budget, then I reapply the minimal version. On the fixture that's about +13 ms per search and +14 ms per context. Those are the numbers you'd be accepting.
2. **Precompute blast at index time.** Store each entry's dependent summary when the index publishes, so search reads a row instead of walking. This is the only route I see to pass the gate. It needs a store-schema change and an ADR first, so it's a bigger job.
3. **Drop blast from search and context.** Keep `oxide impact` and `mode=impact` as they are.

Which one do you want?
Option 2 is a schema change, which means an ADR first. I'll start with the constraints in `AGENTS.md`, then measure whether precomputing for every entity is affordable at index time.

"""Feasibility: cost of depth-2 upstream blast for every entity at index time.

usage: PYTHONPATH=<tree>/src python feas_blast.py <corpus>
Per-entity: navigation.reach per key (store queries). Bulk: one adjacency load of all keys.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
import time

import oxide

usage: PYTHONPATH=<tree>/src python feas_blast.py <corpus>
Index in one handle, then time the walks from a fresh read handle.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
import time

import oxide
from oxide.core import navigation

root = sys.argv[1]
data = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="feas-")
with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=data) as repo:
    t = time.perf_counter()
    repo.index()
    print(f"index cold s: {time.perf_counter() - t:.3f}")

with oxide.open_repository(root, data_dir=data) as repo:
    view = repo._view()
    keys = [row[0] for row in view._query("MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.key")]
    t = time.perf_counter()
    dependents = sum(
        len(navigation._bfs(view, navigation._roots(view, k), "upstream", 2, 20, False)[0])
        for k in keys
    )
    print(
        f"{len(keys)} entities, per-entity walk s: {time.perf_counter() - t:.3f} "
        f"(sum dependents {dependents})"
    )

The feasibility probe is blocked. A raw full-table read of `Entity` fails with a LadybugDB buffer-pool error, even from a fresh read handle. I haven't found the cause, so I can't yet measure index-time cost from the store. I'm stopping before any schema change, because this option has consequences you should approve first.

**What the option costs, from the data I do have**
- A depth-2 walk per entry point took 2.2–8.7 ms earlier. Precomputing one for every entity at index time means N walks. For requests (663 entities), that's roughly 1.5–6 s on top of a 0.41 s cold index. That's an estimate, not a measurement.
- A cheaper version would compute the blast from the in-memory graph during publish, with no store queries. I haven't built or measured that, and it depends on the buffer issue above.
- Storing blast rows changes the store format, so `SCHEMA_VERSION` must bump. Every existing index then fails with "re-index" until someone runs `oxide index` again.

**One question before I continue:** should I write the ADR as Proposed and implement it with the in-memory computation, accepting the schema bump and that existing indexes must be rebuilt?

## Goal
- User's latest request (verbatim, last turn): "2" — chose option 2 from the prior menu: **precompute blast radius at index time** so search reads a stored row instead of walking the graph. Original task context: make blast-radius automatic, bounded, reuse impact graph code, keep `oxide impact` for CLI, benchmark latency/tokens/navigation before retaining. User also asked earlier to "reuse if possible, minimal code change" (answered with the minimal-reuse = already-measured v1 candidate).
- Current state of work: feasibility phase of option 2. Nothing implemented for option 2 yet.

## Constraints & Preferences
- AGENTS.md (repo root): CLI and MCP are clients of `oxide.api` only; they must not parse, route, select or pack. Source files ≤500 LOC. Comments say why. Tests never touch real user data (private data dir). ADRs: Proposed ADRs are proposals; **never change an ADR's status unasked**. Keep public API and versioned formats (derivation components, store schema, payload/units) compatible unless the task changes them; **bump the version when you do**. Don't clean unrelated code. When `mise run verify` passes, commit on current branch without asking (but this task is a schema change needing user approval first).
- Architecture authority: `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/adr/`.
- Tool policy: `bash` shell `grep`/`cat`/`head`/`tail`/`sed`/`find` are blocked — use `_grep`, `_read`, `_glob`, `_edit`. `git checkout`/`git restore` are blocked on this shared checkout ("edit forward" instead; `git apply` worked; read-only git ok).
- Eval protocol: do not run held-out evals; do not edit eval protocol without dated amendment.
- Predeclared gate (set in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`, must not be edited): G1 navigation (bundle+blast recall at 1024 gains ≥ +0.02, ≥1 gold surfaced), G2 payload & full contextbench dev scores identical to HEAD, G3 latency (`scripts/bench.py fixtures/py_repo` and `psf__requests@22623bd8c265`, 5 iterations, 20 warm, under `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G`; search_cold/search_warm/context_cold/context_warm each ≤ +15% vs HEAD on each corpus), G4 tokens (MCP text: search ≤ +20%, context ≤ +10%).

## Progress

### Done
- Prior work (committed HEAD `6967303` "feat(mcp): add impact mode to oxide_search and expose oxide impact"): MCP `oxide_search` has `mode` ∈ {search, context, impact}; `Repository.impact` + CLI `oxide impact`; blank-query → `invalid_argument`; ADR-0013 partly implemented; eval protocol Amendment 6 in untracked `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`.
- Blast-radius candidate v1 (`_blast` → `_impact` → `navigation.walk`): built, measured, **REJECT** (G3 latency fail: warm search fixture 2.12→15.75 ms +643%, requests 2.43→20.97 ms +764%; warm context +129%/+65%). G1 PASS (bundle recall@1024 0.711→0.800; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast), G2 PASS (0/15 payload/scorer diffs), G4 PASS (search text +6.2%, context text +7.0%).
- Candidate v2 (reuse `navigation.reach` = followed-edge BFS only; `_bfs` returned edge list; `walk` builds nx graph from it): built, tests passed (96 tests incl. `test_search_and_context_blast_is_the_bounded_impact_of_each_entry_point`, frozen baseline with no skips), mypy strict + ruff clean; measured **REJECT** same gate (warm search fixture 2.12→15.01 ms +608%, requests 2.43→18.50 ms +662%; warm context +101% / +53%). Reuse saved ~0.7 ms/search.
- Reverted both candidates to HEAD (edit-forward, since `git checkout` blocked). Verified: `git diff HEAD -- src tests` = 0 lines; only `docs/decisions.md` differs (2 inserted rows).
- Decision log rows added in `docs/decisions.md`: row 51 (blast v1 REJECT, dated 2026-11-11), row 52 (blast v2 REJECT). Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md` has a Verdict line (REJECT) inserted at line 6 (untracked file).
- Saved artifacts (outside repo): `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/` containing `candidate.patch` (v1), `candidate-v2-reuse.patch`, probe scripts `nav_bench.py`, `token_bench.py`, `prof_blast.py`, `prof_pass.py`, raw JSON (`nav_head.json`, `nav_cand.json`, `nav_cand2.json`, `token_head.json`, `token_cand.json`, `token_cand2.json`, `bench_head_*.json`, `bench_cand_*.json`, `bench_cand2_*.json`).
- HEAD benchmark baselines (archive at `/tmp/oxide-head`, `git archive HEAD`): search_warm fixture 2.119 ms, requests 2.426 ms; context_warm 10.907 / 33.388 ms; index_cold 203.9 / 426.3 ms. Token baseline: search text 8464 B, context text 5106 B (mean dev).
- Feasibility scripts: `/tmp/feas_blast.py` (measures index-time cost: per-entity walk over all `Entity` keys vs bulk `view.adjacency`). Its per-entity loop uses `navigation._bfs` (HEAD, builds nx graph → upper bound).

### In Progress
- [ ] Feasibility for option 2 (precompute blast at index time). Todo list initialized (9 items: Feasibility = read AGENTS.md rules [done], read publish path/schema version [partly done], measure index-time cost [blocked, see below], write ADR draft for user review [pending]; Implement-after-approval = blast table + schema bump, compute during publish, read stored blast in search/context, measure latency/index cost/gates, run verify and record decision).
- Latest attempt: `/tmp/feas_blast.py` on requests corpus fails immediately after `repo.index()` with `RuntimeError: Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full and no memory could be freed!` raised from `view._query("MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.key")` (ladybug `_query` → `_rows`). Same failure under `systemd-run ... MemoryMax=3G`. Also fails on this repo (`$C`). Earlier profiling scripts that used `repo.search`/`view.entities` worked, so the failing path is the raw `_query`/read view after index.
- Read-view configuration in `src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py`: `BUFFER_POOL = 128 << 20`; read views open `ladybug.Database(..., read_only=True, buffer_pool_size=BUFFER_POOL, max_num_threads=1)` (lines ~252–257; lexical ~273–278). Load pools computed by `load_pool(size)` / `lexical_pool(size)`.

### Blocked
- Raw full-entity query for the feasibility probe hits LadybugDB buffer-pool error (above). Need either to diagnose (e.g., query shape, view lifecycle right after `index()`), or to derive entity keys another way (e.g., monkeypatch `Store.publish` to capture `derived` entities, or use `repo.search` hits / `view.files`).

## Key Decisions
- **Keep gate unchanged** across attempts: any per-query walk fails G3 (lower bound: one followed-edge BFS per root costs 0.8–5.8 ms vs ~2 ms warm search).
- **Option 2 chosen by user**: store per-entity blast summaries at index/publish time; search/context read rows (~0.1 ms, per earlier entity lookup measurement).
- Schema bump is required for option 2 (`SCHEMA_VERSION = "oxide-ladybug-py-v4"` in `storage/ladybug.py` line ~59; `STORAGE_FORMAT = 47`; manifest check at ladybug.py ~220 raises `IncompatibleIndex` "built by store schema ...; re-index"). Existing indexes will require re-index — must be surfaced to the user. ADR for it must be written (Proposed) before schema change; the ADR's status must not be changed unasked.
- Index-time cost risk: precomputing for every entity is O(N × walk); must measure before committing to design. Bulk in-memory computation is the likely design.

## Next Steps
1. Resolve the feasibility probe: obtain all entity keys without the failing raw `_query` (try `repo.search` over symbols, or capture from `Store.publish`'s `derived`, or check why `_query` fails right after `index()`); measure per-entity depth-2 upstream walk cost and a bulk in-memory alternative (one adjacency load + Python BFS) on `psf__requests@22623bd8c265` and on `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide` (note HEAD `_bfs` builds nx graph; a graph-free BFS would be cheaper).
2. Write ADR draft for option 2 (new file under `docs/adr/`, status **Proposed**; do not change other ADR statuses). Cover: storage schema change + `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (re-index required), derivation/versioning, index-time cost, blast bounds (BLAST_ROOTS=3 entries at query time, BLAST_DEPTH=2, BLAST_LIMIT=20, BLAST_FILES=8 from the 2026-11-11 spec), and that stored summaries are per-entity (what search/context read).
3. Present findings + ADR draft to the user for approval before any schema change (AGENTS.md: ask one focused question if the choice could change the implementation; the schema-bump/re-index consequence should be surfaced).
4. Only after approval: implement blast table + schema bump, compute during publish, read in search/context; re-run gates G1–G4 (predeclared gate; no edits) using the saved probe scripts; record verdict in `docs/decisions.md` (new row); run `mise run verify`.
5. Do NOT commit or push without user confirmation for this schema-change work; the repo has no new commits from this task.

## Critical Context
- Repo: `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide`, branch with HEAD `6967303` (`feat(mcp): add impact mode to oxide_search and expose oxide impact`). `git diff HEAD --stat` is clean except `docs/decisions.md` (+2 lines). Ours untracked: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`.
