- User's latest request (verbatim, last turn): "2" — chose option 2 from the prior menu: **precompute blast radius at index time** so search reads a stored row instead of walking the graph. Original task context: make blast-radius automatic, bounded, reuse impact graph code, keep `oxide impact` for CLI, benchmark latency/tokens/navigation before retaining. User also asked earlier to "reuse if possible, minimal code change" (answered with the minimal-reuse = already-measured v1 candidate).
- Current state of work: feasibility phase of option 2. Nothing implemented for option 2 yet.

## Constraints & Preferences
- AGENTS.md (repo root): CLI and MCP are clients of `oxide.api` only; they must not parse, route, select or pack. Source files ≤500 LOC. Comments say why. Tests never touch real user data (private data dir). ADRs: Proposed ADRs are proposals; **never change an ADR's status unasked**. Keep public API and versioned formats (derivation components, store schema, payload/units) compatible unless the task changes them; **bump the version when you do**. Don't clean unrelated code. When `mise run verify` passes, commit on current branch without asking (but this task is a schema change needing user approval first).
- Architecture authority: `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/adr/`.
- Tool policy: `bash` shell `grep`/`cat`/`head`/`tail`/`sed`/`find` are blocked — use `_grep`, `_read`, `_glob`, `_edit`. `git checkout`/`git restore` are blocked on this shared checkout ("edit forward" instead; `git apply` worked; read-only git ok).
- Eval protocol: do not run held-out evals; do not edit eval protocol without dated amendment.
- Predeclared gate (set in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`, must not be edited): G1 navigation (bundle+blast recall at 1024 gains ≥ +0.02, ≥1 gold surfaced), G2 payload & full contextbench dev scores identical to HEAD, G3 latency (`scripts/bench.py fixtures/py_repo` and `psf__requests@22623bd8c265`, 5 iterations, 20 warm, under `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G`; search_cold/search_warm/context_cold/context_warm each ≤ +15% vs HEAD on each corpus), G4 tokens (MCP text: search ≤ +20%, context ≤ +10%).

## Progress

### Done
- Prior work (committed HEAD `6967303` "feat(mcp): add impact mode to oxide_search and expose oxide impact"): MCP `oxide_search` has `mode` ∈ {search, context, impact}; `Repository.impact` + CLI `oxide impact`; blank-query → `invalid_argument`; ADR-0013 partly implemented; eval protocol Amendment 6 in untracked `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`.
- Blast-radius candidate v1 (`_blast` → `_impact` → `navigation.walk`): built, measured, **REJECT** (G3 latency fail: warm search fixture 2.12→15.75 ms +643%, requests 2.43→20.97 ms +764%; warm context +129%/+65%). G1 PASS (bundle recall@1024 0.711→0.800; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast), G2 PASS (0/15 payload/scorer diffs), G4 PASS (search text +6.2%, context text +7.0%).
- Candidate v2 (reuse `navigation.reach` = followed-edge BFS only; `_bfs` returned edge list; `walk` builds nx graph from it): built, tests passed (96 tests incl. `test_search_and_context_blast_is_the_bounded_impact_of_each_entry_point`, frozen baseline with no skips), mypy strict + ruff clean; measured **REJECT** same gate (warm search fixture 2.12→15.01 ms +608%, requests 2.43→18.50 ms +662%; warm context +101% / +53%). Reuse saved ~0.7 ms/search.
- Reverted both candidates to HEAD (edit-forward, since `git checkout` blocked). Verified: `git diff HEAD -- src tests` = 0 lines; only `docs/decisions.md` differs (2 inserted rows).
- Decision log rows added in `docs/decisions.md`: row 51 (blast v1 REJECT, dated 2026-11-11), row 52 (blast v2 REJECT). Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md` has a Verdict line (REJECT) inserted at line 6 (untracked file).
- Saved artifacts (outside repo): `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/` containing `candidate.patch` (v1), `candidate-v2-reuse.patch`, probe scripts `nav_bench.py`, `token_bench.py`, `prof_blast.py`, `prof_pass.py`, raw JSON (`nav_head.json`, `nav_cand.json`, `nav_cand2.json`, `token_head.json`, `token_cand.json`, `token_cand2.json`, `bench_head_*.json`, `bench_cand_*.json`, `bench_cand2_*.json`).
- HEAD benchmark baselines (archive at `/tmp/oxide-head`, `git archive HEAD`): search_warm fixture 2.119 ms, requests 2.426 ms; context_warm 10.907 / 33.388 ms; index_cold 203.9 / 426.3 ms. Token baseline: search text 8464 B, context text 5106 B (mean dev).
- Feasibility scripts: `/tmp/feas_blast.py` (measures index-time cost: per-entity walk over all `Entity` keys vs bulk `view.adjacency`). Its per-entity loop uses `navigation._bfs` (HEAD, builds nx graph → upper bound).

### In Progress
- [ ] Feasibility for option 2 (precompute blast at index time). Todo list initialized (9 items: Feasibility = read AGENTS.md rules [done], read publish path/schema version [partly done], measure index-time cost [blocked, see below], write ADR draft for user review [pending]; Implement-after-approval = blast table + schema bump, compute during publish, read stored blast in search/context, measure latency/index cost/gates, run verify and record decision).
- Latest attempt: `/tmp/feas_blast.py` on requests corpus fails immediately after `repo.index()` with `RuntimeError: Buffer manager exception: Unable to allocate memory! The buffer pool is full and no memory could be freed!` raised from `view._query("MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.key")` (ladybug `_query` → `_rows`). Same failure under `systemd-run ... MemoryMax=3G`. Also fails on this repo (`$C`). Earlier profiling scripts that used `repo.search`/`view.entities` worked, so the failing path is the raw `_query`/read view after index.
- Read-view configuration in `src/oxide/storage/ladybug.py`: `BUFFER_POOL = 128 << 20`; read views open `ladybug.Database(..., read_only=True, buffer_pool_size=BUFFER_POOL, max_num_threads=1)` (lines ~252–257; lexical ~273–278). Load pools computed by `load_pool(size)` / `lexical_pool(size)`.

### Blocked
- Raw full-entity query for the feasibility probe hits LadybugDB buffer-pool error (above). Need either to diagnose (e.g., query shape, view lifecycle right after `index()`), or to derive entity keys another way (e.g., monkeypatch `Store.publish` to capture `derived` entities, or use `repo.search` hits / `view.files`).

## Key Decisions
- **Keep gate unchanged** across attempts: any per-query walk fails G3 (lower bound: one followed-edge BFS per root costs 0.8–5.8 ms vs ~2 ms warm search).
- **Option 2 chosen by user**: store per-entity blast summaries at index/publish time; search/context read rows (~0.1 ms, per earlier entity lookup measurement).
- Schema bump is required for option 2 (`SCHEMA_VERSION = "oxide-ladybug-py-v4"` in `storage/ladybug.py` line ~59; `STORAGE_FORMAT = 47`; manifest check at ladybug.py ~220 raises `IncompatibleIndex` "built by store schema ...; re-index"). Existing indexes will require re-index — must be surfaced to the user. ADR for it must be written (Proposed) before schema change; the ADR's status must not be changed unasked.
- Index-time cost risk: precomputing for every entity is O(N × walk); must measure before committing to design. Bulk in-memory computation is the likely design.

## Next Steps
1. Resolve the feasibility probe: obtain all entity keys without the failing raw `_query` (try `repo.search` over symbols, or capture from `Store.publish`'s `derived`, or check why `_query` fails right after `index()`); measure per-entity depth-2 upstream walk cost and a bulk in-memory alternative (one adjacency load + Python BFS) on `psf__requests@22623bd8c265` and on `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide` (note HEAD `_bfs` builds nx graph; a graph-free BFS would be cheaper).
2. Write ADR draft for option 2 (new file under `docs/adr/`, status **Proposed**; do not change other ADR statuses). Cover: storage schema change + `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (re-index required), derivation/versioning, index-time cost, blast bounds (BLAST_ROOTS=3 entries at query time, BLAST_DEPTH=2, BLAST_LIMIT=20, BLAST_FILES=8 from the 2026-11-11 spec), and that stored summaries are per-entity (what search/context read).
3. Present findings + ADR draft to the user for approval before any schema change (AGENTS.md: ask one focused question if the choice could change the implementation; the schema-bump/re-index consequence should be surfaced).
4. Only after approval: implement blast table + schema bump, compute during publish, read in search/context; re-run gates G1–G4 (predeclared gate; no edits) using the saved probe scripts; record verdict in `docs/decisions.md` (new row); run `mise run verify`.
5. Do NOT commit or push without user confirmation for this schema-change work; the repo has no new commits from this task.

## Critical Context
- Repo: `/home/khoi/Projects/oxide`, branch with HEAD `6967303` (`feat(mcp): add impact mode to oxide_search and expose oxide impact`). `git diff HEAD --stat` is clean except `docs/decisions.md` (+2 lines). Untracked files not ours (do not commit): `.omp/`, `.pi/tasks/`, `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `tests/python/test_agent_*.py`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-*`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-*`. Ours untracked: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`.
- Current file tags observed (may be stale): `src/oxide/api.py#1FB5`, `src/oxide/mcp_server.py#73E7`, `src/oxide/models.py#604A`, `src/oxide/cli.py#74D0`, `src/oxide/core/navigation.py#7F76`, `tests/python/test_mcp.py#E224`, `tests/python/test_impact.py#09C5`, `docs/decisions.md` (latest tag ~`8E6E`).
- Probe/benchmark scripts in `/tmp`: `nav_bench.py <tree> <out.json>` (dev contextbench only, held-out never loaded), `token_bench.py <tree> <out.json>` (MCP output size, per-corpus subprocess), `prof_blast.py`, `prof_pass.py`, `feas_blast.py`; `/tmp/head/` contains HEAD copies of six files.
- Dev corpora used: `fixture:py_repo`, `mwaskom__seaborn@54cab15bdacf`, `pallets__flask@7ee9ceb71e86`, six `psf__requests@*` (cached at `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench/corpora/`). Held-out (`pydata/xarray`, `pytest-dev/pytest`) must not be opened.
- Baseline dev contextbench (`fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-v21`): dev verified file_recall@1024 = 0.711111 (reproduced by HEAD).
- Known env quirk: multiple repositories / certain raw reads in one process can hit ladybug buffer/mmap errors (`Mmap for size 8796093022208 failed`, `store_corrupt` in token probe); token probe works by running each corpus in a subprocess.
- The earlier user message "I think the problem in your code" was never clarified; user later said "Blast radius is using from impact, not a new one" and "reuse if possible, minimal code change".

## Additional Notes
- Reviewer for final report: the answer to the user should state the 2 REJECT verdicts, numbers, and that option 2 requires a schema bump (re-index) and an ADR; no commit made.
- The user's last instruction ("2") is a choice, not yet an approval to change the schema; per AGENTS.md, an ADR and a focused question are needed before the schema change.

2:
3:## Status
4:
5:**Proposed**, 2026-10-25; `mode=impact` implemented 2026-11-10 (see below). The experimental server
6:lives only in `docs/phase-6/agc-v4/scripts/server.py` (at `013e791`). AGC v4, the study
7:that was to decide it, stopped at stage 1 without promoting the interface
8:([docs/phase-6/agc-v4](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/phase-6/agc-v4/README.md)):
9:there is no evidence for this proposal yet. It can become Accepted only through a new
10:preregistered study that promotes it, and the maintainer's agreement.

# ADR-0013: Selective, source-backed graph navigation and tiered context in `oxide_search`

## Status

**Proposed**, 2026-10-25; `mode=impact` implemented 2026-11-10 (see below). The experimental server
lives only in `docs/phase-6/agc-v4/scripts/server.py` (at `013e791`). AGC v4, the study
that was to decide it, stopped at stage 1 without promoting the interface
([docs/phase-6/agc-v4](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/phase-6/agc-v4/README.md)):
there is no evidence for this proposal yet. It can become Accepted only through a new
preregistered study that promotes it, and the maintainer's agreement.

**Partly implemented, 2026-11-10:** `oxide_search` has `mode=impact` over `Repository.impact`, with
the entity `key` as an argument (not `callers`/`callees` in `query`), and `oxide impact` is the CLI
counterpart. The rest stays Proposed: `callers`/`callees` with relation evidence, `outline`, and
downstream unresolved calls need the study below.

## Context

Earlier studies:

| Study | Result | What it showed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AGC v1 (7eca108), REJECT | Tool cost doubled tokens | The cause was OpenCode's code mode, not the tool |
| AGC v2 (5cf699d), REJECT | The agent rarely used a direct tool | Tasks were ones grep/read already solved (94%) |
| AGC v3 (0381565), PROMOTE G (preregistered) | Structural tasks (dispatch, two-hop impact) | Forced use: success 0.86 vs 0.57 for grep/read, false claims 0.67 vs 2.05, cost per success 0.58× |

In v3, the agent picked the tool unprompted in 67% of runs. The guided arm (G) was worse
than the unguided one (D):

- **Measured:** CPS G/D 1.33 (CI 1.10–1.77). The success gap was not significant
  (16/21 vs 14/21, p = 0.73).
- **Mechanism (*inferred*):** the guidance ("callers first, depth 2, don't grep again")
  doubled tool calls and halved verification greps. Precision fell from 0.86 to 0.81 at
  the same recall, with depth-2 walks run from intermediate symbols.
- Analysis: `docs/phase-6/agc-v4/scripts/v3_dg.py` (at `013e791`).

Production MCP already has one tool, `oxide_search`, with `mode=search|context`. A second
tool adds schema to every prompt and one more choice for the agent to make. A new mode
reuses an interface the agent already sees.

## Decision (proposed)

1. **One tool.** `oxide_search` gains three read-only modes. There is no separate
   `oxide_context`, unless AGC v4 shows the split shape has a clear advantage.
   - `mode=callers` or `mode=callees` with a symbol in `query`:
     - the bounded upstream or downstream walk (`Repository.impact`);
     - each hop's count from that symbol and the source line that links it
       (`Repository.relations` evidence);
     - for callers, the name's occurrences that no edge explains, or for callees, the
       calls that weren't resolved.
     - `depth` 1–3, default 1.
   - `mode=outline`: the package map (empty `query`), a file's declarations with line
     ranges, or a symbol's signature, docstring and members.
   - Today's API does not carry all of this. Additive, read-only API is needed first:
     `Repository.outline`; per hop, the linking relation's evidence (`ImpactHop` has only
     `via`), as `path:line` (relation evidence is a byte range, so the API converts);
     and unresolved calls for downstream walks (`Impact.unresolved` is upstream only).
     The server stays a formatter over that API (decision 5).
2. **Source-backed.** Every listed relation cites `path:line` evidence from the index.
   The tool never returns source beyond those lines: exact source is the client's `read`,
   or `mode=context`.
3. **Selective.**
   - No ranking, no packing, and no change to `search` or `context`.
   - The tool's description says when the modes help (relationship questions,
     orientation) and when grep/search is enough (where a single name is defined).
   - No fixed depth, and no "call this first" or "don't grep again" instructions.
   - No system-prompt guidance ships: v3 measured the cost.
4. **Honest about completeness.**
   - Output says it is not exhaustive.
   - It reports the bound that stopped the walk (`stopped_by`) and the unexplained
     residual.
   - Heuristic and ambiguous edges are labelled ("likely"), as in `Impact.proven_depth`.
5. **Boundaries.**
   - MCP stays a client of `oxide.api` (AGENTS.md § Layout): no parsing, routing or
     selection in the server.
   - LadybugDB stays authoritative ([ADR-0002](0002-ladybugdb-knowledge-store.md)).
   - Graph algorithms over projections follow [ADR-0012](0012-networkx-graph-algorithms.md).
   - Code mode is not used.

## Evidence required before Accepted

AGC v4 stopped without promotion, so a new preregistered study must pass. Its rule
should keep AGC v4's terms:

- **Interface:** the single shape is chosen unless the split shape shows the defined clear
  advantage.
- **Gate:** the chosen shape must clear it with *natural* use against a capable grep/read
  baseline. Forced use is a separate diagnostic and never counts as adoption.
- **Tasks:** fresh, rule-selected, across Python and TypeScript and five question types.

Until one does, this ADR stays Proposed (or is withdrawn), and graph navigation stays
API-only (`Repository.impact`).

## Consequences

- **Costs:**
  - About 600 more first-step prompt tokens per session for the larger `oxide_search`
    schema (dev measurement: 615).
  - A new public API read (`outline`).
  - The MCP surface grows by three modes rather than a tool.
- **Risks:**
  - Agents may over-call the graph modes, as G did in v3. The description must stay
    selective, and the gate measures cost per success.
  - Graph incompleteness, which the residual and `stopped_by` make visible.
- **Not decided here:** CLI parity for the new modes; non-OpenCode clients (to be
  measured separately).

# Blast radius in search and context results (design, 2026-11-11)

Status: predeclared before measurement. The gate below was fixed before any candidate
number existed. Results go to `docs/decisions.md`; the gate is not edited afterwards.

Verdict: REJECT (2026-11-11). G3 latency failed, so the code is reverted to HEAD. Numbers and cause: `docs/decisions.md`.

## Problem

`oxide_search` mode `impact` (2026-11-10) asks the agent to know it needs a second call.
Agents that find an entry point and stop never learn what depends on it. Impact should
arrive with the search or context result, bounded, not as a separate mode.

## Design

- `Repository.search` and `Repository.build_context` attach `blast`: one `BlastRoot` per
  entry point, for the first `BLAST_ROOTS = 3` entries in result order.
- Each `BlastRoot` reuses the upstream walk behind `Repository.impact`
  (`navigation.walk`, the same proven relations and bounds), with `BLAST_DEPTH = 2` hops
  and `BLAST_LIMIT = 20` entities. It reports: `key`, `dependents` (reached), `tests`
  (reached `test` entities), `files` (sorted distinct paths, at most `BLAST_FILES = 8`),
  `files_omitted`, `unresolved` (same-name call sites OXIDE could not resolve), and
  `stopped_by`.
- The blast radius is diagnostic: it is outside the context budget. Ranking, routing and
  the packed payload do not change.
- MCP: `oxide_search` drops `mode="impact"` and its `key`, `direction`, `depth` arguments.
  Search results carry `blast` in their structured and text payloads. Context text gets
  one `# blast` head line per root, so text-reading clients see it.
- CLI: `oxide impact` is unchanged and remains the detailed exploration tool. `oxide
  search` and `oxide context` print the same blast summary.
- Retained only if the gate passes. Otherwise the code is reverted and this document and
  the verdict stay as the record.

## Measurement scope

- Dev split of ContextBench-py only: 15 tasks over `fixture:py_repo`, `seaborn`, `flask`
  and six `requests` snapshots. The held-out split (`pydata/xarray`, `pytest-dev/pytest`)
  is not opened for this change.
- Baseline is HEAD `6967303`, extracted with `git archive` to `/tmp/oxide-head`, and run
  with the same interpreter and `PYTHONPATH`.

## Predeclared gate (all must pass to PROMOTE)

G1 navigation usefulness. Per dev task with verified gold, `bundle_recall` is the share of
gold files in the 1024-unit bundle. `with_blast_recall` adds the files surfaced by the
blast radius (as the API reports them). Macro mean over tasks: `with_blast_recall −
bundle_recall ≥ +0.02`, and at least one gold file surfaced by blast and absent from the
bundle across the dev split.

G2 payload unchanged. For every dev task, `payload@1024` hashes identical to HEAD, and the
dev contextbench scores (all budgets, verified and unverified) equal HEAD exactly.

G3 latency. `scripts/bench.py` with 5 iterations and 20 warm repeats, under
`systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUQuota=200% -p MemoryMax=3G`, on `fixtures/py_repo` and
`psf__requests@22623bd8c265`. Median `search_cold`, `search_warm`, `context_cold` and
`context_warm` may each rise at most 15% over HEAD on each corpus.

G4 token overhead. Mean MCP text bytes over the dev split (search at default limit,
context at 1024 units). Search text may rise at most 20%; context text at most 10%.
Structured bytes are reported, not gated. The chars/4 figure is an estimate; no tokenizer
is installed.

## Verdict rule

PROMOTE only if G1 through G4 all pass. Any failure: REJECT, revert the code, record the
numbers and the failing gate in `docs/decisions.md`. Held-out results are not part of
the decision and are not produced for it.

class Store:
    """The single owner of one repository's store in this process.
…

    def publish(
        self,
        capture: Capture,
        derived: Derived,
        components: dict[str, str],
        lexical_unavailable: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Builds, seals and atomically publishes the generation."""
        name, derivation = self._name(capture.snapshot_id, components)
        staging = self.generations / f"{name}.staging"
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
        staging.mkdir()
        try:
            # LadybugDB releases the GIL, so the source blobs and the lexical index are
            # written while the graph loads (docs/fts-footprint.md § 4).
            lexical = None
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
                retaining = pool.submit(self._retain, staging, capture)
                if lexical_unavailable is None:
                    lexical, count = self._documents(staging, derived)
                    old = self.previous()
                    same = old is not None and old.manifest.get("lexical") == lexical
                    reuse = old.directory if old is not None and same else None
                    indexing = pool.submit(self._lexical, staging, lexical, count, reuse)
                snapshot = Snapshot(self.repo_id, capture.snapshot_id, derivation)
                rows = self._load(staging, derived, snapshot)
                retaining.result()
                if lexical is not None:
                    indexing.result()
            facts = json.dumps(derived.facts, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
            (staging / "facts.json").write_bytes(facts)
            manifest = {
                "schema": SCHEMA_VERSION,
                "repo_id": self.repo_id,
                "snapshot_id": capture.snapshot_id,
                "derivation_id": derivation,
                "components": components,
                "lexical_unavailable": lexical_unavailable,
                "files": [
                    [f.path, f.digest, f.size, f.language, f.coverage, list(f.diagnostics)]
                    for f in derived.files
                ],
                "skipped": [[s.path, s.reason] for s in capture.skipped],
                "case_collisions": [list(group) for group in capture.case_collisions],
                "entities": len(derived.entities),
                "relations": len(derived.edges),
                "rows": rows,
                "lexical": lexical,
                "facts": {"format": FACTS_FORMAT, "digest": digest(facts)},
            }
            self._seal(staging, manifest)
            target = self.generations / name
            if target.exists():
                # The unreadable generation this rebuild replaces. A crash between the two
                # renames is undone on the next open (_recover); a failure, just below.
                # Close our own view of it first: Windows can't rename a directory with
                # open files.
                self._drop_view()
                os.rename(target, self.generations / f"{name}.replaced")
            os.rename(staging, target)
            _fsync(self.generations)
        except BaseException:
            shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
            self._restore(name)
            raise
        _write_atomic(self.dir / "CURRENT", name.encode())
        previous, self.current = self.current, name
        self._drop_view()
        for stale in {previous, f"{name}.replaced"} - {name, None}:
            shutil.rmtree(self.generations / str(stale), ignore_errors=True)

    def _retain(self, staging: Path, capture: Capture) -> None:
        """Makes the captured bytes durable in the staging's ``source`` directory."""
        source = staging / "source"
        source.mkdir()
        retained = self.generations / self.current / "source" if self.current else None
        for f in capture.files:
            name = f.digest.removeprefix("sha256:")
            blob = source / name
            if blob.exists() or (retained and _link(retained / name, blob, f.data)):
                continue  # a linked blob was made durable when its generation was sealed
            blob.write_bytes(f.data)
            _fsync(blob)
        _fsync(source)

    def _documents(self, staging: Path, derived: Derived) -> tuple[str, int]:
        """Writes the lexical documents; their digest identifies the lexical index."""
        csv = staging / "Doc.csv"
        count = _write_csv(csv, ((e.key, document(e)) for e in derived.entities))
        return digest(csv.read_bytes()), count

    def _lexical(self, staging: Path, documents: str, count: int, reuse: Path | None) -> None:
        """Builds ``lexical.lbug`` from ``Doc.csv``, or links ``reuse``'s, a readable
        generation with the same documents: the index is a function of them alone."""
        csv, target = staging / "Doc.csv", staging / "lexical.lbug"
        if reuse is not None:
            try:
                os.link(reuse / "lexical.lbug", target)
                csv.unlink()
                return
            except OSError:
                pass  # no hard links here: build it
        # One thread: on two, FTS BM25 scores drift by one ULP in ~10% of builds
        # (indexing-throughput § 9 at 013e791). Only the final CHECKPOINT writes pages:
        # an auto-checkpoint inside CREATE_FTS_INDEX leaves dead pages (docs/fts-footprint.md).
        db = ladybug.Database(
            str(target),
            buffer_pool_size=lexical_pool(csv.stat().st_size),
            max_num_threads=1,
            auto_checkpoint=False,
        )
        conn = ladybug.Connection(db)
        try:
            for statement in _LEXICAL_SCHEMA:
                _rows(conn, statement)
            options = "header=false, quote='\"', escape='\"', delim=',', parallel=false"
            _rows(conn, f"COPY Doc FROM {_literal(csv)} ({options})")
            csv.unlink()
            read = _rows(conn, "MATCH (d:Doc) RETURN count(d)")[0][0]
            if read != count:
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"read back {read} documents, wrote {count}")
            _rows(conn, "CREATE (:Identity {key: $key})", {"key": documents})
            _rows(conn, f"LOAD EXTENSION {_literal(fts_location())}")
            _rows(conn, "CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('Doc', 'lexical', ['terms'], stemmer := 'porter')")
            _rows(conn, "CHECKPOINT")
        finally:
            conn.close()
            db.close()

    def _seal(self, staging: Path, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Writes the manifest, then makes the staging durable."""
        (staging / "MANIFEST.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(manifest, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        for path in staging.iterdir():
            # A linked lexical index was made durable when its generation was sealed (as
            # with blobs); flushing it would open a file the still-open previous view holds,
            # which Windows may refuse.
            if path.is_file() and path.stat().st_nlink == 1:
                _fsync(path)
        _fsync(staging)

    def _load(self, staging: Path, derived: Derived, snapshot: Snapshot) -> dict[str, int]:
        # Rows stream to CSV instead of lists: those lists were the largest Python share
        # of the publish peak on VS Code while the lexical index builds alongside.
        none = SourceRef("", -1, -1, "")

        def entities() -> Iterator[tuple[object, ...]]:
            for e in derived.entities:
                src = e.source or none
                row = (e.key, e.category, e.kind, e.name, e.signature or "", src.path, src.start)
                yield (*row, src.end, src.digest, e.test)

        unresolved: dict[str, tuple[object, ...]] = {}

        def tail(site: int, edge: Edge) -> tuple[object, ...]:
            ev = edge.evidence or none
            return (edge.name or "", site, ev.path, ev.start, ev.end)

        def rels() -> Iterator[tuple[object, ...]]:
            for site, edge in enumerate(derived.edges):
                for target in edge.targets:
                    yield (
                        edge.source,
                        target,
                        edge.kind,
                        edge.resolution,
                        edge.basis,
                        *tail(site, edge),
                    )

        def opaque() -> Iterator[tuple[object, ...]]:
            for site, edge in enumerate(derived.edges):
                if edge.resolution == "unresolved":
                    node = unresolved_key(edge.name or "")
                    unresolved.setdefault(node, (node, node[2:]))
                    yield (edge.source, node, edge.kind, edge.basis, *tail(site, edge))

        written = {
            table: _write_csv(staging / f"{table}.csv", rows)
            for table, rows in (("Entity", entities()), ("Rel", rels()), ("Opaque", opaque()))
        }
        # Filled while Opaque was written; COPY still loads nodes before relationships.
        written["Unresolved"] = _write_csv(staging / "Unresolved.csv", unresolved.values())
        tables = ("Entity", "Unresolved", "Rel", "Opaque")
        size = sum((staging / f"{table}.csv").stat().st_size for table in tables)
        pool = load_pool(size)
        # The staging load alone gets a second thread for COPY (rows unchanged); read views
        # keep one.
        db = ladybug.Database(
            str(staging / "graph.lbug"),
            buffer_pool_size=pool,
            max_num_threads=2,
            auto_checkpoint=False,
        )
        conn = ladybug.Connection(db)
        try:
            if db.get_storage_version() != STORAGE_FORMAT:
                raise IncompatibleIndex(f"ladybug storage format is not {STORAGE_FORMAT}")
            for statement in _SCHEMA:
                _rows(conn, statement)
            _rows(conn, "BEGIN TRANSACTION")
            for table in tables:
                csv = staging / f"{table}.csv"
                if written[table]:
                    options = "header=false, quote='\"', escape='\"', delim=',', parallel=false"
                    _rows(conn, f"COPY {table} FROM {_literal(csv)} ({options})")
                csv.unlink()
            _rows(conn, "CREATE (:Identity {key: $key})", {"key": identity(snapshot)})
            _rows(conn, "COMMIT")
            counted = {
                "Entity": "MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN count(e)",
                "Unresolved": "MATCH (u:Unresolved) RETURN count(u)",
                "Rel": "MATCH ()-[r:Rel]->() RETURN count(r)",
                "Opaque": "MATCH ()-[r:Opaque]->() RETURN count(r)",
            }
            read = {table: _rows(conn, query)[0][0] for table, query in counted.items()}
            if read != written:
                # COPY can drop rows whose endpoints are missing; never publish that.
                raise StoreCorrupt(f"read back {read}, wrote {written}")
            _rows(conn, "CHECKPOINT")
        finally:
            conn.close()
            db.close()
        return read

# AGENTS.md

OXIDE v2 (on `main`): a structural context engine for agents. One Python package, `oxide`, in `src/oxide/` (ADR-0011); the Rust/Bun implementation it replaced is recoverable at `f79808a`.
`CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to this file, so Claude and Codex share one root policy.

The architecture authority is `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, with standing rules and research verdicts in `docs/decisions.md`, the evaluation protocol in `fixtures/eval/README.md` and decisions in `docs/adr/` (Proposed ADRs are proposals, not Accepted decisions; never change an ADR's status unasked). When they disagree with anything else in the repo, they win.

This file is always loaded; keep it short. New commands go in `docs/agents/workflow.md`; the public API is documented in `docs/public-api.md`.

## Layout and ownership

- `src/oxide/api.py`, `models.py`: the public API and its typed results/errors, the stable product boundary.
- `src/oxide/core/`: repository intelligence and deterministic policy (Python slice, derivation, retrieval, TreeRouter, selection/packing). No filesystem or database access except through the read view it is given.
- `src/oxide/capture.py`, `src/oxide/storage/`: worktree capture; LadybugDB ownership, generations, publication and queries. Nothing else touches LadybugDB.
- `src/oxide/cli.py`, `src/oxide/mcp_server.py` (FastMCP) and future editor adapters: Python clients of `oxide.api` only. They must not parse source, route, select or pack.
- Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Judges, if ever added, are optional external services.
- Toolchain: Mise is the entrypoint (`mise run verify`, which CI runs); uv manages Python and dependencies (`pyproject.toml`, committed `uv.lock`); pytest, Ruff, mypy `--strict`. Rust, Bun/TypeScript, pnpm, Deno and `packages/*` are retired; don't reintroduce them without an ADR.

## How to work

- For fully-autonomous tasks, don't poll background tasks; they will send you their output once they're done.
- Implementation first: read the code, change it, add or adjust a test, `mise run verify`; before a push also `mise run pythons` (CI's 3.12/3.14 rows). Feature, bug-fix, language and refactor work needs no study, preregistration, plan doc or report.
- Run `mise run tier` before review/commit. Tier 0 needs `mise run verify`; tier 1 also needs an independent zero-context review using the printed rubric(s); tier 2 additionally needs a Goldfish-reviewed intent spec before implementing a feature or behavior change. The tier and review flow are in `docs/agents/workflow.md`. Agents may commit after required checks; human review remains at merge.
- Library first: an existing helper, the standard library or an installed dependency (tree-sitter queries, LadybugDB queries, NetworkX) before your own code. Native libraries do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy. A new dependency needs a reuse, packaging or API reason (SPEC § System architecture).
- No speculative abstractions, flags, options or features: build only what the current phase needs. Don't duplicate logic or policy, but don't add an abstraction just to remove a few repeated lines.
- Minimal documentation: update only the doc that owns a changed fact (SPEC, `docs/public-api.md`, `docs/agents/workflow.md`). No new design notes, plans or reports unless asked or a gate cites them. Comments say why, never what.
- Graph selection is algorithm-driven: a named, standard graph algorithm (NetworkX or a LadybugDB query) over stored relations with a stated objective, not hand-tuned weights or ad-hoc traversal.
- Benchmark-backed decisions: a quality or performance claim needs before/after numbers (ContextBench gates per `docs/agents/workflow.md` for retrieval/routing/packing/selection, `scripts/bench.py` for speed). Fix the pass/fail rule before reading held-out results; record the verdict as one row in `docs/decisions.md` § Research verdicts. No numbers, no claim, no merge.
- Keep changes small and cohesive. Don't clean up unrelated code during a focused task.
- Keep the public API and versioned formats (derivation components, store schema, payload/units versions) compatible unless the task says to change them; bump the version when you do. Legacy v1 compatibility (SQLite indexes, symbol ids, CLI/MCP/JSON surface) and the retired Rust/TS protocol are not requirements (SPEC § Compatibility policy).
- Fix root causes. Don't weaken tests, regenerate goldens or re-baseline just to make a failure go away.
- Experiments are only for claims a test can't settle: the quality and performance claims above, or promoting an optional judge.
- Read the code, tests and docs before stating how something works. Label each claim as measured or inferred.
- If missing or ambiguous information could change the implementation, check the repo first. If that doesn't settle it, ask one focused question instead of guessing. Don't invent permanent ID/schema/transport/model policy to unblock scaffolding (`docs/decisions.md` rule 4).
- Before finishing, read the full diff for accidental changes in scope, public API surface (`oxide/__init__.py`), dependencies (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`) or generated files.
- Tests never touch real user data: every test and subprocess gets a private data location (`tests/python/conftest.py`).
- When an implementation is done and `mise run verify` passes, commit it on the current worktree branch without asking. Don't push, tag, release, edit GitHub issues or roadmaps, or start the next phase unless asked.
- Keep every OXIDE source file at or below 500 LOC. Tests, docs and CSS are exempt, and so are vendored or generated agent tooling (`.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode/`), which stay as their tools ship them. Markdown is documentation, not source. Split a source file before completion if your change takes it over the limit.
- If unsure about a problem or a bug, search relevant sources of the problem before tackling it.

## Read before touching

| Area | Read first |
|---|---|
| Anything architectural | `docs/spec/SPEC.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/adr/` |
| Python engine, storage, removed/retained features | `docs/adr/0011-python-engine-vectorless.md`, `docs/public-api.md` |
| Build, test, lint, commit format | `docs/agents/workflow.md` |
| Issues, triage labels, domain docs | `docs/agents/` (`issue-tracker.md`, `triage-labels.md`, `domain.md`) |
| Historical evidence and legacy reproduction | `docs/decisions.md` (verdicts; reports and the migration audit are pinned at `013e791`). Port semantic lessons only where current SPEC requires them; legacy layout and APIs are not v2 instructions. |
| v2 review policy | `docs/review/` — reviewer-facing invariants for the Python engine (public API, storage/generations, core/retrieval, capture/language, evidence/benchmarks). Architecture authority remains `docs/spec/SPEC.md` and `docs/decisions.md`. |

## Always-on rules

- Legacy code and docs are historical evidence, not a template (SPEC, `docs/decisions.md` rule 2). The old implementation is recoverable at `ac985b28`; don't port it into `src/oxide/` without a stated SPEC requirement.
- Retrieval, routing and packing changes are evaluated per SPEC § Evaluation against the frozen baselines (`tests/python/test_baseline.py` checks Phase 3 exactly); never regenerate a frozen artifact to make a failure pass. Legacy numbers in pinned historical reports are historical comparators, not v2 gates.
- Models judge; deterministic code decides. Keep JEV and learned judges optional; there are no embeddings. The deterministic offline path needs no model or network (only `oxide prepare` fetches the pinned FTS extension, explicitly).
- A restriction is a conclusion you earn from a real failure, not a field you read. Never report an operation as blocked, unavailable, or not-permitted based on a metadata flag, a config field, or a docs claim. Attempt it and quote the actual error. If you genuinely cannot attempt it, say "not attempted", never "we can't".

In repositories indexed by CodeGraph (a `.codegraph/` directory exists at the repo root), reach for it BEFORE grep/find or reading files when you need to understand or locate code:

- **MCP tool** (when available): `codegraph_explore` answers most code questions in one call — the relevant symbols' verbatim source plus the call paths between them, including dynamic-dispatch hops grep can't follow. Name a file or symbol in the query to read its current line-numbered source. If it's listed but deferred, load it by name via tool search.
- **Shell** (always works): `codegraph explore "<symbol names or question>"` prints the same output.

If there is no `.codegraph/` directory, skip CodeGraph entirely — indexing is the user's decision.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ContextBundle:

    query: str

    endpoint: str
    manifest: str

class OxideError(Exception):
    """Base of every OXIDE failure; ``code`` is stable, the message is for humans."""

class InvalidPath(OxideError):
    code = "invalid_path"


class OwnershipConflict(OxideError):
    code = "ownership_conflict"

def module_name(path: str) -> str | None:
    if not path.endswith(".py"):
        return None
    parts = path[:-3].split("/")
    if parts[-1] == "__init__":
        parts.pop()
    return ".".join(parts) if parts and all(p.isidentifier() for p in parts) else None

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Derived:
    files: tuple[FileInfo, ...]
    entities: tuple[Entity, ...]
    edges: tuple[Edge, ...]
    # Encoded facts of every parsed file, by dialect and digest (``FACTS_FORMAT``): a
    # cache for the next derivation, not knowledge.
    facts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
    reused: int = field(default=0, compare=False)  # files whose cached facts were usable


def components(storage: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Named versions of everything that shapes a generation (ADR-0010 § DerivationId)."""
    parser = f"tree-sitter={version('tree-sitter')}"
    return {
        "id-namespace": ID_NAMESPACE,
        "python": python.VERSION,
        "python-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-python={version('tree-sitter-python')}",
        "typescript": typescript.VERSION,
        "typescript-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-typescript={version('tree-sitter-typescript')}",
        "javascript": typescript.JAVASCRIPT_VERSION,
        "javascript-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-javascript={version('tree-sitter-javascript')}",
        "go": go.VERSION,
        "go-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-go={version('tree-sitter-go')}",
        "rust": rust.VERSION,
        "rust-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-rust={version('tree-sitter-rust')}",
        "java": java.VERSION,
        "java-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-java={version('tree-sitter-java')}",
        "c": c.VERSION,
        "c-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-c={version('tree-sitter-c')}",
        "cpp": cpp.VERSION,
        "cpp-parser": f"{parser} tree-sitter-cpp={version('tree-sitter-cpp')}",
        "terms": TERMS_VERSION,
        "tree-projection": TREE_PROJECTION,
        **storage,
    }


def derivation_id(parts: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    encoded = json.dumps(sorted(parts.items()), separators=(",", ":")).encode()
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()

class Repository:
    def __init__(
…
    @serialized
    def _context(
…
        """``build_context``, optionally ordered ``by`` a judge. Internal (ADR-0009 § 5)."""
…
        budget = _count("budget", budget, MAX_BUDGET)
        view = self._view()
        found = retrieval.retrieve(view, query, hints)
        entries = {e.key: e for e in found.entries}
        route = routing.route(view, list(entries))
        routed = {c.key: c for c in route.candidates}
        later = sorted((k for k in routed if k not in entries), key=lambda k: (routed[k].depth, k))
        order = [k for k in entries if k in routed] + later
        beyond = max(0, len(order) - packing.GRAPH_NODES)
        order = order[: packing.GRAPH_NODES]
        known = view.entities([*order, *(a for k in order for a in packing.ancestors(k))])
        hinted = {k[5:] for k, e in entries.items() if any(s.kind == "path" for s in e.seeds)}
        pool = [
            packing.Candidate(
                known[k],
                routed[k].depth,
                entries[k].rank if k in entries else None,
                bool(entries[k].seeds) if k in entries else False,
                (source := known[k].source) is not None and source.path in hinted,
                entries[k].score if k in entries else None,
                tuple(f"{s.kind}:{s.hint}" for s in entries[k].seeds) if k in entries else (),
                routed[k].origins,
            )
            for k in order
            if k in known
        ]
        # Module-level views need the top-level declarations of every parsed file.
        files = [
            c.entity.key
            for c in pool
            if c.entity.category == "file"
            and c.entity.source is not None
            and view.files[c.entity.source.path].coverage != "unsupported"
        ]
        children = view.adjacency(files, kinds=("contains",))
        tops = view.entities(
            b for k in files for kind, b, *_ in children[k][0] if kind == "contains"
        )
        declarations = {
            k: [
                (s.start, s.end)
                for kind, b, *_ in children[k][0]
                if kind == "contains" and b in tops and (s := tops[b].source) is not None
            ]
            for k in files
        }
        judge = by(query, view.snapshot.derivation_id, view.source) if by else None
        items, omissions = packing.pack(pool, known, budget, view.source, declarations, judge)
        degradations = []
        if found.lexical.state != "ran":
            degradations.append(f"lexical channel {found.lexical.state}: {found.lexical.detail}")
        if route.stopped_by is not None:
            degradations.append(f"routing stopped by its {route.stopped_by} bound")
        if beyond:
            degradations.append(f"{beyond} routed candidates beyond the graph node limit")
        incomplete = {f.path for f in view.files.values() if f.coverage != "complete"}
        used_paths = {c.entity.source.path for c in pool if c.entity.source is not None}
        degradations += [f"incomplete parse: {path}" for path in sorted(used_paths & incomplete)]
        if judge is not None and judge.outcome not in (None, "judged"):
            degradations.append(f"judge {judge.identity} fell back: {judge.outcome}")
        summary = RouteSummary(
            route.root_fallback,
            route.regions,
            len(route.candidates),
            route.deferred,
            route.fanout_truncations,
            route.stopped_by,
        )
        versions = {
            "retrieval": retrieval.RETRIEVAL_VERSION,
            "router": routing.ROUTER_VERSION,
            "selector": packing.SELECTOR_VERSION,
            "payload": packing.PAYLOAD_VERSION,
            "derivation": view.snapshot.derivation_id,
        }
        if judge is not None and judge.outcome == "judged":
            versions |= judge.versions
        return ContextBundle(
            snapshot=view.snapshot,
            query=query,
            budget=budget,
            used=sum(i.units for i in items),
            units=packing.UNITS_VERSION,
            items=tuple(items),
            omissions=tuple(omissions),
            lexical=found.lexical,
            hints=tuple(found.issues),
            route=summary,
            degradations=tuple(degradations),
            versions=versions,
        )


def open_repository(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    data_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    create: bool = True,
) -> Repository:
    """Opens (and exclusively owns) the store of the repository at ``path``. Nothing is
    indexed until ``index()``; reads before that raise ``NotIndexed``. With
    ``create=False`` (read-only clients) a repository without a store raises
    ``NotIndexed`` here, and nothing is written."""
    return Repository(path, data_dir, create)


def index_repository(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, data_dir: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None
) -> IndexReport:
    with Repository(path, data_dir) as repo:
        return repo.index()


def prepare() -> Path:
    """Fetches and verifies the pinned FTS extension (``oxide prepare``); returns its
    path. The only network access OXIDE makes, and only when called."""
    return prepare_fts()

"""Typed public data model of OXIDE v2 (ADR-0011, SPEC § Repository knowledge model).

Every value here is plain, immutable data. Entity keys are the domain identity
(ADR-0010): deterministic, snapshot-local and never a database row id.

- repository: ``repo``
- module: ``module:python:a.b``, ``module:typescript:src/a``
- file: ``file:<repo path>``
- symbol: ``symbol:<repo path>#Outer.inner~1`` (``~n`` only for a nonzero ordinal)

Domain order is the code point order of keys.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal

Category = Literal["repository", "module", "file", "symbol"]
RelationKind = Literal[
    "contains", "contains_logical", "defines", "references", "calls", "imports", "tested_by"
]
Resolution = Literal["resolved", "ambiguous", "unresolved"]
Basis = Literal["syntactic", "resolved", "heuristic"]
Coverage = Literal["complete", "partial", "unsupported"]
SkipReason = Literal["symlink", "special", "too_large", "unreadable", "invalid_name"]
HintKind = Literal["selection", "path", "symbol", "changed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class SourceRef:
    """Half-open byte range ``[start, end)`` of one captured file, named by its digest."""

# ADR-0014: Precomputed blast radius in search and context results

## Status

**Proposed**, 2026-11-11. Implemented in the same change, so the code is the evidence:
the gate below decides whether it stays. Until a verdict in `docs/decisions.md` promotes
it, this ADR stays Proposed. It changes the 2026-11-10 `oxide_search` `mode=impact`
implementation recorded in [ADR-0013](0013-graph-navigation-in-oxide-search.md); ADR-0013's
own status is not changed.

## Context

The 2026-11-11 design put the blast radius into `search` and `context`, computed by a walk
per query (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`). Both
variants failed the predeclared latency gate (G3), recorded in `docs/decisions.md`:

| Variant | Warm search, fixture / requests | Warm context, fixture / requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1: walk through `navigation.walk` (networkx) | 2.12 → 15.75 ms (+643%) / 2.43 → 20.97 ms (+764%) | +129% / +65% |
| v2: reuse `navigation.reach` (edges only) | 2.12 → 15.01 ms (+608%) / 2.43 → 18.50 ms (+662%) | +101% / +53% |

Each entry point needs a depth-2 walk of database queries, which costs milliseconds per
query, and no reuse of the walk code removes that cost. The G1 usefulness gain was real
(bundle recall at 1024 units 0.711 → 0.800), so the information is worth the latency only
if it is read, not walked.

## Decision

1. **Store one row per entity at publication.** Each generation holds a `Blast` node per
   entity: the bounded upstream walk of `Repository.impact` (depth 2, limit 20), summarized as
   `dependents`, `tests`, `file_count`, `files` (the first 8 distinct paths), `unresolved`
   and `stopped_by`. Blast is part of the sealed generation, so it can never be stale.
2. **Compute it with the same walk.** `core/blast.py` runs `navigation.walk` over an
   in-memory view of the generation's relations. That view mirrors `View.adjacency` and
   `View.mentions`, including the edge allowance, so the stored value equals what
   `Repository.impact` returns for the same entity. `navigation.walk` depends on a protocol
   with one method, `adjacency`, which both the read view and the in-memory view provide.
3. **Read, don't walk.** `search` and `build_context` attach the rows of their first
   `BLAST_ROOTS = 3` entries as `blast`. The read is one key-filtered query for at most three
   keys. Ranking, routing and packing do not change, so the payload is unchanged.
4. **MCP.** `oxide_search` drops `mode="impact"` and its `key`, `direction` and `depth`
   arguments. Search and context carry `blast`; context text gets one `# blast` line per
   root. The CLI keeps `oxide impact` as the detailed exploration tool and prints the
   summaries under `oxide search` and `oxide context`.
5. **Versions.** `SCHEMA_VERSION` becomes `oxide-ladybug-py-v5`, and `storage_components`
   gains `blast`, whose value includes `NAVIGATION_VERSION`, so any change to the walk changes
   the derivation id. Existing indexes raise `incompatible_index` ("re-index"). They are not
   migrated (SPEC § Compatibility), so users run `oxide index` once.

## Evidence required before Accepted

The gate is the 2026-11-11 gate, unchanged: G1 navigation usefulness, G2 payload and dev
scores identical to HEAD, G3 latency (search and context, cold and warm, each ≤ +15%), and
G4 token overhead. Index-time cost is reported, not gated, because the first build of each
generation pays it once. A failure reverts the code and records the verdict.

## Consequences

- **Costs:**
  - One walk per entity during each publish. Its measured cost is in `docs/decisions.md`.
  - A `Blast` table in the store, one row per entity.
  - Re-index required after upgrading (the schema changes).
- **Risks:**
  - The index-time walk could be slow on large repositories with high-degree nodes; the
    per-walk bounds (depth, limit, edge allowance) cap it, but the total is O(entities).
  - A stored value and `Repository.impact` could disagree if the in-memory view drifts from
    `View`; a test compares them on every entity of a fixture.
- **Rejected:**
  - Walk per query (v1, v2 above): fails G3.
  - Cache per query keyed by generation: adds invalidation state for no gain over storing the
    row at publish.
  - Columns on `Entity`: every entity read would carry blast data.

"""Bounded impact and dependency navigation over typed relations (SPEC § Relations).

``upstream`` answers "what depends on this": callers, referrers and importers (incoming
``calls``/``references``/``imports``) and the tests that exercise it (outgoing
``tested_by``). ``downstream`` answers "what does this depend on" (outgoing ``calls``/
``references``/``imports``). The root stands for itself and everything it physically
contains (a class's methods, a file's declarations) and, for a file, the modules that
logically contain it, since imports name modules.

Level-synchronous BFS in domain order with a visited set, so cycles terminate and
results do not depend on store row order. It runs twice: over every followed edge, and
over proven edges only (``resolved`` with a non-heuristic basis), so ambiguous
candidates and the ``tested_by`` heuristic never make a path proven. Reached entities
in a dependency cycle with another reached entity are flagged (strongly connected
components of the reached subgraph). Bounds fire visibly.

The reached subgraph is kept as a NetworkX projection (ADR-0012): ``Walk.graph`` holds
every walked edge in traversal direction, with the ``via`` of its first step in domain
order, as bounded as the walk
itself; ``Walk.stopped_by`` says whether it is complete. NetworkX is imported lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Literal

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import networkx as nx

    from oxide.storage.ladybug import Adjacent, View

NAVIGATION_VERSION = "oxide-impact-bfs-v2"
MAX_EDGES = 20_000  # adjacency rows examined per pass
Direction = Literal["upstream", "downstream"]
_CROSS = ("calls", "references", "imports")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Hop:
    key: str
    depth: int
    proven_depth: int | None
    via: str  # "<kind>:<in|out>:<key reached from>" on a first shallowest path
    cyclic: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Walk:
    roots: tuple[str, ...]
    hops: tuple[Hop, ...]
    stopped_by: str | None  # "depth", "limit" or "edges"; None when exhausted
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str]  # the walked edges, traversal direction, edge attr ``via``


def _steps(
    direction: Direction, key: str, out: Adjacent, into: Adjacent, proven_only: bool
) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """(neighbor, via) of one entity, in domain order."""
    if direction == "upstream":
        found = [(a, f"{kind}:in:{key}", p) for kind, a, p, _ in into if kind in _CROSS]
        found += [(b, f"tested_by:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind == "tested_by"]
    else:
        found = [(b, f"{kind}:out:{key}", p) for kind, b, p, _ in out if kind in _CROSS]
    return sorted({(n, via) for n, via, p in found if p or not proven_only})


def _roots(view: View, key: str) -> list[str]:
    """``key``, its physical descendants and, for a file, its logical modules."""
    roots, layer = [key], [key]
    while layer:
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, kinds=("contains",))
        layer = sorted({b for k in layer for kind, b, *_ in adjacency[k][0] if kind == "contains"})
        roots += layer
    if key.startswith("file:"):
        into = view.adjacency([key], kinds=("contains_logical",))[key][1]
        roots += sorted(a for kind, a, *_ in into if kind == "contains_logical")
    return list(dict.fromkeys(roots))


def _bfs(
    view: View, roots: list[str], direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int, proven_only: bool
) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, str]], nx.DiGraph[str], str | None]:
    import networkx as nx

    seen = set(roots)
    found: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {}
    graph: nx.DiGraph[str] = nx.DiGraph()
    layer, examined, level = roots, 0, 0
    while layer:
        # Keys the allowance cut are absent, so a pass never reads past its edge budget.
        adjacency = view.adjacency(layer, MAX_EDGES - examined + 1)
        steps = {k: _steps(direction, k, *adjacency[k], proven_only) for k in adjacency}
        if level == depth:
            beyond = any(n not in seen for k in steps for n, _ in steps[k])
            return found, graph, "depth" if beyond else "edges" if len(steps) < len(layer) else None
        level += 1
        upcoming: list[str] = []
        for source in layer:
            if source not in adjacency:
                return found, graph, "edges"
            examined += sum(map(len, adjacency[source]))
            for neighbor, via in steps[source]:
                if not graph.has_edge(source, neighbor):  # keep the first step's ``via``
                    graph.add_edge(source, neighbor, via=via)
                if neighbor in seen:
                    continue
                if len(found) >= limit:
                    return found, graph, "limit"
                seen.add(neighbor)
                found[neighbor] = (level, via)
                upcoming.append(neighbor)
            if examined > MAX_EDGES:
                return found, graph, "edges"
        layer = upcoming
    return found, graph, None


def walk(view: View, key: str, direction: Direction, depth: int, limit: int) -> Walk:
    import networkx as nx

    roots = _roots(view, key)
    found, graph, stopped_by = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, False)
    proven, _, _ = _bfs(view, roots, direction, depth, limit, True)
    cyclic = {k for c in nx.strongly_connected_components(graph) if len(c) > 1 for k in c}
    hops = tuple(
        Hop(k, d, proven[k][0] if k in proven else None, via, k in cyclic)
        for k, (d, via) in sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[1][0], item[0]))
    )
    return Walk(tuple(roots), hops, stopped_by, graph)

from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError
from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations
from pydantic import Field, TypeAdapter

from oxide.api import MAX_DEPTH, Repository, open_repository
from oxide.models import ContextBundle, Impact, OxideError, SearchResult, advice

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Output bounds: entries per search, and units per bundle (api.MAX_BUDGET is far larger).
MAX_RESULTS = 100
MAX_BUDGET = 32_768
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2048
DEFAULT_IMPACT = 25
DEFAULT_DEPTH = 3
LOOPBACK = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")

# shortcut: one lock serializes calls across all repositories; use per-store locks if
# multi-repository throughput ever matters.
_lock = threading.Lock()

Repo = Annotated[
    str | None,
    Field(
        description="Repository root path. Optional when the server serves exactly one "
        "repository (`oxide mcp --repo PATH`).",
        max_length=4096,
    ),
]
Query = Annotated[
    str, Field(description="What you are looking for, in words or identifiers.", max_length=2000)
]
Hint = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=1024)]
Paths = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Repository-relative file paths to seed from.", max_length=32),
]
Symbols = Annotated[
    tuple[Hint, ...],
    Field(description="Symbol names or dotted suffixes (`Class.method`).", max_length=32),
]
Mode = Annotated[
    Literal["search", "context", "impact"],
    Field(
        description="search: ranked locations, never source (default). context: a source "
        "bundle within `budget`. impact: what depends on the entity `key`."
    ),
]
Key = Annotated[
    str,
    Field(
        max_length=1024,
        description="impact: entity key from a mode=search entry, e.g. `symbol:pkg/core.py#low`.",
    ),
]
Direction = Annotated[
    Literal["upstream", "downstream"],
    Field(
        description="upstream: what depends on the entity (callers, importers, tests). "
        "downstream: what the entity depends on."
    ),
]
READ_ONLY = ToolAnnotations(read_only_hint=True, open_world_hint=False)


def _resolver(repos: Sequence[str]) -> Callable[[str | None], str]:
    served = sorted({os.path.realpath(r) for r in repos})

    def resolve(repository: str | None) -> str:
        if repository is None:
            if len(served) == 1:
                return served[0]
            raise ToolError(
                "`repository` is required" + (f"; served: {', '.join(served)}" if served else "")
            )
        if served and os.path.realpath(repository) not in served:
            raise ToolError(f"{repository!r} is not served; served: {', '.join(served)}")
        return repository

    return resolve


def _read[T](
    repository: str,
    data_dir: str | None,
    read: Callable[[Repository], T],
    handles: dict[str, Repository],
) -> T:
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""

        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)

def _read[T](
…
    """Retain one handle per root until shutdown; evict failed handles for explicit repair."""
    with _lock:
        anyio.from_thread.check_cancelled()
        key = os.path.realpath(repository)
        try:
            try:
                if key not in handles:
                    handles[key] = open_repository(key, data_dir=data_dir, create=False)
                return read(handles[key])
            except BaseException:
                if repo := handles.pop(key, None):
                    repo.close()
                raise
        except OxideError as error:
            log.warning("%s: %s", error.code, error)
            detail = (
                str(error)
                if error.code == "invalid_argument"
                else advice(error, repository, private_data_dir=data_dir is not None)
            )
            raise ToolError(f"error[{error.code}]: {detail or 'request failed'}") from None


def _invalid(message: str) -> ToolError:
    return ToolError(f"error[invalid_argument]: {message}")


def server(repos: Sequence[str] = (), data_dir: str | None = None) -> FastMCP:
    """The MCP server; non-empty ``repos`` restricts which repositories calls may name.

    One tool, ``oxide_search``, whose ``mode`` picks one API operation: ``search``
    (``Repository.search``), ``context`` (``build_context``) or ``impact``
    (``Repository.impact``). Structural search stays a Python API: an agent trial found no
    benefit over grep (docs/decisions.md, structural-mcp-trial).
    """
    resolve = _resolver(repos)
    handles: dict[str, Repository] = {}

    def close_handles() -> None:
        with _lock:
            for repo in handles.values():
                repo.close()
            handles.clear()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(app: FastMCP) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(close_handles)

    app = FastMCP(
        "oxide",
        instructions="Structural code context for an indexed repository (`oxide index` "
        "builds the initial index; local tracking keeps it fresh). oxide_search finds what "
        "is defined (mode=search), builds a budgeted bundle of the relevant source with "
        "provenance (mode=context), or lists what depends on an entity (mode=impact).",
        # Unexpected exceptions reach the client as a generic message, never their text.
        mask_error_details=True,
        lifespan=lifespan,
    )
    results = TypeAdapter(SearchResult | ContextBundle | Impact).json_schema()
    output = {"type": "object", **results}

    @app.tool(annotations=READ_ONLY, output_schema=output)
    def oxide_search(
        query: Query | None = None,
        repository: Repo = None,
        mode: Mode = "search",
        limit: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_RESULTS,
                description=f"search: lexical hits (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT}). impact: entities "
                f"returned (default {DEFAULT_IMPACT}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        budget: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_BUDGET,
                description=f"context: size in oxide-units-v1 (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
        paths: Paths = (),
        symbols: Symbols = (),
        key: Key | None = None,
        direction: Direction | None = None,
        depth: Annotated[
            int | None,
            Field(
                ge=0,
                le=MAX_DEPTH,
                description=f"impact: hops to follow (default {DEFAULT_DEPTH}).",
            ),
        ] = None,
    ) -> ToolResult:
        """Search an indexed repository. mode=search (default) finds candidate symbols,
        files and modules: hint seeds first, then BM25 rank; locations (path, byte range,
        digest) and symbol metadata, never source text. mode=context builds a bounded,
        source-backed bundle: relevant declarations and their enclosing headers, each
        under a `### path:first-last` heading, within `budget` units; the structured
        result adds omissions, routing, degradations and the snapshot. `paths` and
        `symbols` are hints that seed both. mode=impact lists what depends on the entity
        `key` from a mode=search entry: upstream (default) callers, importers and tests, or
        downstream what it calls. Hops come nearest first with their proven depth;
        `stopped_by` names the bound that cut the walk; `unresolved` counts same-name call
        sites OXIDE could not resolve, so dependents may be missing. Locations, never source.
        `query` is required for search and context; `key` for impact. Not needed to find
        where one name is defined: use mode=search."""
        target = resolve(repository)
        if mode == "impact":
            for name, given in (("query", query), ("budget", budget)):
                if given is not None:
                    raise _invalid(f"`{name}` does not apply to mode=impact")
            if paths or symbols:
                raise _invalid("`paths` and `symbols` do not apply to mode=impact")
            if not key:
                raise _invalid("mode=impact needs `key`, an entity key from a mode=search entry")
            entity = key
            walk = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.impact(
                    entity,
                    direction=direction or "upstream",
                    depth=DEFAULT_DEPTH if depth is None else depth,
                    limit=DEFAULT_IMPACT if limit is None else limit,
                ),
                handles,
            )
            value = {"hops_returned": len(walk.hops)} | dataclasses.asdict(walk)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if key is not None or direction is not None or depth is not None:
            raise _invalid("`key`, `direction` and `depth` apply to mode=impact only")
        if query is None:
            raise _invalid("`query` is required for mode=search and mode=context")
        words = query
        if mode == "search":
            if budget is not None:
                raise _invalid("`budget` applies to mode=context only")
            count = DEFAULT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
            found = _read(
                target,
                data_dir,
                lambda repo: repo.search(words, limit=count, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
                handles,
            )
            # The status leads: clients that clip the tail (OpenCode code mode) keep it
            # (docs/phase-6/output-integrity/ at 013e791).
            more = found.lexical.truncated or any(h.issue == "truncated" for h in found.hints)
            value = {"entries_returned": len(found.entries), "more_available": more}
            value |= dataclasses.asdict(found)
            text = json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
            return ToolResult(content=text, structured_content=value)
        if limit is not None:
            raise _invalid("`limit` applies to mode=search and mode=impact only")
        size = DEFAULT_BUDGET if budget is None else budget
        bundle = _read(
            target,
            data_dir,
            lambda repo: repo.build_context(words, size, paths=paths, symbols=symbols),
            handles,
        )
        head = (
            f"# oxide context: {bundle.used}/{bundle.budget} {bundle.units}, "
            f"{len(bundle.items)} items, {len(bundle.omissions)} omitted, "
            f"snapshot {bundle.snapshot.snapshot_id}\n"
        )
        if "judge" in bundle.versions:  # this repository's source went to the judge
            head += f"# judged by {bundle.versions['judge']}\n"
        head += "".join(f"# degraded: {d}\n" for d in bundle.degradations)
        head += "".join(f"# hint {h.kind} {h.hint}: {h.issue}\n" for h in bundle.hints)
        # The model reads the payload as text; applications get the whole bundle.
        return ToolResult(
            content=head + bundle.payload, structured_content=dataclasses.asdict(bundle)
        )

    return app


def serve(repos: Sequence[str], data_dir: str | None, http: bool, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    """Runs until stdin closes (stdio) or the process is interrupted (HTTP)."""
    app = server(repos, data_dir)
    if not http:
        app.run(show_banner=False)
        return
    if host not in LOOPBACK:
        # Unauthenticated: never listen beyond this machine.
        raise ValueError(f"--host must be one of {', '.join(LOOPBACK)}")
    app.run(
        transport="http",
        host=host,
        port=port,
        stateless_http=True,
        host_origin_protection=True,
        show_banner=False,
    )
