# ADR-0014: Precomputed blast radius in search and context results

## Status

**Accepted**, 2026-11-11. The predeclared gate (G1–G4, `docs/decisions.md` row 53) passed,
and the owner accepted the validation items below. The measured costs are optimization debt,
listed in their own section, not open questions. This ADR changes the 2026-11-10
`oxide_search` `mode=impact` implementation recorded in
[ADR-0013](0013-graph-navigation-in-oxide-search.md); ADR-0013's own status is not changed.

## Context

The 2026-11-11 design put the blast radius into `search` and `context`, computed by a walk
per query (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`). Both
variants failed the predeclared latency gate (G3), recorded in `docs/decisions.md`:

| Variant | Warm search, fixture / requests | Warm context, fixture / requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1: walk through `navigation.walk` (networkx) | 2.12 → 15.75 ms (+643%) / 2.43 → 20.97 ms (+764%) | +129% / +65% |
| v2: reuse `navigation.reach` (edges only) | 2.12 → 15.01 ms (+608%) / 2.43 → 18.50 ms (+662%) | +101% / +53% |

Each entry point needs a depth-2 walk of database queries, which costs milliseconds per
query, and no reuse of the walk code removes that cost. The information is worth the
latency only if an agent reads it, not walks it for every query.

## Decision

1. **Store one blast radius per entity, on its `Entity` row.** Six columns
   (`blast_dependents`, `blast_tests`, `blast_file_count`, `blast_files`,
   `blast_unresolved`, `blast_stopped_by`) hold the bounded upstream walk of
   `Repository.impact` (depth 2, limit 20): reached entities, those that are tests, distinct
   source paths (the first 8 listed, in `blast_files` as JSON), same-name unresolved call
   sites, and the bound that stopped the walk. The generation seals them, so they cannot be
   stale.
2. **Compute it with the same walk.** `core/blast.py` runs `navigation.walk` over an
   in-memory view of the generation's relations. That view mirrors `View.adjacency` and
   `View.mentions`, including the edge allowance, so the stored value equals what
   `Repository.impact` returns for the same entity. `navigation.walk` depends on a protocol
   with one method, `adjacency`, which both the read view and the in-memory view provide.
   The unresolved-site lookup is indexed by name tail, not a scan.
3. **Read, don't walk, in the query that already runs.** `View.entries(keys)` returns each
   entity with its blast radius from the same Cypher query as `View.entities`.
   `search` and `build_context` use it for their entries, and the first `BLAST_ROOTS = 3`
   entries carry `blast`. Ranking, routing and packing do not change, so the payload is
   unchanged.
4. **MCP.** `oxide_search` drops `mode="impact"` and its `key`, `direction` and `depth`
   arguments. Search and context carry `blast`; context text gets one `# blast` line per
   root. The CLI keeps `oxide impact` as the detailed exploration tool and prints the
   summaries under `oxide search` and `oxide context`.
5. **Versions.** `SCHEMA_VERSION` becomes `oxide-ladybug-py-v5`, and `storage_components`
   gains `blast`, whose value includes `NAVIGATION_VERSION`, so any change to the walk changes
   the derivation id. Existing indexes raise `incompatible_index` ("re-index"). They are not
   migrated (SPEC § Compatibility), so users run `oxide index` once.

## Validation (2026-11-11)

**Navigation is not payload recall.** On the ContextBench dev split (15 tasks), the scored
1024-unit payload is byte-identical with and without blast (payload hashes equal on all 15
tasks), so payload recall is unchanged: 0.711 both ways. The G1 gain (0.711 → 0.800) counts
gold files that the blast radius names. An agent sees those files only in the `blast` field
or the `# blast` text line, never in the scored payload. Three gold files, in three tasks
(`psf__requests-2317`, `-5414`, `-2931`), appear only through blast. The blast radius also
names 1.07 non-gold files per task. The same 0.800 holds on the context surface
(`bundle.blast`). Whether agents act on those lines is not measured.

**Large repository.** `ansible` (1,720 Python files, 15,735 entities; no ContextBench tasks,
so neither dev nor held-out) on this machine, 200% CPU and 3 GiB, 5 paired rounds:

| Measure | HEAD | With blast | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index, median | 3.42 s | 4.72 s | +38% (blast walk 1.2 s of it) |
| Peak RSS after index | 382–386 MiB | 346–353 MiB | not higher |
| Storage after index | 49.45 MB | 49.96 MB | +1.0% |
| Search, cold / warm | 8.2 / 7.0 ms | 9.4 / 8.1 ms | +14.5% / +15.5% (later sessions, warm: +5.5% and +8.5%) |
| Context, cold / warm | 90 / 85 ms | 90 / 84 ms | flat |
| Reopen | 148 ms | 148 ms | flat |

- Blast compute peak 31 MB on the Python heap, 2.6 MB retained after publish.
- Stored value equals the live `Repository.impact` walk for every entity whose walk
  succeeds: 15,502 entities, 0 mismatches.
- An index-time regression was found and fixed without changing output. The unresolved-site
  lookup scanned every unresolved edge per entity (33 s of the 35 s blast compute on ansible;
  cold index 3.6 s → 38.6 s). It is now indexed by name tail and equal to the scan on all
  15,735 calls.
- Read-path encodings measured and rejected: one JSON cell for all six fields (no gain,
  +0.45 MB storage); a second query for the three reporting keys (search +21% to +29%);
  `CASE` projection of the blast cells only for reporting keys (no gain).
- Gate G3 (predeclared, fixture and requests) passes on the medians recorded in
  `docs/decisions.md`. Ansible is outside the gate; its numbers are above.

## Optimization debt

Accepted with these measured costs. Each has a known direction; none is a correctness issue.

| Cost | Measured | Direction not yet taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index | +38% on ansible (1.2 s of walk per 15.7k entities); +6% on requests, +1% on fixture | Recompute the walk only for entities whose upstream changed (delta publish); bound the cost of hub nodes (the single `repo` walk takes 161 ms) |
| Warm search on large repositories | +6% to +16% on ansible (cold +14.5%) | A read path that does not widen the entity query. The three alternatives measured were all worse or no better |
| Storage | +1.0% on ansible | Fewer or narrower blast fields per row |
| Memory | Not higher on ansible; blast heap peak 31 MB, 2.6 MB retained | Stream the in-memory relations if the peak grows with repository size |

The repeated-`impact` read-pool exhaustion is a separate defect, present on `main` before this
change, and is tracked in [issue #55](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/issues/55). It is not a
cost of this ADR: search and context do not walk at query time, but `oxide impact` and
`Repository.impact` are affected on large repositories.

## Acceptance evidence

The gate is the 2026-11-11 gate, unchanged: G1 navigation usefulness, G2 payload and dev
scores identical to HEAD, G3 latency (search and context, cold and warm, each ≤ +15%), and
G4 token overhead. Index-time cost is reported, not gated. The gate passed (row 53); the
validation above is the evidence for the trade-offs; the owner accepted them on 2026-11-11.

The derivation id changed from `sha256:ff500e5a…` to `sha256:daa271b3…`. The only changed
components are `storage-schema` (v4 → v5) and the new `blast` component. Compatibility of the
frozen contextbench outputs is unchanged: the per-task compatibility fields match the frozen
results. Only the pin was updated, as recorded in `docs/decisions.md` row 54.

## Consequences

- **Costs:**
  - One walk per entity during each publish: 1.2–1.3 s on a 15.7k-entity repository.
  - Six more columns on every `Entity` row (+1.0% storage on ansible); re-index required
    after upgrading.
  - Search reads six more columns per candidate row: +6% to +16% warm on ansible.
- **Risks:**
  - The index-time walk is O(entities) times the bounded walk. Its measured p99 is 0.5 ms
    per entity and the largest single walk 161 ms (`repo`), so high-degree nodes are bounded
    in practice but not in principle.
  - A stored value and `Repository.impact` could disagree if the in-memory view drifts from
    `View`; a test compares them on every entity of a fixture, and the same comparison passed
    on every ansible entity whose walk succeeds.
- **Rejected:**
  - Walk per query (v1, v2 above): fails G3.
  - A separate `Blast` node table read with its own query: a second Cypher execute per call
    cost +26% to +57% on warm fixture search (`micro2`, harness queries), so the blast
    columns moved onto the entity row and the read was merged.
  - A second query for the reporting keys only (search +21% to +29% on ansible).
  - One JSON cell instead of six columns: no measured gain, +0.45 MB storage.
  - Cache per query keyed by generation: adds invalidation state for no gain over storing the
    row at publish.

# ADR-0014: Precomputed blast radius in search and context results

## Status

**Accepted**, 2026-11-11. The predeclared gate (G1–G4, `docs/decisions.md` row 53) passed,
and the owner accepted the validation items below. The measured costs are optimization debt,
listed in their own section, not open questions. This ADR changes the 2026-11-10
`oxide_search` `mode=impact` implementation recorded in
[ADR-0013](0013-graph-navigation-in-oxide-search.md); ADR-0013's own status is not changed.

## Context

The 2026-11-11 design put the blast radius into `search` and `context`, computed by a walk
per query (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md`). Both
variants failed the predeclared latency gate (G3), recorded in `docs/decisions.md`:

| Variant | Warm search, fixture / requests | Warm context, fixture / requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1: walk through `navigation.walk` (networkx) | 2.12 → 15.75 ms (+643%) / 2.43 → 20.97 ms (+764%) | +129% / +65% |
| v2: reuse `navigation.reach` (edges only) | 2.12 → 15.01 ms (+608%) / 2.43 → 18.50 ms (+662%) | +101% / +53% |

Each entry point needs a depth-2 walk of database queries, which costs milliseconds per
query, and no reuse of the walk code removes that cost. The information is worth the
latency only if an agent reads it, not walks it for every query.

## Decision

1. **Store one blast radius per entity, on its `Entity` row.** Six columns
   (`blast_dependents`, `blast_tests`, `blast_file_count`, `blast_files`,
   `blast_unresolved`, `blast_stopped_by`) hold the bounded upstream walk of
   `Repository.impact` (depth 2, limit 20): reached entities, those that are tests, distinct
   source paths (the first 8 listed, in `blast_files` as JSON), same-name unresolved call
   sites, and the bound that stopped the walk. The generation seals them, so they cannot be
   stale.
2. **Compute it with the same walk.** `core/blast.py` runs `navigation.walk` over an
   in-memory view of the generation's relations. That view mirrors `View.adjacency` and
   `View.mentions`, including the edge allowance, so the stored value equals what
   `Repository.impact` returns for the same entity. `navigation.walk` depends on a protocol
   with one method, `adjacency`, which both the read view and the in-memory view provide.
   The unresolved-site lookup is indexed by name tail, not a scan.
3. **Read, don't walk, in the query that already runs.** `View.entries(keys)` returns each
   entity with its blast radius from the same Cypher query as `View.entities`.
   `search` and `build_context` use it for their entries, and the first `BLAST_ROOTS = 3`
   entries carry `blast`. Ranking, routing and packing do not change, so the payload is
   unchanged.
4. **MCP.** `oxide_search` drops `mode="impact"` and its `key`, `direction` and `depth`
   arguments. Search and context carry `blast`; context text gets one `# blast` line per
   root. The CLI keeps `oxide impact` as the detailed exploration tool and prints the
   summaries under `oxide search` and `oxide context`.
5. **Versions.** `SCHEMA_VERSION` becomes `oxide-ladybug-py-v5`, and `storage_components`
   gains `blast`, whose value includes `NAVIGATION_VERSION`, so any change to the walk changes
   the derivation id. Existing indexes raise `incompatible_index` ("re-index"). They are not
   migrated (SPEC § Compatibility), so users run `oxide index` once.

## Validation (2026-11-11)

**Navigation is not payload recall.** On the ContextBench dev split (15 tasks), the scored
1024-unit payload is byte-identical with and without blast (payload hashes equal on all 15
tasks), so payload recall is unchanged: 0.711 both ways. The G1 gain (0.711 → 0.800) counts
gold files that the blast radius names. An agent sees those files only in the `blast` field
or the `# blast` text line, never in the scored payload. Three gold files, in three tasks
(`psf__requests-2317`, `-5414`, `-2931`), appear only through blast. The blast radius also
names 1.07 non-gold files per task. The same 0.800 holds on the context surface
(`bundle.blast`). Whether agents act on those lines is not measured.

**Large repository.** `ansible` (1,720 Python files, 15,735 entities; no ContextBench tasks,
so neither dev nor held-out) on this machine, 200% CPU and 3 GiB, 5 paired rounds:

| Measure | HEAD | With blast | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index, median | 3.42 s | 4.72 s | +38% (blast walk 1.2 s of it) |
| Peak RSS after index | 382–386 MiB | 346–353 MiB | not higher |
| Storage after index | 49.45 MB | 49.96 MB | +1.0% |
| Search, cold / warm | 8.2 / 7.0 ms | 9.4 / 8.1 ms | +14.5% / +15.5% (later sessions, warm: +5.5% and +8.5%) |
| Context, cold / warm | 90 / 85 ms | 90 / 84 ms | flat |
| Reopen | 148 ms | 148 ms | flat |

- Blast compute peak 31 MB on the Python heap, 2.6 MB retained after publish.
- Stored value equals the live `Repository.impact` walk for every entity whose walk
  succeeds: 15,502 entities, 0 mismatches.
- An index-time regression was found and fixed without changing output. The unresolved-site
  lookup scanned every unresolved edge per entity (33 s of the 35 s blast compute on ansible;
  cold index 3.6 s → 38.6 s). It is now indexed by name tail and equal to the scan on all
  15,735 calls.
- Read-path encodings measured and rejected: one JSON cell for all six fields (no gain,
  +0.45 MB storage); a second query for the three reporting keys (search +21% to +29%);
  `CASE` projection of the blast cells only for reporting keys (no gain).
- Gate G3 (predeclared, fixture and requests) passes on the medians recorded in
  `docs/decisions.md`. Ansible is outside the gate; its numbers are above.

## Optimization debt

Accepted with these measured costs. Each has a known direction; none is a correctness issue.

| Cost | Measured | Direction not yet taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold index | +38% on ansible (1.2 s of walk per 15.7k entities); +6% on requests, +1% on fixture | Recompute the walk only for entities whose upstream changed (delta publish); bound the cost of hub nodes (the single `repo` walk takes 161 ms) |
| Warm search on large repositories | +6% to +16% on ansible (cold +14.5%) | A read path that does not widen the entity query. The three alternatives measured were all worse or no better |
| Storage | +1.0% on ansible | Fewer or narrower blast fields per row |
| Memory | Not higher on ansible; blast heap peak 31 MB, 2.6 MB retained | Stream the in-memory relations if the peak grows with repository size |

The repeated-`impact` read-pool exhaustion is a separate defect, present on `main` before this
change, and is tracked in [issue #55](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/issues/55). It is not a
cost of this ADR: search and context do not walk at query time, but `oxide impact` and
`Repository.impact` are affected on large repositories.

## Acceptance evidence

The gate is the 2026-11-11 gate, unchanged: G1 navigation usefulness, G2 payload and dev
scores identical to HEAD, G3 latency (search and context, cold and warm, each ≤ +15%), and
G4 token overhead. Index-time cost is reported, not gated. The gate passed (row 53); the
validation above is the evidence for the trade-offs; the owner accepted them on 2026-11-11.

The derivation id changed from `sha256:ff500e5a…` to `sha256:daa271b3…`. The only changed
components are `storage-schema` (v4 → v5) and the new `blast` component. Compatibility of the
frozen contextbench outputs is unchanged: the per-task compatibility fields match the frozen
results. Only the pin was updated, as recorded in `docs/decisions.md` row 54.

## Consequences

- **Costs:**
  - One walk per entity during each publish: 1.2–1.3 s on a 15.7k-entity repository.
  - Six more columns on every `Entity` row (+1.0% storage on ansible); re-index required
    after upgrading.
  - Search reads six more columns per candidate row: +6% to +16% warm on ansible.
- **Risks:**
  - The index-time walk is O(entities) times the bounded walk. Its measured p99 is 0.5 ms
    per entity and the largest single walk 161 ms (`repo`), so high-degree nodes are bounded
    in practice but not in principle.
  - A stored value and `Repository.impact` could disagree if the in-memory view drifts from
    `View`; a test compares them on every entity of a fixture, and the same comparison passed
    on every ansible entity whose walk succeeds.
- **Rejected:**
  - Walk per query (v1, v2 above): fails G3.
  - A separate `Blast` node table read with its own query: a second Cypher execute per call
    cost +26% to +57% on warm fixture search (`micro2`, harness queries), so the blast
    columns moved onto the entity row and the read was merged.
  - A second query for the reporting keys only (search +21% to +29% on ansible).
  - One JSON cell instead of six columns: no measured gain, +0.45 MB storage.
  - Cache per query keyed by generation: adds invalidation state for no gain over storing the
    row at publish.

# Decisions

The standing architectural decisions of OXIDE v2 and the research verdicts that constrain
them. [SPEC](spec/SPEC.md) is the architecture authority and the [ADRs](adr/) record
individual decisions; this file never changes an ADR's status, and a Proposed ADR is not a
requirement. The evaluation protocol is in [`fixtures/eval/`](../fixtures/eval/README.md).

Reports, harnesses and raw results behind every verdict are frozen at
[`013e791`](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs)
(`docs/phase-6/<study>/`, `docs/BOOTSTRAP.md`, `docs/migration-audit/`). The v1
implementation is pinned at `ac985b28`, the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime at `f79808a`.

## Standing rules

1. One Python package, `oxide` (ADR-0011). A new package or dependency needs a reuse, packaging or API reason.
2. Legacy v1 (`ac985b28`) is evidence, not a template. Reusing it requires a stated SPEC requirement, a boundary-fit reason and tests. No legacy SQLite schemas, row IDs, migrations or cache locations; derived state is rebuildable from captured source.
3. Repository intelligence lives in `oxide.core`, I/O in `oxide.capture` and `oxide.storage`. LadybugDB objects, native IDs, rows and Cypher stay inside `oxide.storage`; the API exposes only domain values. Integrations (the CLI, `oxide mcp`, editors) are clients of `oxide.api` and never parse, route or select.
4. When SPEC and code disagree, SPEC wins. If SPEC is ambiguous, record the ambiguity and a proposal; don't invent permanent ID, schema, transport or model policy to unblock scaffolding.
5. Vectorless: no embeddings, vector indexes or model runners. Lexical entry points, TreeRouter, the heuristic value and the packer need no model or network.
6. Models judge; deterministic code decides thresholds, traversal, stopping, inclusion, budget, fallback and packing. A `DecisionProvider` seam behind `oxide.core.packing.value` carries abstention and a deterministic fallback; JEV and every learned judge stay optional, and CI never runs a live judge.
7. Structure comes before similarity: retrieval finds entry points, routing finds context, and the TreeIndex keeps cross-edges.
8. Native libraries (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX, hashing) do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy.
9. Never execute repository code or build hooks while indexing. Respect repository scope and source privacy.
10. Frozen baselines keep their provenance. Never regenerate gold or erase a negative result to make a challenger pass; promoting a quality change to a default needs gate evidence.

Each row is closed; its report is under `docs/phase-6/<study>/` at the pin above.

| Graph ranking (`graph-v1`..`v3`) | Resolution raised routed coverage 0.673 → 0.730. REJECT PPR + communities, dispatch routing and the order tiebreak; the loss after routing comes from budget allocation and the relevance signal. |
| Graph navigation (`graph-navigation`, `-v2`, `networkx-v1`) | Basis for ADR-0012 and ADR-0013 (both Proposed). |
| Agent-guided context (`agc`, `agc-v2`..`v4`) | v2 REJECT (adoption); v4 STOP at stage 1, so ADR-0013 stays Proposed without evidence. |
| Optional judges (`decision-study-v1`..`v3`, `jev-reliability`, `jev-order-m1`..`m3`) | v3 PASS (+0.159 at 4,096 units); reliability PASS only under immediate fallback. M3 and ADR-0009 NOT READY: JEV stays off. |
| Storage (`leann-graph-storage`, [`fts-footprint`](fts-footprint.md)) | REJECT compaction; DEFER the traversal memo. ACCEPT `auto_checkpoint=False`, exact wide top-k, blob fsync overlap with a 65,536-entry LRU. REJECT two query threads. |
| Output (`toon-serialization`, `outline-comparison`, `output-integrity`) | REJECT TOON and outlines. Output-integrity fixes shipped. |
| Retrieval (`path-hint-utility` and diagnostics) | PROMOTE path hints (`oxide-select-greedy-v4`): dev hinted `line_recall@4096` 0.685 → 0.785 (Python), 0.360 → 0.626 (TypeScript). REJECT source bodies; file localization NOT VIABLE; router reachability NEGATIVE. |

A `DecisionProvider` seam behind `oxide.core.packing.value` carries abstention and a deterministic fallback; JEV and every learned judge stay optional, and CI never runs a live judge.
7. Structure comes before similarity: retrieval finds entry points, routing finds context, and the TreeIndex keeps cross-edges.
8. Native libraries (tree-sitter, LadybugDB, NetworkX, hashing) do recursive and latency-sensitive work; Python holds bounded policy.
9. Never execute repository code or build hooks while indexing. Respect repository scope and source privacy.
10. Frozen baselines keep their provenance. Never regenerate gold or erase a negative result to make a challenger pass; promoting a quality change to a default needs gate evidence.

## Research verdicts

Each row is closed; its report is under `docs/phase-6/<study>/` at the pin above.

| Area | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Graph ranking (`graph-v1`..`v3`) | Resolution raised routed coverage 0.673 → 0.730. REJECT PPR + communities, dispatch routing and the order tiebreak; the loss after routing comes from budget allocation and the relevance signal. |
| Graph navigation (`graph-navigation`, `-v2`, `networkx-v1`) | Basis for ADR-0012 and ADR-0013 (both Proposed). |
| Agent-guided context (`agc`, `agc-v2`..`v4`) | v2 REJECT (adoption); v4 STOP at stage 1, so ADR-0013 stays Proposed without evidence. |
| Optional judges (`decision-study-v1`..`v3`, `jev-reliability`, `jev-order-m1`..`m3`) | v3 PASS (+0.159 at 4,096 units); reliability PASS only under immediate fallback. M3 and ADR-0009 NOT READY: JEV stays off. |
| Storage (`leann-graph-storage`, [`fts-footprint`](fts-footprint.md)) | REJECT compaction; DEFER the traversal memo. ACCEPT `auto_checkpoint=False`, exact wide top-k, blob fsync overlap with a 65,536-entry LRU. REJECT two query threads. |
| Output (`toon-serialization`, `outline-comparison`, `output-integrity`) | REJECT TOON and outlines. Output-integrity fixes shipped. |
| Retrieval (`path-hint-utility` and diagnostics) | PROMOTE path hints (`oxide-select-greedy-v4`): dev hinted `line_recall@4096` 0.685 → 0.785 (Python), 0.360 → 0.626 (TypeScript). REJECT source bodies; file localization NOT VIABLE; router reachability NEGATIVE. |
| Structure (`astgrep-feasibility`, `structural-mcp-trial`) | ast-grep feasible (94 MB, pinned). REJECT a structural MCP tool: grep F1 0.994 vs 0.978. |
| Indexing (`incremental-indexing`, `change-classification`) | Incremental indexing shipped; change classification NOT WORTH IT. |
| FTS distribution (`release-blockers`) | Upstream replaced the FTS 0.21.0 files, so OXIDE mirrors the original builds ([`fts-mirror/`](fts-mirror/RELEASE.md)). |
| Selection (`cover-selector`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT opt-in budgeted-coverage selector `oxide-select-cover-v0` vs `greedy-v4`: dev verified span_recall@1024 0.508→0.358, line 0.548→0.383; heldout span@1024 0.109→0.018; context warm +20%, RSS flat. Stays experimental, not the default. |
| Selection (`excerpt`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT opt-in body excerpts `oxide-select-excerpt-v0` (header + widest whole-line window that fits by exact rendered units, most query-term hits) vs `greedy-v4`: dev verified span_recall@1024 0.508→0.552, line@256 0.180→0.304, but file_recall@4096 0.900→0.833; heldout span@1024 0.109→0.079, file@1024 0.529→0.408 (excerpts spend budget other files' views used); context warm 47→109 ms, RSS flat. Gold: 217 spans = 185 verified + 32 unverified (dev 3, heldout 29); stage tables count verified only. |
| Indexing (`resolver-scope-index`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE: the Python resolver indexes each scope's child declarations by name and precomputes its star-import flag instead of scanning per lookup. Output identical (entities/relations equal, ContextBench gate exact). xarray@1757dff, `scripts/bench.py` 5 iterations under 200% CPU/3G: index_cold median 1.476→1.383 s (−6%); one-file re-index 0.933→0.823 s (−12%, resolution 0.33→0.22 s). |
| Packing (`adjacent-merge`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE `oxide-payload-v4`: same-file views separated only by whitespace share one item and heading (−4% of units on dev at every budget). Python dev verified span_recall@256 0.047→0.080, line@256 0.180→0.193; heldout within tolerance (span@4096 −0.009, file@4096 +0.020). TS heldout span@256 0.018→0.036, dev file_recall −0.010. Frozen as py baseline-v20, ts baseline-v17. Labelling only outermost nested symbols as well saved ~1% more units with no recall change: not kept. |
| Indexing (`delta-publish`, 2026-11-03) | REJECT publishing a re-index as a delta on a copy of the previous `graph.lbug` (xarray, one-def insert in `xarray/core/utils.py`; full publish 0.58 s of 0.83 s). The delta is small without edge ordinals (157 entities, 50 Rel, 93 Opaque rows), but `site` is a global ordinal, so 28,159 rows shift in 39 runs. Apply 0.58 s plus checkpoint 0.13 s = 0.95 s total, against a 0.52 s bulk load. Inexact: in-place FTS maintenance (ladybug 0.21) returned 1054 of 1065 hits for one query. Even with stable ordinals, FTS rebuild (0.20 s) and checkpoint (0.13–0.15 s) leave no gain. Other levers: Python resolution of unchanged files ≤0.17 s upper bound, needs exact dependency tracking through the closed-world dispatch; FTS/CSV pipelining ≤0.06 s. Both not pursued. |
| Indexing (`split-lexical`, 2026-11-03) | PROMOTE store schema `oxide-ladybug-py-v4`: the FTS documents and index live in a per-generation `lexical.lbug`, built on a side thread while the graph loads and hard-linked from the previous generation when the document digest is unchanged (the index is a function of the documents alone). Exact: ContextBench py (baseline-v21) and TS (baseline-v18) `results.json` identical to v20/v17 apart from the derivation id, metrics byte-identical. Speed (200% CPU cap): one-def re-index ansible 2.53→2.02 s (−20%), xarray 0.81→0.67 s (−17%); body-only edit ansible 2.52→1.91 s (−24%), xarray 0.81→0.66 s (−19%); TS cold index over 82 corpora 418→352 s (−16%). Cost: concurrent pools raise the VS Code cold-index peak RSS 1150→1347 MB (sampled, 2 runs); streaming the graph rows to CSV instead of holding lists brings it to 1268 MB (+10%), time unchanged, CSV bytes identical. CREATE_FTS_INDEX needs ~10 MiB of pool per MB of documents (VS Code 23.2 MB: 256 MiB fails, 270 MiB fits), so the lexical pool is `BUFFER_POOL + 10 × bytes`; at 2× all 14 VS Code corpora failed. In-place FTS patching was 5× faster than a rebuild but left one-ULP drift in multi-term BM25 sums: REJECT. |
| Indexing (`automatic-freshness`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE local in-process watching with incremental capture and full-content recovery. Predeclared gate: in a two-file fixture, unchanged capture reads 2→0 source files and one-file edits read 2→1; automatic updates equal full rebuilds. No retrieval policy change. `scripts/bench.py fixtures/py_repo --iterations 5 --warm 20`, Linux/Python 3.13.17, 200% CPU/3G, same 11 files / 65 entities / 196 relations: median cold index 340.26→354.04 ms, explicit unchanged index 8.04→7.88 ms, reopen 24.26→39.79 ms, warm search 2.04→3.15 ms, warm context 18.57→18.72 ms, peak RSS 188.13→184.06 MiB. Reopen now reconciles source; these are small-fixture overhead measurements, not an end-to-end speedup claim. |
| Indexing (`reconcile-keep-cache`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a periodic or failed-watcher reconcile re-walks the tree and lets the stat key choose which bytes to re-read, instead of clearing the capture cache; only an explicit `index()` rehashes. Healthy watchers reconcile every 300 s (was 30 s), failed ones poll every 30 s. Predeclared rule: reconcile ≥25% cheaper with an identical snapshot, standard bench within noise. Same-commit A/B of `_index(True)` (7 runs, status `unchanged`, snapshot equal, 200% CPU/3G, warm page cache): ansible 1540 files median 190→117 ms (−39%), xarray 135 files 19.6→13.6 ms (−31%). Standard bench `fixtures/py_repo --iterations 10 --warm 20` vs the parent commit, two interleaved runs: reopen 54.0/57.2→52.5/52.9 ms, warm search 4.6/4.5→4.5/4.5 ms, peak RSS 193/192→195/192 MiB; warm context is bimodal (≈19 or ≈38 ms) in both builds, so not attributable. Not measured: cold page cache (the saved reads cost more there) and the 10× rarer walk, which is arithmetic, not a run. Limit: an edit with the same size, mtime, inode and ctime after a missed event is caught only by explicit `index()`. |
| Indexing (`watcher-restart`, 2026-11-04) | PROMOTE: a failed watcher (overflow, watch limit) no longer degrades the repository to polling for life; the freshness thread retries `watch` after 30 s, doubling to 300 s, and forces one full walk once the new watcher is live, so events lost in the gap are recovered. Rule: a restarted watcher must resync and clear `failed`, with the healthy path unchanged (`test_failed_watcher_is_restarted_and_resynced`; 469 passed). Cost removed, measured on ansible (1540 files, 200% CPU/3G, median of 15 warm searches): healthy 7.4 ms, permanently degraded 73.3 ms (every read walks the tree). Not measured: a real inotify overflow (simulated by a raising `watch`), and cold page cache. |
| Blast radius in search and context (`blast-radius-in-search`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT automatic blast radius: `BlastRoot` for each of the first 3 entry points, upstream walk to depth 2 (≤20 entities, ≤8 listed files), predeclared in [the 2026-11-11 spec](superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-blast-radius-in-search-design.md). Dev split only (15 tasks; held-out not opened). G1 navigation PASS: bundle file recall@1024 0.711→0.800 with blast; 3 gold files surfaced only by blast; 1.07 surfaced files per task that are neither in the bundle nor gold. G2 PASS: 0/15 payloads and 0/15 full scorer outputs differ from HEAD. G4 PASS: MCP text search +6.2%, context +7.0%. G3 FAIL (`scripts/bench.py`, 5×20, 200% CPU/3G): warm search 2.12→15.75 ms on `fixtures/py_repo` (+643%), 2.43→20.97 ms on `psf__requests@22623bd8c265` (+764%); warm context 10.91→25.02 ms (+129%) and 33.39→55.24 ms (+65%); `index_cold` −3%. Cause: each root's upstream walk costs 2.2–8.7 ms (two BFS passes plus NetworkX), and a single pass alone is 0.8–5.8 ms per root, so no single-pass variant can meet the 15% search gate. Code reverted to HEAD; `oxide impact` and MCP `mode=impact` unchanged. Candidate patch and raw numbers: `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`. |
| Blast radius v2, reuse (`blast-radius-reuse`, 2026-11-11) | REJECT, same gate. Rewritten to reuse the followed-edge BFS (`navigation.reach`, no proven pass, no NetworkX graph) and existing `view` queries; `impact()` unchanged. Same semantics: dev G1 0.711→0.800, G2 0/15 diffs, G4 +6.2% search / +7.0% context text. G3 still FAILS: warm search 2.12→15.01 ms (+608%, `fixtures/py_repo`) and 2.43→18.50 ms (+662%, requests); warm context 10.91→21.92 ms (+101%) and 33.39→50.96 ms (+53%). Reuse saved about 0.7 ms per search: the per-root BFS is the cost, not the proven pass. Code reverted; patch and numbers in `~/.cache/oxide/experiments/blast-2026-11-11/`. |
| Blast radius, precomputed (`blast-precomputed`, 2026-11-11) | PASS the predeclared gate G1–G4; ADR-0014 is Accepted (row 54). Blast radius is stored per entity at publish (six `blast_*` columns on `Entity`, store schema `oxide-ladybug-py-v5`) and read in the entity query. `mode=impact` retired from MCP; `oxide impact` unchanged. Dev split only (15 tasks; held-out not used in the decision). G1 PASS, as a navigation surface, not payload recall: payload recall@1024 is 0.711 with and without blast (payloads identical, 0/15 diffs); files named by blast raise search and context surfaces to 0.800; 3 gold files (`requests-2317`, `-5414`, `-2931`) appear only through blast; 1.07 non-gold blast files per task. G2 PASS (0/15 payload and score diffs; only `versions.derivation` changes with the schema bump). G3 PASS on predeclared medians (5×20, 200% CPU/3G): fixture search cold −24%, warm −9%, context cold −4%, warm +2%; requests search cold +1%, warm +11%, context cold +2%, warm +1%; per-round spread about ±30%. G4 PASS: search text +6.2%, context text +7.0%. Re-index required. Pin updated: row 54. |
| Blast radius validation and acceptance (`blast-validation`, 2026-11-11) | ACCEPTED by the owner, 2026-11-11 (ADR-0014 Accepted); the measured trade-offs are listed as optimization debt in the ADR. (1) Index regression found and fixed without changing output: `Graph.mentions` scanned every unresolved edge per entity (ansible: 33.3 of 34.8 s blast compute; cold index 3.6 → 38.6 s). Now indexed by name tail; equal to the scan on all 15,735 calls. Ansible (1,720 Python files, 15,735 entities, 5 paired rounds): cold index 3.42 → 4.72 s (+38%; walk 1.2 s), peak RSS 382–386 → 346–353 MiB (not higher), storage 49.45 → 49.96 MB (+1.0%), blast heap peak 31 MB, 2.6 MB retained. (2) Query latency on ansible: search cold +14.5%, warm +15.5% (later sessions warm +5.5%, +8.5%); context cold +0.1%, warm −1.0%; reopen +0.3%. Rejected on measurement: one JSON cell (no gain, +0.45 MB), second query for reporting keys (search +21% to +29%), `CASE` projection (no gain). (3) Stored value equals live `Repository.impact` for 15,502 entities whose walk succeeds, 0 mismatches. (4) Pre-existing, not caused by this change (HEAD identical): `Repository.impact` raises `store_corrupt` on 233 of 15,735 ansible entities after many walks on one open repository; the 128 MiB read pool is not released; tracked in issue #55. `oxide impact` is affected on large repositories; search and context do not walk. (5) Derivation pin: `fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-v21` `versions.derivation` and the 38 corpus labels changed `sha256:ff500e5a…` → `sha256:daa271b3…`.
